attributePath.description: 4D-native sub-grammar used inside Text-typed attributePath parameters (QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE and family). Fully specifiable from 4D's own docs.
rules: Segments are dot-separated; leading/trailing spaces around a segment are trimmed.
A trailing [] on a segment marks that attribute as an array.
An optional single letter inside the brackets (e.g. [i]) names a placeholder for referencing a specific array element in downstream formulas.

SQL.note: Embedded in SQL EXECUTE / SQL SET PARAMETER string arguments.

Regex.note: Embedded in Match regex / Replace string pattern arguments.

SQLWhereClauseWithExpressionSubstitution.note: A SQL-2-compliant boolean search-condition fragment (the WHERE-clause of an implicit "SELECT * FROM table WHERE ..."), evaluated by 4D's own integrated SQL engine (not an external SQL connection). Can additionally embed references to 4D expressions/variables using the same <> or :MyVar substitution syntax supported inside Begin SQL/End SQL blocks and the other integrated SQL commands -- so the full grammar is SQL-2 plus this 4D-specific expression-substitution extension, which is why it is modeled as its own foreignGrammars entry rather than a plain 'SQL' one.

SAXContext.description: Opaque parsing/generation context threaded through the SAX command family.

onErrCallHandler.description: Expected calling convention for a method registered via ON ERR CALL — invoked automatically by 4D when an error occurs, not called directly by user code.
onErrCallHandler.trigger: A runtime error occurs while this handler is active.

IMAPListenerOnMailCreated.description: IMAP New transporter's parameter.listener.onMailCreated callback: called when a new message is detected/added to the mailbox (requires IMAP IDLE support).

expectedParams.name: event
expectedParams.description: Event data: event.type = "mailCreated" (Text); event.mailCount = number of messages now in the mailbox (Integer).

IMAPListenerOnMailDeleted.description: IMAP New transporter's parameter.listener.onMailDeleted callback: called when a message is permanently deleted.
IMAPListenerOnMailDeleted.trigger: A message is permanently deleted from the selected mailbox while the transporter's IMAP IDLE listener is active.

expectedParams.name: event
expectedParams.description: Event data: event.type = "mailDeleted" (Text); event.msgNumber = deleted message's sequence number (Integer).

IMAPListenerOnFlagsModified.description: IMAP New transporter's parameter.listener.onFlagsModified callback: called when a message's flags are modified.
IMAPListenerOnFlagsModified.trigger: A message's flags change in the selected mailbox while the transporter's IMAP IDLE listener is active.

expectedParams.name: event
expectedParams.description: Event data: event.type = "FlagsModified" (Text); event.msgNumber = affected message's sequence number (Integer); event.flags = updated flags (Collection).

queryThemeChain.description: Repeated calls build up a multi-level sort/query; a trailing '*' means more calls are coming, its absence on the final call triggers execution.
queryThemeChain.example:
ORDER BY([Inv];[Inv]type;>;[Inv]product;>;*)
ORDER BY([Inv];[Inv]desc;>)  // final call, no *, triggers the sort

saxParsing.description: SAX-style XML generation: commands must be called in properly nested open/set/close order across the whole method.

constraints: aTable must be explicitly specified; the default table cannot be used.
Parameters ($1...$n) are not supported inside formula.
If used with PRINT SELECTION and BREAK LEVEL and a local variable, all three must execute from the same method or an error occurs at reevaluation time.
commands.summary: Sorts the current selection of aTable using one or more formula-based levels.

constraints: If aField, order, and * are all omitted, ORDER BY displays the interactive Order By editor instead of sorting.
Overloads 2 and 3 declare the identical parameter type (Pointer). Which one applies depends on what the pointer actually references at runtime — not checkable from the call site alone.
Pointers are kept as-is (not evaluated); dates/times/objects/collections have their own storage-semantics footnotes.

the current list item

overloads.semanticRole: Draw/redraw using a numeric graph-type code; may be followed by GRAPH SETTINGS to adjust further.
Draw and fully configure the graph in one call via an object of settings; GRAPH SETTINGS must NOT be called afterward.

platformConstraints.note: This overload is not supported there per historical doc notes; verify against the target release.

If either is null, both fall back to default graph values.

constraints: Must NOT be called if the graph was generated using GRAPH's Object (graphSettings) overload.
If aTable is omitted, applies to the default table; errors if none is set.

silentCoercionDefault.condition: If the parameter's type is not explicitly defined, 4D coerces it to Text before passing it to the JavaScript function.

constraints: Calling a JS function that opens a blocking dialog (alert(), print()) is not recommended; the user cannot interact with the Web area while 4D code runs.

discriminatedBy.rule: Keys of attribObj correspond 1:1 to attribName values in overload 1's variadic group.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the 4D.ClassStore object for 4D's built-in classes. Per the Classes concept page, two class stores exist: `cs` for user/component classes, `4D` for built-in classes.
The ABORT PROCESS BY ID command stops a specific process on the 4D Server.

constraints: Only works on 4D Server; does nothing if called from a remote client or 4D single-user.
Requires the ServerNet network layer.
Intended only for debugging/administration, not as a regular application procedure.

overloads.semanticRole: Stops the interrupted execution from within an installed error-handling method, in place of 4D's standard error dialog box.

constraints: Only meaningful when called from within an error-handling project method installed via ON ERR CALL; it stops the execution that ON ERR CALL intercepted and resumes control at the appropriate outer level (form, menu, process, or import/export/query operation) instead of showing 4D's standard error dialog.

overloads.semanticRole: The ACCEPT command is used in form or object methods (or in subroutines) to: accept a new or modified record, for which data entry has been initiated using ADD RECORD or MODIFY RECORD .

constraints: Cannot be queued: executing ACCEPT twice in a row in response to one event has the same effect as executing it once.
In headless mode, only allowed inside offscreen areas created by VP Run offscreen area or WA Run offscreen area.

members.name: data
members.description: Numeric field or variable on which to accumulate

overloads.semanticRole: Registers one or more numeric fields/variables to be subtotaled by break level during the next PRINT SELECTION report; must be called (together with BREAK LEVEL) before that report.

constraints: Must be executed, together with BREAK LEVEL, before every PRINT SELECTION report for which break/subtotal processing is wanted.

params.name: arrActivities
params.description: Filled with one object per in-progress operation, describing message, timing, and context/details.
If passed, get the server's activity snapshot instead of the local one (remote mode only).

overloads.semanticRole: Returns a snapshot of in-progress 4D operations as a single array of structured Objects, one per operation (including nested subOperations).

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the caller wants all operation info returned as a single structured Object array, one element per operation.

params.name: arrUUID
params.description: UUID identifier for each operation.

params.name: arrStart
params.description: Start time of each operation, "yyyy:mm:dd hh:mm:ss:mls" format.

params.name: arrDuration
params.description: Duration of each operation, in milliseconds.

params.name: arrInfo
params.description: Label describing each operation.

params.name: arrDetails
params.description: Per-operation object with dbContextInfo/dbOperationDetails/subOperations, if requested.
If passed, get the server's activity snapshot instead of the local one (remote mode only).

overloads.semanticRole: Returns a snapshot of in-progress 4D operations as several synchronized flat arrays (one element per operation per array) instead of one Object array.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the caller wants operation info spread across several parallel/synchronized flat arrays instead of one Object array.

constraints: The trailing '*' parameter is only meaningful when 4D runs in remote mode: passing it retrieves a snapshot of the operations on the server instead of local operations; it is ignored when the command runs on 4D Server or 4D single-user.

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table to use for data entry, or the default table if omitted.
If passed, the data-entry window is drawn without scroll bars and cannot be reduced.

overloads.semanticRole: Lets the user interactively add a new record to aTable (or the default table), displaying the current input form until the record is accepted or canceled.
ADD TO SET adds the current record of aTable to set .

constraints: The set named in 'set' must already exist (e.g. created with CREATE SET / CREATE EMPTY SET), otherwise an error occurs -- ADD TO SET does not implicitly create it.
If aTable has no current record, ADD TO SET silently has no effect.

overloads.semanticRole: The ADJUST BLOBS CACHE PRIORITY command modifies the priority of the "blobs" data related to aTable in cache for the current process.

constraints: priority must be one of the named 'Cache Management' theme constants (Cache priority low / Cache priority very low / Cache priority normal / Cache priority high / Cache priority very high), not an arbitrary Integer.
Only works in local mode (4D Server or 4D single-user); cannot be used in 4D remote mode.
Handles priority for BLOB, text, picture, and object fields only (data stored in the data file); scalar-field priority is handled by ADJUST TABLE CACHE PRIORITY instead.
A new call replaces any priority previously set by this command in the same process.

overloads.semanticRole: The ADJUST INDEX CACHE PRIORITY command modifies the priority value of the index(es) related to the aField in cache for the current process.

constraints: priority must be one of the named 'Cache Management' theme constants (Cache priority low / Cache priority very low / Cache priority normal / Cache priority high / Cache priority very high), not an arbitrary Integer.
Only works in local mode (4D Server or 4D single-user); cannot be used in 4D remote mode.
Applies to all indexes on aField, including keyword indexes, but does not change composite-index priority.
A new call replaces any priority previously set by this command in the same process.

overloads.semanticRole: The ADJUST TABLE CACHE PRIORITY command modifies the priority value of the data related to aTable in cache for the current process.

constraints: priority must be one of the named 'Cache Management' theme constants (Cache priority low / Cache priority very low / Cache priority normal / Cache priority high / Cache priority very high), not an arbitrary Integer.
Only works in local mode (4D Server or 4D single-user); cannot be used in 4D remote mode.
Handles priority for scalar-type fields only (date, number, string); binary-type fields (BLOB, text, picture, object) priority is handled by ADJUST BLOBS CACHE PRIORITY instead.
A new call replaces any priority previously set by this command in the same process.

overloads.semanticRole: The ALERT command displays an alert dialog box composed of a note icon, a message, and an OK button.

constraints: Do not call ALERT from the On Activate or On Deactivate form-event handling code of a form/object method; doing so causes an endless loop.

overloads.semanticRole: ALL RECORDS selects all the records of aTable for the current process.
The APPEND DATA TO PASTEBOARD command appends to the pasteboard the data contained in the BLOB data under the data type specified in dataType .

constraints: Under Windows, when dataType is a Text data type ("TEXT", com.4d.private.text.native, or com.4d.private.text.utf16), the string in the data BLOB must end with a NULL character.

To append multiple instances of the same data type, or non-text/non-picture data, use APPEND DATA TO PASTEBOARD; to clear the pasteboard and set a single text/picture/file-path value, use SET TEXT TO PASTEBOARD / SET PICTURE TO PASTEBOARD / SET FILE TO PASTEBOARD instead.
To append fresh data (rather than add to what's already there), call CLEAR PASTEBOARD first.

overloads.semanticRole: The APPEND MENU ITEM command appends new menu items to the menu whose number or reference is passed in menu .

constraints: If menu is a MenuRef (string), the process parameter serves no purpose and is ignored.

Unless the trailing '*' is passed, itemText uses a mini-grammar of metacharacters: ';' separates multiple item labels in one call; a leading '(' disables the item; "-" or "(-" creates a separator line; '<B'/'<I'/'<U' set bold/italic/underline style; '!' followed by a character sets a check-mark character; '^' followed by a character selects a Mac OS icon resource (code + 208); '/' followed by a character sets a keyboard shortcut.
When the trailing '*' is passed, all of those metacharacters (including ';') are treated as literal standard characters instead, which also means only one menu item can be created per call.
Newly appended items have no associated method/action; SET MENU ITEM PROPERTY or SET MENU ITEM METHOD (or Menu selected in a form method) must be used to wire them up.
subMenu must be an existing menu reference (e.g. created with Create menu); if the call appends more than one item, the submenu is attached to the first one.

overloads.semanticRole: The APPEND TO ARRAY command adds a new element at the end of array and assigns value to the element.

constraints: value's type must be compatible with array's element type or the 4D syntax error 54 ("Argument types are incompatible") is raised; a string array (Text/String) accepts Text or String values, and a number array (Integer/Longint/Real) also accepts Time values.
In interpreted mode, if array does not yet exist, this command creates it with the type of value.

overloads.semanticRole: The APPEND TO LIST command appends a new item to the hierarchical list whose list reference number you pass in list .

jointConstraints.rule: Although both are individually optional, sublist and expanded must be passed together (or both omitted); passing only one is invalid. Omit both, or pass sublist as 0, to attach no child list.

overloads.semanticRole: APPLY TO SELECTION applies statement to each record in the current selection of aTable .

constraints: statement cannot reference call parameters ($1...$n).
On 4D Server, statement is not executed on the server: every record in the selection is sent back to the local workstation to be modified there.
If the current selection is empty, the command has no effect.
If used within a transaction, all changes made by statement can be rolled back if the transaction is canceled.

overloads.semanticRole: The ARRAY BLOB command creates and/or resizes an array of Blob type elements in memory.
The ARRAY BOOLEAN command creates and/or resizes an array of Boolean elements in memory.
Creates or resizes an in-memory array of Date elements; enlarging an existing array leaves existing elements unchanged and initializes new elements to the null date (!00/00/00!).
Creates or resizes an in-memory array of 2-byte Integer elements; enlarging an existing array leaves existing elements unchanged and initializes new elements to 0.
Creates or resizes an in-memory array of 4-byte Longint elements; enlarging an existing array leaves existing elements unchanged and initializes new elements to 0.
The ARRAY OBJECT command creates and/or resizes an array of language Object type elements in memory.

Creates or resizes an in-memory array of Picture elements; enlarging an existing array leaves existing elements unchanged and initializes new elements to empty pictures (Picture size returns 0 for them).

Creates or resizes an in-memory array of Pointer elements; enlarging an existing array leaves existing elements unchanged and initializes new elements to a null pointer (Is nil pointer returns True for them).
The ARRAY REAL command creates and/or resizes an array of Real elements in memory.
Creates or resizes an in-memory array of Text elements; enlarging an existing array leaves existing elements unchanged and initializes new elements to "" (empty string).
Creates or resizes an in-memory array of Time elements; enlarging an existing array leaves existing elements unchanged and initializes new elements to the null time (00:00:00).

params.name: collection
params.description: Collection to fill; existing elements are replaced and new ones appended if the source array(s) are longer.

members.name: array
members.description: Array whose elements are copied into collection (or into propertyName's values, if passed).

members.name: propertyName
members.description: Object property name to fill with this array's values; if any propertyName is passed for one (array;propertyName) pair, it becomes mandatory for all of them, since collection is then built as an array of objects rather than of plain values.

overloads.semanticRole: Copies one or more arrays' elements into collection, either as plain collection elements or, when propertyName(s) are given, as a named property of each element object.
Creates or replaces the first-level items of a hierarchical list or choice list from the elements of array, optionally assigning explicit per-item reference numbers via itemRefs.

constraints: Only sets first-level items of the target list; nested/sub-items are not addressable via this command.
If list is a numeric ListRef (hierarchical list), that list must already have been created previously (e.g. via New list) -- this command cannot create a new hierarchical list from scratch.

If list is a Text choice-list name, this command modifies the structure file, so any local edits are lost on next structure-file update in production, and it cannot be used against a read-only structure (a .4dz project, including remote projects, or a component).
If itemRefs is omitted, 4D automatically assigns list item reference numbers 1, 2, ... N.

params.description: If present, defer execution of this statement and stack it with other ARRAY TO SELECTION(...; *) lines until a final call without *.

overloads.semanticRole: Copies one or more parallel arrays into a selection of records field-by-field (by array/record order), creating new records if the arrays are longer than the current selection; the optional trailing * defers execution so several such statements can be stacked and run together.

constraints: All fields listed must belong to the same table (no related/foreign-table fields), and all arrays must have the same number of elements or a syntax error is generated.

If the array has more elements than the current selection, new records are created; existing and new records are saved automatically. Because it can create records, this command ignores a table's read-only state.
Records locked by another process are skipped (left unmodified) and collected into the process set LockedSet, which can be tested after the call.

Passing the trailing * defers execution: 4D stores the statement in memory instead of running it immediately, letting several ARRAY TO SELECTION lines (like QUERY) stack up and execute together as one final call without *; the command can therefore also be called with no parameters at all to run the stacked lines.

overloads.semanticRole: Evaluates boolExpression and, if it is false, halts code execution and raises error -10518 showing messageText (or the assertion text itself if messageText is omitted); does nothing if boolExpression is true.

constraints: Assertions can be globally enabled/disabled application-wide via SET ASSERT ENABLED; when disabled, ASSERT is a no-op regardless of boolExpression.
On failure (boolExpression false) triggers error -10518 with the assertion text (or messageText if supplied) prefixed by "Assert failed:"; interceptable via an ON ERR CALL method.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the absolute (unsigned) value of number, i.e. number unchanged if positive, or its negation if negative.
Returns an object describing the given standard action's current availability/status (enabled, visible, checked/unchecked/mixed, title, current parameter value) in the specified form context.

constraints: action can be a plain action-name string or a constant from the Standard Action theme; some actions require the 'name?param=value' pattern (e.g. "gotoPage?value=2").
If target is omitted, the ak current form context is used by default.
Returns null (undefined) if the action's status cannot be determined (e.g. not attached to any object or menu command).

Returns an object with these properties: enabled (Boolean, true if the action can be invoked); status (Text, one of "checked"/"unchecked"/"mixed" -- e.g. for ak font bold, "checked" means the selection is bold, "unchecked" means it isn't, "mixed" means only part of the selection is); title (Text, current localized action label, e.g. "Undo"); visible (Boolean, true if the action is visible in the form); value (Text, current value of the action's parameter string, if any, e.g. "10pt" for "fontSize?value=10pt"). The parameter table's Function-result row instead lists boolean properties isEnabled/isVisible/isChecked/isMixed/isUnknownState; that table entry is a documentation error/stale summary -- the properties above (enabled/status/title/visible/value, from the Description section prose) are the correct, authoritative shape.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns True in a form method when the window containing the form becomes the frontmost window of the frontmost process (the On Activate form event); obsolete, superseded by Form event code.

constraints: Equivalent to testing whether Form event code returns On Activate.
Do not place TRACE or ALERT in the Activated phase of a form -- this causes an endless loop.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns True only if the current process has an active (not suspended) transaction in progress.

constraints: Returns False both when there is no current transaction and when the current transaction has been suspended via SUSPEND TRANSACTION -- callers needing to distinguish 'no transaction' from 'suspended transaction' must track that separately.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns a new date obtained by adding years, months, and days to date, correctly handling per-month day counts and leap years (unlike manually adding a day count with the + date operator).
Returns True during the After execution cycle (the On Validate form event) following object/form validation.

constraints: Requires the On Validate event property to be enabled for the form and/or the object in the Design environment, otherwise the After execution cycle never fires.
Equivalent to testing whether Form event code returns On Validate.

overloads.semanticRole: Opens (or creates) the document on disk exactly like Open document, but positions the file pointer at the document's end instead of its beginning, returning the same document-reference value (typed Time per the classic API) used by other Document commands.

constraints: Identical to Open document except the file position is set to the end of the document instead of the beginning; see Open document for the full parameter/behavior reference.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the full path of the 4D executable file/application currently running.

Returns an object describing the current application instance's activity and network configuration (CPU/network usage, server listening state, ports, UI mode flags, uptime, etc.), scoped to wherever the call executes.

constraints: Information reflects where the command is executed: called from a remote 4D it describes only that workstation; called in code running on the server it describes the server.

On Windows, the cpuUsage/networkInputThroughput/networkOutputThroughput counters require having been previously initialized by an earlier call to Application info (e.g. from the On Startup database method) before they report real values.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns a numeric constant identifying which kind of 4D environment (desktop, remote, server, volume desktop, tool4d) the calling process is running under.

constraints: The returned Integer is one of the predefined Application type constants: 4D Local mode=0, 4D Volume desktop=1, 4D Desktop=3, 4D Remote mode=4, 4D Server=5, tool4d=6 (values 2 and 7+ unused/reserved as of this doc snapshot).

params.name: buildNum
params.description: Filled with the internal build/compilation number of the running 4D application.
If present, return the long (8-character) version string instead of the short (4-character) one.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns an encoded version-number string for the running 4D environment (short 4-char form by default, or long 8-char form with the * flag), optionally also filling buildNum with the internal build number.

constraints: Without the * parameter, returns a 4-character string (version, 'R' number, revision); with * present, returns an 8-character string additionally prefixed with a final/beta flag and internal compilation number.
For applications compiled and merged with 4D Volume Desktop, the returned buildNum is not significant -- version info is managed by the developer in that context.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the arctangent of number, expressed in radians.
Evaluates and returns boolExpression's value, additionally raising an ASSERT-style error -10518 as a side effect if the value is false and assertions are enabled.

constraints: If assertions are disabled (via SET ASSERT ENABLED), Asserted simply returns boolExpression's value without ever raising an error; if enabled and boolExpression is false, it raises error -10518 exactly like ASSERT before still returning the (false) result.

overloads.semanticRole: Computes the arithmetic mean of series (an indexed field, an object-field attribute selected via attributePath, or a numeric array).

constraints: If series is an array, it must be a one- or two-dimension Integer/Longint/Real array (not Text/Boolean/etc).
attributePath only applies when series is an object field; it selects a (possibly nested, dot-notation, case-sensitive) numeric attribute, and non-numeric values along that path are ignored.
Sets the OK system variable to 1 on normal completion, or 0 if the user interrupts via the progress thermometer's Stop button.

params.name: selector
params.description: Which piece of last-backup information to retrieve; selects the type/meaning of info1 and info2.

params.name: info1
params.description: First value associated with selector; concrete type/meaning depends on which selector constant was passed.

params.name: info2
params.description: Second value associated with selector; concrete type/meaning depends on which selector constant was passed.

overloads.semanticRole: Fills info1 and info2 with the piece of information about the last database backup selected by selector.

discriminatedBy.rule: The concrete type and semantic meaning returned in info1/info2 vary per selector constant (e.g. last backup date vs. duration vs. destination); see the 'Backup and Restore' theme constants.

constraints: selector must be one of the predefined constants from the "Backup and Restore" theme; the concrete type and meaning of info1 and info2 both depend on which selector constant is passed (e.g. one selector returns a Date in info1, another returns Integer).

overloads.semanticRole: Starts a database backup immediately using the current backup settings, without prompting the user for confirmation.

constraints: Must not be called from the On Backup Startup or On Backup Shutdown database methods, since BACKUP itself triggers those methods at the start/end of its run (would recurse).
No confirmation dialog is shown; a progress bar appears. On 4D Server, calling from a client runs as a stored procedure but always executes on the server.

params.name: toDecode
params.description: Base64/Base64URL-encoded value to decode; overwritten in place with the decoded value if decoded is omitted.

params.name: decoded
params.description: Receives the decoded value, if supplied.
If present, decode using the Base64URL variant instead of standard Base64.

overloads.semanticRole: Decodes a Base64/Base64URL-encoded text or blob value from toDecode, either into decoded or back into toDecode itself if decoded is omitted.

constraints: If decoded is omitted, the command overwrites toDecode in place with the decoded value instead of writing to a separate parameter.
See BASE64 ENCODE for details on the Base64 vs. Base64URL format distinction (selected here via the trailing *).

params.name: toEncode
params.description: Raw value to encode; overwritten in place with the encoded value if encoded is omitted.

params.name: encoded
params.description: Receives the encoded value, if supplied.
If present, encode using the Base64URL variant instead of standard Base64.

overloads.semanticRole: Encodes toEncode as Base64/Base64URL, either into encoded or back into toEncode itself if encoded is omitted.

constraints: If encoded is omitted, the command overwrites toEncode in place with the encoded value instead of writing to a separate parameter.
Base64URL (selected via the trailing *) is an alternate encoding with URL/filename-safe substitutions per RFC 4648, distinct from standard Base64.

overloads.semanticRole: Makes the computer emit a beep (or the system's configured alert sound).

constraints: Do not call from within a Web connection process -- the beep is produced on the 4D Web server machine, not the client browser machine.

params.name: compressed
params.description: Compression mode/status of the BLOB (a BLOB-theme compression constant, or 0 if not compressed).

params.name: expandedSize
params.description: Size of the BLOB in bytes when not compressed.

params.name: currentSize
params.description: Current (possibly compressed) size of the BLOB in bytes.

overloads.semanticRole: Fills compressed (and, if requested, expandedSize/currentSize) with information about how blob is currently compressed and its size(s).

constraints: compressed's returned value is one of the BLOB theme compression constants (e.g. Compact/Fast/GZIP Best/GZIP Fast, or 0 for not compressed) -- see the BLOB theme constants for the exact value/meaning mapping.

overloads.semanticRole: Overwrites the entire contents of document on disk with the data stored in blob.

constraints: If document already exists, it must not currently be open, otherwise an error is generated; if it does not exist, the command creates it.
To let the user pick the target document interactively, use Open document or Create document instead and pass their resulting process document reference.

params.name: picture
params.description: Filled with the picture decoded from pictureBlob.

params.name: codec
params.description: Picture codec ID to force when decoding pictureBlob.

overloads.semanticRole: Decodes a picture stored (in any native format) inside pictureBlob into the picture variable/field.

constraints: Works regardless of the picture's original stored format inside the BLOB (like READ PICTURE FILE, but from a BLOB instead of a file).
codec lets you force interpretation of the BLOB's bytes using a specific picture codec ID instead of auto-detecting the format.

overloads.semanticRole: Replaces the current database's user accounts and groups with the contents of the encrypted users BLOB previously produced by USERS TO BLOB.

constraints: users must be a BLOB previously created by USERS TO BLOB; it is encrypted.
Only the database Administrator or Designer may execute this command; any other caller gets a no-op plus privilege error -9949.

In a project database, this only migrates users/groups into directory.json (all existing entries there are replaced except "Designer"/"Administrator"); in a binary database, all negative-reference-number (Administrator-created) users/groups are removed and replaced by the BLOB's contents.

params.name: blob
params.description: BLOB containing 4D variable data.

params.name: variable
params.description: Overwritten with the data read from blob.

params.name: offset
params.description: Byte position within blob to read variable from; on return, updated to the position of the next variable within the BLOB.

overloads.semanticRole: Reads variable's data out of blob at the given (or default) byte offset, advancing offset past the value read.

constraints: The BLOB's data must already be laid out to match the destination variable's type/size (typically written earlier via VARIABLE TO BLOB); mismatched data produces undefined results.
If offset is omitted, variable data is read starting at the beginning of the BLOB (offset 0).

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the size of blob, in bytes.

params.name: byteOrder
params.description: 0 = native, 1 = Macintosh, 2 = PC byte ordering.

params.name: offset
params.description: Byte offset to read from; on return, updated to the offset immediately following the read 2-byte value.

overloads.semanticRole: Reads a 2-byte Integer from blob at the given (or default) byte offset using byteOrder's byte ordering, advancing offset past the value read.

constraints: byteOrder selects how the 2 read bytes are interpreted: 0 = native byte ordering, 1 = Macintosh byte ordering, 2 = PC byte ordering.
If offset is omitted, reading starts at the beginning of the BLOB (byte 0).

params.name: offset
params.description: Byte offset to read the hierarchical-list data from; on return, updated to the offset immediately following the data read.

overloads.semanticRole: Creates a new hierarchical list from data stored in blob at the given (or default) byte offset, advancing offset past the data read, and returns the new list's reference number.

constraints: If offset is omitted, reading starts at the beginning of the BLOB (byte 0).
The BLOB's data must have previously been produced by LIST TO BLOB for the created list to be well-formed.

params.name: blob
params.description: BLOB from which to get the Long Integer value

params.name: byteOrder
params.description: Byte ordering of the 4-byte value to read

sentinelValues.meaning: Native byte ordering
Macintosh byte ordering
PC byte ordering

params.name: offset
params.description: Offset within the BLOB (expressed in bytes); on return, incremented by the number of bytes read so it can be reused for the next read

overloads.semanticRole: Reads and returns a 4-byte Long Integer value from a BLOB at a given (or default) byte offset, honoring an explicit byte ordering, and advances the offset variable by the bytes consumed.

constraints: offset must be between 0 and (BLOB size - 4); otherwise error -111 is generated.
Byte-swapping across Macintosh/PC platforms is the caller's responsibility; this command does not perform it automatically beyond the byteOrder parameter.

overloads.semanticRole: Restores the current 4D print settings from a BLOB previously produced by Print settings to BLOB, returning a status code indicating whether the load succeeded and whether the printer identity changed.

constraints: printSettings must have been generated by the Print settings to BLOB command.
The restored settings only take effect as long as no subsequent command (e.g. SET PRINT OPTION, or PRINT SELECTION without the '>' parameter) modifies them.
PRINT SELECTION, PRINT LABEL, and PRINT RECORD must be called with the '>' parameter for the settings applied by this command to be kept.

params.name: blob
params.description: BLOB from which to get the Real value

params.name: realFormat
params.description: Internal format and byte ordering of the Real value to read

sentinelValues.meaning: Native real format
Extended real format
Macintosh Double real format
PC (Windows) Double real format

params.name: offset
params.description: Offset within the BLOB (expressed in bytes); on return, incremented by the number of bytes read (8 or 10) so it can be reused for the next read

overloads.semanticRole: Reads and returns a Real value from a BLOB at a given (or default) byte offset, honoring an explicit internal format/byte ordering, and advances the offset variable by the bytes consumed (8 or 10).

constraints: offset must be between 0 and (BLOB size - 8 or - 10, depending on realFormat); otherwise error -111 is generated.

params.name: blob
params.description: BLOB from which to get the text

params.name: textFormat
params.description: Format and character set of the text to read

sentinelValues.meaning: Mac C string
Mac Pascal string
Mac text with length
Mac text without length (requires textLength)
UTF8 C string
UTF8 text with length
UTF8 text without length (requires textLength)

params.name: offset
params.description: Offset within the BLOB (expressed in bytes); on return, incremented by the number of bytes read

params.name: textLength
params.description: Number of characters to read; only used (and required) when textFormat is 'Mac text without length' (3) or 'UTF8 text without length' (6) -- ignored for the other formats, which self-describe their length

overloads.semanticRole: Reads and returns a Text value from a BLOB at a given (or default) byte offset, decoded per an explicit character-set/length format, and advances the offset variable by the bytes consumed.

constraints: The 'UTF8' format constants can only be used when the application runs in Unicode mode.
The 'Mac' format constants cannot work with texts greater than 32 KB.

params.name: booleanArr
params.description: Filled with one element per record (by absolute record number): True if the record belongs to set, False otherwise

params.name: set
params.description: Name of the set to test membership against
params.default: UserSet in the current process, if omitted

overloads.semanticRole: Fills a Boolean array, one element per record in the table (indexed by absolute record number), indicating whether each record belongs to the given (or default UserSet) set.

constraints: The total number of elements filled in booleanArr is not guaranteed to equal the number of records actually present in the table; any extra elements are set to False.

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the number of break levels (and optionally which level triggers a page break) to activate break processing for the next report printed with PRINT SELECTION.

constraints: Must be called, together with ACCUMULATE, before every report (via PRINT SELECTION) for which break processing is wanted -- these two commands activate break processing.
The form must have at least as many Break areas as the number passed in level; extra Break areas are ignored.

overloads.semanticRole: Brings all windows belonging to the given process to the front (no-op if it is already frontmost).

constraints: If the process is hidden, SHOW PROCESS must be used first; otherwise BRING TO FRONT has no effect.

overloads.semanticRole: Launches the application build/generation process using the given (or an interactively chosen) build application settings file.

constraints: Only works with 4D Developer (single-user); cannot be called from 4D Server, 4D in remote mode, or a merged application.
If the compiled code is outdated, this command first launches the compiler; MESSAGES OFF can hide its progress bar.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns True when the current record pointer of the given (or default) table is positioned before the first record of the current selection, including when the selection is empty.
Returns True when the current form event corresponds to the Before (On Load) execution cycle.

constraints: The 'On Load' event property must be selected for the form and/or object in the Design environment for the Before execution cycle to be generated.

overloads.semanticRole: Marks the start of an inline block of SQL statements (closed by End SQL) to be interpreted by the process's current SQL data source.

constraints: Is a keyword, not a callable command with parameters; a block opened with Begin SQL must be closed with a matching End SQL keyword.
Multiple SQL statements on one line must be separated with a semicolon; the 4D Debugger evaluates SQL code line by line.

overloads.semanticRole: Coerces an arbitrary expression to a Boolean, returning False for Undefined/Null/non-Boolean-non-zero-safe types and the natural Boolean value otherwise (useful when an expression might evaluate to null or undefined but a Boolean is required).
Posts a formula (with optional parameters) to a window's message box so it executes in the context of the form displayed in that window, regardless of the calling process.

constraints: Arrays cannot be passed as parameters to formula.
formula's parameters arrive as named parameters (if formula is a function/project method) or sequentially in $1, $2, ...
Executes regardless of which process owns window, allowing a preemptive process to exchange information with a form's (cooperative) process via its message box.

overloads.semanticRole: Sends an event from a subform instance up to the subform container object so it can be handled in the context of the parent form.

constraints: Must be placed in the form method of the subform, or in the object method of one of the subform's objects.
The event is only received in the object method of the subform container.
For a custom (non-4D) event, pass a negative value to avoid colliding with existing/future 4D event numbers.

overloads.semanticRole: Creates (if needed) and posts a formula (with optional parameters) to the message box of the named/numbered worker process, requesting it execute the formula in its own context.

constraints: If process names a nonexistent process not created by CALL WORKER or 4D itself, the command does nothing; if it names a nonexistent worker by name, a new worker process is created.
The main process (always process number 1) is a worker process callable via CALL WORKER, but should be addressed by number since its name varies by language.
Arrays cannot be passed as parameters to formula.

overloads.semanticRole: Cancels the transaction of the corresponding nesting level started by START TRANSACTION in the current process, rolling back the data operations performed during it.

constraints: Does not affect unsaved changes to records currently displayed -- they remain displayed after the command executes.

overloads.semanticRole: Cancels the current interactive context (data entry started by ADD RECORD/MODIFY RECORD, a DIALOG-displayed form, a DISPLAY SELECTION/MODIFY SELECTION, or an in-progress form print), acting like the user pressing Escape.

constraints: Cannot be queued; two CANCEL calls in a row from one method have the same effect as one.
In the On Printing Detail form event during Print form execution, CANCEL suspends printing of the current form and resumes it on the next page, rather than cancelling data entry.

overloads.semanticRole: Switches the identity of the current database user, either interactively (dialog box, if called without parameters) or programmatically by name/ID and password, discarding the previous user's access privileges.

constraints: Has no effect in project databases opened in single-user mode.
Resets any alias set for the current user via SET USER ALIAS.
If called with no parameters, displays the database connection dialog box instead of switching programmatically.
If the given user account does not exist or was deleted, error -9979 is returned (interceptible via ON ERR CALL).

overloads.semanticRole: Displays the 4D License Manager dialog box, letting a user activate plug-ins or the Web server license on the local machine.

constraints: Can only be used with 4D single-user applications; cannot be called from a component.
When passwords are enabled, only the Designer or Administrator can execute it effectively; other users get a no-op.

overloads.semanticRole: Replaces the current user's password with the given new password.

constraints: Passwords are case-sensitive.

overloads.semanticRole: Displays the log file viewer dialog box, which includes a Rollback button to cancel operations recorded in the database's data log.

constraints: Can only be used in single-user applications, notably to expose the rollback function in 4D Volume Desktop applications (no Design mode).
In a client/server application it has no effect and returns error 1421.
Because it exposes a rollback function, access should typically be restricted to database administrators.

overloads.semanticRole: Deletes the hierarchical list identified by list from memory, optionally (with the '*' flag) also deleting all of its attached sublists.

constraints: Lists attached to a form object via the Property List window are loaded/cleared automatically by 4D and do not need CLEAR LIST; only lists loaded/copied/extracted/created programmatically need it.

overloads.semanticRole: Frees the memory used by a named selection without affecting the underlying table, selection, or records.

constraints: Not needed if the named selection was created with CUT NAMED SELECTION and then consumed by USE NAMED SELECTION, since it no longer exists in memory afterward.

overloads.semanticRole: Empties the pasteboard of all its contents (including every format of any duplicated data).

constraints: Must be called once before appending new data with APPEND DATA TO PASTEBOARD, since that command does not clear the pasteboard itself.
SET TEXT TO PASTEBOARD and SET PICTURE TO PASTEBOARD already clear the pasteboard automatically before appending, so this command is not needed before them.

overloads.semanticRole: Erases a semaphore previously created by the Semaphore function, if the calling process created it.

constraints: A process can only clear a semaphore it created; calling it on a semaphore created by another process does nothing.
Semaphores not cleared remain in memory until the creating process ends.

overloads.semanticRole: Frees the memory used by a named set without affecting the underlying table, selections, or records.

constraints: Use SAVE SET first if the set's contents need to be preserved before clearing.

overloads.semanticRole: Resets a local, process, or interprocess variable to its type's default value (e.g. empty string, 0, no elements) without removing it from memory.

constraints: Process and local variables are cleared automatically by 4D (when their process ends, or when their defining method returns, respectively), so explicit clearing is mainly useful to reclaim memory early.

overloads.semanticRole: Closes the system document referenced by docRef, flushing any written data to disk.

constraints: Is the only way to ensure data written to the file is actually saved to disk.
Every document opened with Open document, Create document, or Append document must eventually be closed.

overloads.semanticRole: Closes the print job opened by OPEN PRINTING JOB and sends the assembled print document to the current printer.

constraints: Starting with 4D v20 R4, printing jobs are non-blocking in new projects (see the Non-blocking printing compatibility setting).

overloads.semanticRole: Closes the resource file referenced by resFile, previously opened with Open resource file.

constraints: Only needs to be called once to close a resource file, even if it was opened multiple times.
Does nothing if applied to the 4D application/database resource files, or given an invalid reference number.
4D automatically closes all remaining open resource files when the application quits or another database is opened.

overloads.semanticRole: Closes the active custom window previously opened by Open window or Open form window in the current process (or a specified external window).

constraints: Passing an explicit window reference number has no effect for windows opened via Open window/Open form window: CLOSE WINDOW always closes the last window created by one of those two commands regardless of the number passed.
An explicit window reference number is only meaningful to target an external window (opened outside of Open window/Open form window).
Has no effect if no custom window is open, if called while a form is active in the window, or targeting a system window.

params.name: collection
params.description: Collection to copy in array(s)

params.name: array
params.description: Array to receive the elements of the collection; if propertyName passed, array to receive the values of propertyName in the collection

params.name: propertyName
params.description: Object property name whose values to copy in array ("" for all elements); mandatory if collection holds objects

overloads.semanticRole: Fills one or more arrays with either the raw elements of a values collection, or with a named property's values pulled from each object of an objects collection, optionally fanning out multiple (array; propertyName) pairs in one call.

constraints: propertyName is mandatory when collection contains objects (values are read from that property of each object); it must be omitted when collection contains plain values.
Any number of additional (array; propertyName) pairs may be passed to fan the same collection out into multiple arrays in one call.
After execution every filled array has a size equal to the collection length.

overloads.semanticRole: Combines two pictures (pict1, pict2) using the given combination mode (horizontal/vertical concatenation or superimposition) into a third, compound-type resulting picture.

constraints: operator selects one of three combination modes (constants of the 'Picture Transformation' theme): 1 = horizontal concatenation, 2 = vertical concatenation, 3 = superimposition.
horOffset/vertOffset only apply when operator is superimposition (3); they translate pict2 before superimposing it onto pict1.
Differs from the & and | picture operators: those always rasterize to a plain bitmap, while COMBINE PICTURES preserves the compound-type characteristics of the source pictures.

params.name: componentsArray
params.description: Names of the components loaded by the 4D application for the current host project

overloads.semanticRole: Sizes and fills an array with the names of the components currently loaded for the host project.

constraints: Callable from either the host project or a component; returns an empty array if the project uses no components.

params.name: blob
params.description: BLOB to compress (compressed in place)

params.name: compression
params.default: 1 (Compact compression mode) if omitted or an unrecognized value is passed

sentinelValues.meaning: Compact compression mode: most compact, slowest to compress/decompress (default)
Fast compression mode: fastest to compress/decompress, larger result
GZIP best compression mode: most compact GZIP compression
GZIP fast compression mode: fastest GZIP compression

params.description: Compression algorithm/mode to use

overloads.semanticRole: Compresses the contents of a BLOB in place using the selected (or default) compression algorithm, when the BLOB is large enough to be worth compressing.

constraints: Only compresses BLOBs whose size is >= 255 bytes; smaller BLOBs are silently left uncompressed (no error) and the OK variable is set to 0.

After the call, the OK system variable is set to 1 on success, 0 if compression could not be performed (including the too-small-BLOB case). Error -10600 is only generated if the BLOB itself is damaged.
A compressed BLOB is still an ordinary BLOB and can still be modified directly; doing so may prevent EXPAND BLOB from decompressing it correctly.

overloads.semanticRole: Displays a modal confirmation dialog (note icon, message, OK and Cancel buttons, with optional custom button titles) and sets the OK system variable according to the user's choice.

constraints: Must not be called from a form/object method handling the On Activate or On Deactivate form events (causes an endless loop).
Sets the OK system variable to 1 if the user validates (OK/Enter) or 0 if the user cancels.

params.name: xCoord
params.description: Horizontal coordinate of the point: initial value in, converted value out

params.name: yCoord
params.description: Vertical coordinate of the point: initial value in, converted value out

params.name: from

sentinelValues.meaning: XY Current form: origin is top left corner of current form
XY Current window: origin is top left corner of current window
XY Main window: origin is top left corner of main window on Windows; same as XY Screen on macOS
XY Screen: origin is top left corner of main screen

params.description: Coordinate system to convert from

params.name: to

sentinelValues.meaning: XY Current form: origin is top left corner of current form
XY Current window: origin is top left corner of current window
XY Main window: origin is top left corner of main window on Windows; same as XY Screen on macOS
XY Screen: origin is top left corner of main screen

params.description: Coordinate system to convert to

overloads.semanticRole: Converts an (x;y) point in place from one coordinate system (form/subform, window, or screen) to another.

constraints: When called from a subform (or a subform object) with 'from' = XY Current form, the coordinates are relative to the subform itself, not to its parent form.

For conversions involving a form window's position (e.g. GET WINDOW RECT results, or values passed to Open form window), use XY Main window, since that is the coordinate system used by window commands on Windows (on macOS it is equivalent to XY Screen).

If 'from' is XY Current form and the point is in the body of a list form, the result depends on the calling context: inside On Display Detail it is relative to the record currently drawn; otherwise, while a record is being edited, it is relative to that record; otherwise it is relative to the first record.

params.name: 4Dtext
params.description: Text expressed in the current character set of 4D

params.name: charSet
params.description: Name (string) or MIBEnum number (integer) of the character set to convert to

params.name: convertedBLOB
params.description: BLOB containing the converted text

overloads.semanticRole: Converts a 4D Unicode text into another character set and returns the converted bytes as a BLOB.

constraints: charSet accepts either a standard character-set name string (e.g. "ISO-8859-1", "UTF-8") or its numeric MIBEnum identifier; several names can map to the same MIBEnum (aliases).
The produced BLOB can subsequently be read back with the Convert to text command.

params.name: picture
params.description: Picture to be converted (in); converted picture (out)

params.name: codec
params.description: Picture Codec ID: a file extension (e.g. ".gif") or a Mime type (e.g. "image/jpeg")

params.name: compression
params.description: Compression quality between 0 (most mediocre quality, high compression) and 1 (best quality, low compression)

overloads.semanticRole: Converts a picture to a new codec/type in place, optionally applying a compression quality when the target codec supports it.

constraints: If codec matches the picture's current type, no conversion occurs and the picture is returned as-is, unless compression is also passed.
compression is only honored when the target codec supports a compression quality setting (e.g. JPEG, HDPhoto) via the WIC/ImageIO APIs.
Codecs not supported in 4D 64-bit versions (e.g. PICT) require running the conversion on a 4D 32-bit version.

params.name: source
params.description: Array from which to copy

params.name: destination
params.description: Array to which to copy (created or overwritten with source's contents, size, and type)

overloads.semanticRole: Creates or overwrites the destination array with an exact copy of the source array's contents, size, and type.

constraints: In compiled mode the destination array must already be of the same type as the source array (behavior is only guaranteed to match interpreted mode when types match).
Copying object/collection arrays duplicates only references, not the underlying objects/collections; use OB Copy to duplicate the objects themselves.

params.name: srcBlob
params.description: Source BLOB

params.name: dstBlob
params.description: Destination BLOB (may be resized)

params.name: srcOffset
params.description: Source position for the copy (relative to the beginning of srcBlob)

params.name: dstOffset
params.description: Destination position for the copy (relative to the beginning of dstBlob)

params.name: len
params.description: Number of bytes to be copied

overloads.semanticRole: Copies a specified number of bytes from one offset of a source BLOB to a specified offset of a destination BLOB, resizing the destination if needed.

constraints: The destination BLOB can be resized if necessary to accommodate the copied bytes.

overloads.semanticRole: Copies a file or folder from sourceName to destinationName, optionally renaming a copied file, optionally overwriting an existing destination document when '*' is passed.

constraints: Without the trailing '*' parameter, an error is generated if a document already exists at destinationName; with '*', the existing document is silently deleted and overwritten.

To designate a folder rather than a file, both sourceName and destinationName must end with the platform folder separator; all intermediate folders in destinationName must already exist (they are not created).
newName only applies when copying a single file, to rename it at the destination; it is not used when copying a folder.

overloads.semanticRole: Copies the current selection of a table into a new (or replaced) named selection, leaving the table's current selection and current record unchanged.

constraints: The default table for the current process is used when aTable is omitted.
The source table's current selection and current record are left unchanged (only a copy is stored under name).
Use CLEAR NAMED SELECTION to free the memory used by name once no longer needed; memory cost is ~4 bytes per selected record.

overloads.semanticRole: Copies the contents of one set into another (creating/replacing the destination set).

constraints: srcSet and dstSet do not need to be the same set type (process/interprocess/local-client), as long as both are visible on the same machine.

overloads.semanticRole: Creates an alias/shortcut file pointing at the given target file or folder.

constraints: If targetPath is an empty string, the command does nothing.
Under Windows, if aliasPath does not end with the (invisible) ".LNK" extension, it is automatically appended.
If aliasPath is just a name (no path), the alias is created in the current working folder (usually the folder containing the structure file).

overloads.semanticRole: Creates a new (non-existent) data file on disk and hot-swaps it in as the data file used by the running 4D application, replacing the currently open one.

constraints: Fails/does nothing if a file already exists at accessPath (the command checks the path does not already correspond to an existing file before proceeding).
On 4D Server (since v13), executing this command internally calls QUIT 4D on the server first, which prompts every remote client with a server-quitting dialog.

overloads.semanticRole: Creates (or clears, if it already exists) a new empty set for a table, ready to be populated via ADD TO SET.

constraints: The default table for the process is used when aTable is omitted.
If a set with the same name already exists, it is cleared/replaced by the new empty set.
CREATE SET already implicitly creates the set it targets, so calling CREATE EMPTY SET first is unnecessary before CREATE SET.

overloads.semanticRole: Creates a folder at the given pathname, optionally creating any missing intermediate folders recursively when '*' is passed.

constraints: Without the trailing '*' parameter, an error is generated (and no folder created) if any intermediate folder in folderPath does not already exist.

With '*', missing intermediate folders are created recursively and no error is generated; in this mode folderPath may even include a trailing document name, which is ignored while the folder hierarchy above it is still created.

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table for which to create an index

params.name: fieldsArray
params.description: Pointer(s) to field(s) to be indexed

params.name: indexType

sentinelValues.meaning: Keywords index: word-by-word indexing (Text/Alpha/Picture fields only); cannot be composite
Default index type: 4D picks the most optimized type (excluding keywords) for the field contents
Standard B-Tree index
Cluster B-Tree index: optimized when few distinct keywords occur frequently

params.description: Type of index to create

params.name: indexName
params.description: Name of the index to create; if it already exists, the command does nothing
If passed, indexing runs asynchronously

overloads.semanticRole: Creates a standard or keyword index on one or more fields of a table, optionally running the indexing asynchronously.

constraints: Keyword indexes (indexType = -1) cannot be composite: fieldsArray must contain exactly one field.
Composite indexes require two or more fields in fieldsArray, and the order of the fields in the array matters for how the index is built.
If an index named indexName already exists, the command does nothing.
With '*' passed, indexing runs asynchronously: the calling method continues immediately, regardless of whether indexing has finished.
Locked records encountered during indexing are skipped until unlocked; the command waits for them.

overloads.semanticRole: Creates a new empty in-memory record for a table (without displaying it), for programmatic field assignment rather than interactive data entry.

constraints: The new record becomes the current record, but the current selection is left untouched.
The record only exists in memory until SAVE RECORD is called for the table; if the current record changes before saving (e.g. via a query), the new record is lost.
Does not require aTable to be in read/write mode; it can be used even when the table is read-only.

overloads.semanticRole: Loads the existing related (One-side) record for the given Many-side field, or creates a new related record in memory if none matches yet.

constraints: If a matching related (One-side) record already exists, this behaves like RELATE ONE and simply loads it into memory; otherwise a new related record is created.
When a new related record is created, you must assign the One-side field(s) from the Many-side field(s) yourself, then call SAVE RELATED ONE to persist it.

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table from which to create the selection

params.name: recordArray

elementTypeSelectsMode.Integer array: each element is an absolute record number to include in the selection
elementTypeSelectsMode.Boolean array: the Xth element (True/False) indicates whether record number X belongs to the selection

params.description: Array of record numbers, or array of booleans indicating per-record membership

params.name: selectionName
params.default: applies to the current selection if omitted or an empty string
params.description: Name of the named selection to create

overloads.semanticRole: Builds a named selection (or updates the current selection) for a table from either an array of record numbers or a parallel array of per-record booleans.

constraints: If selectionName is omitted or an empty string is passed, the command updates the current selection instead of creating a named selection.
With a Longint/Integer array, all values must be distinct valid record numbers; a duplicate or invalid (not-created) record number generates error -10503.
With a Boolean array, elements are read from index 0 to N-1 and the array length should equal the table's record count; if shorter, only the records covered by the array can be part of the selection.
Record numbers can be reused after a record is deleted and a new one created, so a stale Integer array of record numbers can silently select the wrong records.

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table of the set

params.name: recordsArray

elementTypeSelectsMode.Integer array: each element is an absolute record number to include in the set
elementTypeSelectsMode.Boolean array: the Nth element (True/False) indicates whether record N belongs to the set

params.description: Array of record numbers, or array of booleans indicating per-record membership

params.name: setName
params.default: applies to the Userset system set if omitted or an empty string
params.description: Name of the set to create

overloads.semanticRole: Builds a named set (or the Userset system set) for a table from either an array of record numbers or a parallel array of per-record booleans.

constraints: If setName is omitted or an empty string is passed, the command is applied to the Userset system set instead.
With a Longint/Integer array, an invalid record number (e.g. a never-created record) generates error -10503.
With a Boolean array, elements are read from index 0 to N-1; the array length should equal the table's record count, otherwise only the covered records can be in the set.

overloads.semanticRole: Creates a set from a table's current selection, saving both the selection and current record so USE SET can restore them later.

constraints: The default table for the process is used when aTable is omitted.
The current selection is copied into set and the current record pointer is saved with it; USE SET restores both the selection and current record later.
Sets have no sort order of their own; when a set is used, the default (creation) record order applies.
If a set with the same name already exists, it is cleared/replaced by the new set.

params.name: source
params.description: 4D picture field or variable to convert as a thumbnail

params.name: dest
params.description: Resulting thumbnail

params.name: width
params.description: Thumbnail width in pixels

params.name: height
params.description: Thumbnail height in pixels

params.name: mode

sentinelValues.meaning: Scaled to fit
Scaled to fit proportional
Scaled to fit prop centered (default)

params.description: Thumbnail creation/resizing mode

params.name: depth
params.description: Obsolete, ignored; do not use - the command always uses the current screen depth

overloads.semanticRole: Generates a resized thumbnail preview of a source picture into a destination picture field/variable, using a default or explicit size and scaling mode.

constraints: depth is obsolete and must be omitted: the command always uses the current screen color depth regardless of any value passed.
Only the three listed 'Picture Display Formats' constants (2, 5, 6) are valid for mode; other constants from that theme do not apply to this command.

overloads.semanticRole: Moves (rather than copies) a table's current selection into a new named selection, leaving the table's current selection empty afterward.

constraints: The default table for the process is used when aTable is omitted.
Unlike COPY NAMED SELECTION, this moves the current selection reference rather than duplicating it: after the call, the table's current selection in the current process becomes empty.
Should not be used while a record is being modified (since the current selection is emptied out from under it).
More memory-efficient than COPY NAMED SELECTION, since only the reference to the list is moved rather than 4 bytes per record being duplicated.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns an object describing the current cache contents (used memory, and the tables/indexes/BLOBs etc. currently loaded), optionally scoped to all running databases instead of just the current one.

constraints: Only works in local mode (4D and 4D Server); must not be called from a 4D application running in remote mode.

dbFilter is an object carrying a "dbFilter" attribute: pass the value "All" to get cache information for every running database (including components), or "" (or omit the parameter) to restrict to the current database only.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns a collection describing every step of the current process's method call chain (method/formula, calling database/component, and line number), equivalent to the Debugger window's call stack.

constraints: Works from any 4D environment including compiled mode, but requires Range checking to not be disabled for the command to operate correctly in compiled mode.
The 'formula' property of a returned object is omitted (Undefined) when the corresponding source code is not available.

overloads.semanticRole: Caps lock down returns TRUE if the Caps Lock key is pressed.
Overwrites a run of characters in source starting at a given position with newChars, returning the result at source's original length.

constraints: If newChars is an empty string, source is returned unchanged.
If where is less than 1 or greater than the length of source, source is returned unchanged.
Always returns a string of the same length as source (overlays characters starting at where rather than inserting them, unlike Insert string).

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the character whose UTF-16 code is charCode (1-65535); the inverse of Character code.
Returns the Unicode UTF-16 code (1-65535) of the first character of the character string; the inverse of Char.

constraints: If character contains more than one character, only the code of the first character is returned.

overloads.semanticRole: Selects and returns one of the value parameters; if criterion is Boolean it acts as a ternary (must pass exactly value1/value2), if criterion is an Integer it acts as a 0-based index into the full value list.

jointConstraints.rule: When criterion is Boolean, exactly two value parameters (value1, value2) are expected/used. When criterion is Integer, at least one value parameter is expected and criterion is a 0-based position into value1, value2, ... ; an out-of-range criterion yields a type-appropriate null value.

constraints: All value parameters must be of the same type; the command performs no type-consistency check itself.
value parameters cannot be pictures, pointers, BLOBs, or arrays.
Choose evaluates every value parameter before returning, even ones that are not selected -- side effects and errors in any value parameter always occur.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the number of consecutive clicks of the same mouse button in the current mouse-click form event (2 for a double-click).

constraints: Must only be called in the context of an On Clicked, On Header Click, or On Footer Click form event handler.

params.name: command
params.description: Command number to look up.

params.name: info
params.description: Filled in with a bit field describing the command: bit 0 = thread-safe, bit 1 = deprecated.

params.name: theme
params.description: Filled in with the name of the 4D language theme the command belongs to.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the (localized) name of the command numbered command, and optionally fills in info (thread-safe/deprecated bit field) and theme (language theme name) by reference.

constraints: Sets the OK variable to 1 if command is a valid, existing command number, and to 0 otherwise.
Some disabled-but-still-numbered commands return an empty string for the name even though OK is set to 1.

overloads.semanticRole: Compacts the data file (and its index file, if any) associated with a structure file, replacing the original data file in place and returning the pathname of the folder holding the preserved originals.

constraints: Can only be executed from 4D in local (single-user) mode or from 4D Server as a stored procedure.
The dataPath file must not already be open when the command is executed, otherwise an error is generated.

The option parameter is a combination of bit-flag constants from the 'Data File Maintenance' theme (e.g. Compact address table, Create process, Do not create log file, Timestamp log file name, Update records); passing 'Compact address table' alone implicitly also enables 'Update records'.
The method callback parameter is only ever invoked when the 'Create process' option bit is passed (asynchronous compacting); otherwise it is ignored.

overloads.semanticRole: Compares two text values under the current data-language collation (like the '<' operator) and returns -1/0/1, optionally modified by case/diacritic/kana/width-sensitivity options.

constraints: options is a combination of bit-flag 'sk ...' constants from the Strings theme (e.g. sk case insensitive, sk char codes, sk diacritic insensitive, sk kana insensitive, sk strict, sk whole word, sk width insensitive); several are mutually exclusive alternatives (case-insensitive vs. char-codes vs. strict) while others (kana/width insensitive, diacritic/case insensitive) can be combined.
sk kana insensitive and sk width insensitive only take effect when the current data language is Japanese; otherwise the comparison behaves as if sk strict were specified.
The @ wildcard character is not supported by Compare strings; it is evaluated as a literal '@'.
Return value is one of -1 (aString lower), 0 (equal), or 1 (aString higher) -- not an arbitrary signed magnitude.

overloads.semanticRole: Compiles the current host project (using Structure Settings compiler options, optionally overridden by options).

discriminatedBy.rule: Omitted -- compiles the currently opened host project.

overloads.semanticRole: Compiles the specified .4DProject file instead of the current host project (using Structure Settings compiler options, optionally overridden by options).

discriminatedBy.rule: Passed as a 4D.File -- compiles that project file instead of the current host project.

constraints: Binary databases cannot be compiled with this command.
Cannot be called while another compilation is already running (e.g. one launched from the Compiler window).
Components referenced via options.components must already be compiled (binary components are supported).
Passing an empty collection in options.targets performs a syntax check only, without compiling.
options.plugins is only honored with the projectFile syntax (not the host-project syntax).

overloads.semanticRole: Returns True if the current mouse event was a contextual (right-button, or Control+click on Mac OS) click.

constraints: Should only be used in the context of the On Clicked form event.

overloads.semanticRole: Converts an absolute POSIX-syntax pathname to the equivalent pathname in the current platform's system syntax.

constraints: posixPath must be an absolute disk path beginning with "/"; network paths (e.g. ftp://...) are not supported.

The '*' literal-symbol parameter tells the command that posixPath is percent-encoded (special characters escaped); if posixPath is actually encoded but '*' is omitted, the returned system path is invalid. Without '*', the output path is not encoded either.

overloads.semanticRole: Converts a system-syntax pathname (Windows or Mac OS, relative or absolute) to an absolute POSIX-syntax pathname.

constraints: systemPath may be relative to the database folder or absolute; a relative path is completed against the database folder in the returned value. The command always returns an absolute POSIX pathname.
The command does not verify that the path exists on disk.
The '*' literal-symbol parameter requests percent-encoding of special characters in the returned POSIX path (e.g. "My folder" -> "My%20folder"); by default (omitted), the output is not encoded.

overloads.semanticRole: Converts the raw bytes of a BLOB, interpreted as text in the given character set, into a 4D Text value (UTF-16).

constraints: charSet may be given as a standard character-set name or alias (e.g. "ISO-8859-1", "UTF-8") or as a numeric identifier (longint); see CONVERT FROM TEXT for the supported set.
If charSet designates a Unicode encoding (UTF-8, UTF-16, or UTF-32) and the BLOB begins with a Byte Order Mark, the BOM is detected and honored during conversion.

overloads.semanticRole: Duplicates the hierarchical list referenced by list and returns the reference number of the new, independent copy.

constraints: Call CLEAR LIST on the duplicate once it is no longer needed.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns a new collection of all parameters actually passed to the current method/function, optionally starting from the startFrom index (useful for forwarding a variable-length parameter list to another call).

constraints: Inside a formula, returns only the parameters passed via apply()/call(), not those passed to the enclosing method/function.
Returns an empty collection if the calling method/function was not itself called by another method/function, or if no parameters were passed to it.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the cosine of number, expressed in radians.
Counts how many elements of array are equal to value.

constraints: array and value must be the same type or a compatible type; supported array element types are Text, number, Date, Pointer, Object, and Boolean.
For Object arrays, value must itself be an object reference (comparison is by reference, not deep equality).
Returns 0 if no element matches value.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the number of items in a hierarchical list, either just the currently visible/expanded ones or the total including collapsed sublists.

interactionNotes.note: The leading '*' selects how 'list' is interpreted: passed = list is an object name (Text) identifying a form representation of the list; omitted = list is a ListRef (Integer). The trailing '*' selects what is counted: passed = total item count regardless of expand/collapse state; omitted = only currently visible items, which requires the object-name form if multiple representations of the same list exist in the form.

constraints: If several form objects reference the same list by name and the '@' wildcard is used in an object name match, the command applies only to the first matching object.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the number of items in the given menu (by number or MenuRef), in the specified process's menu bar (or the current process if process is omitted).

constraints: If menu is a MenuRef (reference), the process parameter is ignored.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the number of menus in the menu bar of the specified process (or the current process if process is omitted).
Returns the number of parameters actually passed to the current project method/function call.

constraints: Meaningful only inside a project method/function that was itself called by another method/function; returns 0 if the calling method is invoked directly from a menu.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the number of screen monitors connected to the machine.
Returns the highest alive process number, which (before any process has been aborted in the session) equals the total number of open processes including internal kernel processes.

constraints: Counts all processes including automatically-managed kernel processes (Main, Design, Cache Manager, Indexing, Web Server, etc.), not just user-created ones -- see Count user processes for the user-only count.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the number of live, user-initiated processes (i.e. those whose Process info origin is >= 0), excluding specific internal/system process types.
