params.description: If passed, the credentials are intended for an HTTP proxy rather than the target server; pass this in addition to a non-starred call if both the proxy and the server require authentication.

overloads.semanticRole: Registers client credentials to be encoded into the next HTTP request sent via HTTP Request or HTTP Get.

constraints: Encoded credentials are attached only to the next HTTP Request or HTTP Get call in the current process; if the 'HTTP reset auth settings' option (set via HTTP SET OPTION) is enabled, credentials are discarded after each request and this command must be called again before every subsequent request.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): HTTP client protocol: HTTP AUTHENTICATE / HTTP SET OPTION / HTTP SET CERTIFICATES FOLDER configure per-process client state -> HTTP Get or HTTP Request issues the request and consumes that state -> HTTP GET OPTION / HTTP Get certificates folder read back the currently active state.

params.name: option
params.description: Code of the HTTP client option whose current value to retrieve (one of the HTTP Client theme option constants).

params.name: value
params.description: Filled with the current value of option (its default, or the last value set via HTTP SET OPTION).

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the current value of an HTTP client option that will be used by the next request issued via HTTP Get or HTTP Request.

constraints: Options are local to the current process (or, inside a component, to the executing component).

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): HTTP client protocol: HTTP AUTHENTICATE / HTTP SET OPTION / HTTP SET CERTIFICATES FOLDER configure per-process client state -> HTTP Get or HTTP Request issues the request and consumes that state -> HTTP GET OPTION / HTTP Get certificates folder read back the currently active state.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the pathname of the folder 4D currently searches for client certificate files required by Web servers (the default "ClientCertificatesFolder" folder, or a custom one set via HTTP SET CERTIFICATES FOLDER).

constraints: Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): HTTP client protocol: HTTP AUTHENTICATE / HTTP SET OPTION / HTTP SET CERTIFICATES FOLDER configure per-process client state -> HTTP Get or HTTP Request issues the request and consumes that state -> HTTP GET OPTION / HTTP Get certificates folder read back the currently active state.

params.name: url
params.description: URL to send the GET request to, e.g. http://[{user}:[{password}]@]host[:{port}][/{path}][?{queryString}].

params.name: response
params.description: Filled with the body of the server response; the variable's type (Text/Blob/Picture/Object/Collection) selects how the raw response is decoded/parsed.

params.name: headerNames
params.description: In: names of request headers to send. Out: overwritten with the names of headers returned by the server.

params.name: headerValues
params.description: In: values of request headers to send. Out: overwritten with the values of headers returned by the server.
If passed, keep the server connection alive after this call instead of closing it automatically.

overloads.semanticRole: Sends an HTTP GET request to a URL and returns the server's response body plus response headers; the function result is the HTTP status code (0 if the connection itself failed).

constraints: If the response type doesn't match what the server actually returned (e.g. Object requested but response isn't parseable JSON), the mismatched case falls back: for Object, a 4D.Blob object is returned instead of a parse failure.
A return value of 0 indicates a network-level failure (DNS/unreachable server, not an HTTP error status) and an error is generated, interceptable via ON ERR CALL.
During HTTPS requests, the server certificate's authority is not checked by this command.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): HTTP client protocol: HTTP AUTHENTICATE / HTTP SET OPTION / HTTP SET CERTIFICATES FOLDER configure per-process client state -> HTTP Get or HTTP Request issues the request and consumes that state -> HTTP GET OPTION / HTTP Get certificates folder read back the currently active state.

params.name: data
params.description: Raw multipart/form-data HTTP message (a request or a response) to parse, as text or as a blob.

overloads.semanticRole: Parses a multipart/form-data HTTP message into a structured object, one property per part of the multipart data.

params.name: httpMethod
params.description: HTTP method of the request (e.g. GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE), one of the HTTP Client theme method constants.

params.name: url
params.description: URL to send the request to, e.g. http://[{user}:[{password}]@]host[:{port}][/{path}][?{queryString}].

params.name: contents
params.description: Body of the request; its type selects the default Content-Type sent (text/plain UTF8, application/byte-stream, a picture MIME type, or application/json) when Content-Type isn't explicitly set via headerNames/headerValues.

params.name: response
params.description: Filled with the body of the server response; the variable's type (Text/Blob/Picture/Object/Collection) selects how the raw response is decoded/parsed.

params.name: headerNames
params.description: In: names of request headers to send. Out: overwritten with the names of headers returned by the server.

params.name: headerValues
params.description: In: values of request headers to send. Out: overwritten with the values of headers returned by the server.
If passed, keep the server connection alive after this call instead of closing it automatically.

overloads.semanticRole: Sends an arbitrary HTTP request (any method) with an optional body to a URL and returns the server's response body plus response headers; the function result is the HTTP status code (0 if the connection itself failed).

constraints: If the response variable's type doesn't match the actual result, the mismatched-Object case falls back to returning a 4D.Blob object rather than failing to parse.
A return value of 0 indicates a network-level failure (DNS/unreachable server, not an HTTP error status) and an error is generated, interceptable via ON ERR CALL.
During HTTPS requests, the server certificate's authority is not checked by this command.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): HTTP client protocol: HTTP AUTHENTICATE / HTTP SET OPTION / HTTP SET CERTIFICATES FOLDER configure per-process client state -> HTTP Get or HTTP Request issues the request and consumes that state -> HTTP GET OPTION / HTTP Get certificates folder read back the currently active state.

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the active client certificates folder (used to locate the client certificate files required by Web servers) for all processes of the current session.

constraints: certificatesFolder may be relative to the application structure file or absolute, expressed using system (platform-native) path syntax; if the folder doesn't exist or the pathname is invalid, an error is generated (interceptable via ON ERR CALL).
Takes effect immediately for subsequent HTTP Request/HTTP Get calls in every process of the database, without restarting the application.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): HTTP client protocol: HTTP AUTHENTICATE / HTTP SET OPTION / HTTP SET CERTIFICATES FOLDER configure per-process client state -> HTTP Get or HTTP Request issues the request and consumes that state -> HTTP GET OPTION / HTTP Get certificates folder read back the currently active state.

overloads.semanticRole: Sets an HTTP client option (e.g. timeout, redirect handling, compression, auth dialog, logging) to be used by the next request issued via HTTP Get or HTTP Request.

constraints: Options are local to the current process (or, inside a component, to the executing component).
If the same option is set more than once before the next request, only the value from the last call is used.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): HTTP client protocol: HTTP AUTHENTICATE / HTTP SET OPTION / HTTP SET CERTIFICATES FOLDER configure per-process client state -> HTTP Get or HTTP Request issues the request and consumes that state -> HTTP GET OPTION / HTTP Get certificates folder read back the currently active state.

overloads.semanticRole: The IDLE command is designed only for use with the compiler.

constraints: Only meaningful in compiled databases: it should be inserted inside long-running loops (e.g. a For loop) that contain no other 4D command calls, so the compiler still yields control back to the 4D engine periodically during that loop.

overloads.semanticRole: The IMAP New transporter command configures a new IMAP connection according to the parameter parameter and returns a new transporter object.

constraints: The parameter object's .host property is mandatory; all other properties are optional and default as documented (e.g. .port defaults to 993, .connectionTimeOut to 30s, .checkConnectionDelay to 300s).
The .accessTokenOAuth2 and .password properties are consumed for authentication but are not echoed back on the returned transporter object.
The defined connection/check timeouts should be kept lower than the mail server's own timeout, otherwise the client-side timeout has no effect.

The optional .listener property is an Object with up to three named 4D.Function callback slots, each with its own (transporter:Object, event:Object) signature and event-payload shape -- documented as the IMAPListenerOnMailCreated, IMAPListenerOnMailDeleted, and IMAPListenerOnFlagsModified entries in references/4d-command-ir-callbacks.json (event.type is "mailCreated"/"mailDeleted"/"FlagsModified" respectively; onMailCreated also carries event.mailCount, onMailDeleted/onFlagsModified carry event.msgNumber, and onFlagsModified additionally carries event.flags). Not referenced via the schema's single-string callbackContractRef because that field supports only one contract per command, not a multi-slot listener object; cross-referenced here in prose instead.

params.name: fileName
params.description: Pathname of the file to import; pass an empty string to display the standard Open File dialog box.

params.name: project
params.description: In: XML import project settings (Text/DOM ref) or a legacy BLOB-format project. Out: updated with the new project settings, if * is also passed.
If passed together with project, forces display of the import dialog box pre-seeded with project's settings, letting the user adjust them before import.

overloads.semanticRole: Imports data from fileName using either an interactive dialog (if project is omitted) or a predefined/programmatic import project, optionally letting the user still adjust that project's settings via the dialog.

constraints: The optional * only has an effect when project is also passed; * without project is meaningless since there is then no predefined project to seed the dialog with.
The OK system variable is set to 1 on success and 0 if the user cancels the file/import dialog or the import fails.

overloads.semanticRole: The IMPORT DIF command reads data from document , a Windows or Macintosh DIF document, into the table aTable by creating new records for that table.

constraints: By default this command decodes the document using UTF-8; since DIF documents generally use the IBM437 character set, USE CHARACTER SET may need to be called first to set the correct charset.
Field/variable assignment is positional by front-to-back layering order of objects on the current input form, not by name; the input form must contain no buttons, and subform objects are ignored.
Default field/record delimiters (tab / carriage return) come from the FldDelimit/RecDelimit system variables and can be reassigned before the call.

overloads.semanticRole: The IMPORT STRUCTURE command imports, into the current database, the XML definition of the 4D database structure passed in the xmlStructure parameter.

constraints: If any imported table name collides with an existing table name in the current structure, an error is generated and the whole import is aborted.
Fails with an error if the current structure is compiled and/or read-only, and cannot be called from a 4D application running in remote mode.

overloads.semanticRole: The IMPORT SYLK command reads data from document , a Windows or Macintosh SYLK document, into the table aTable by creating new records for that table.

constraints: By default this command decodes the document using UTF-8; since SYLK documents generally use the ISO-8859-1 character set, USE CHARACTER SET may need to be called first to set the correct charset.
Field/variable assignment is positional by front-to-back layering order of objects on the current input form, not by name; the input form must contain no buttons, and subform objects are ignored.
Default field/record delimiters (tab / carriage return) come from the FldDelimit/RecDelimit system variables and can be reassigned before the call.

overloads.semanticRole: The IMPORT TEXT command reads data from document , a Windows or Macintosh text document, into the table aTable by creating new records for that table.

constraints: By default this command decodes the document using UTF-8 (USE CHARACTER SET can change this).
Field/variable assignment is positional by front-to-back layering order of objects on the current input form, not by name; the input form must contain no buttons, and subform objects are ignored.
Default field/record delimiters (tab / carriage return) come from the FldDelimit/RecDelimit system variables and can be reassigned before the call.

overloads.semanticRole: The INSERT IN ARRAY command inserts one or more elements into the array array .
The INSERT IN BLOB command inserts the number of bytes specified by len into the BLOB blob at the position specified by offset .

constraints: Does not support 4D.Blob objects, only the legacy Blob type, because this command alters the blob passed as a parameter in place.

overloads.semanticRole: Inserts a new item (with its own reference number, text, and optional sublist) into a hierarchical list before a given item, the last-added item, or the currently selected item.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when list should be interpreted as an object name (string) identifying a form representation of the list; when * is omitted, list is a hierarchical list reference number (ListRef).

jointConstraints.rule: Although both are individually optional, sublist and expanded must be passed together (or both omitted); passing only one is invalid.

constraints: Required to use the object-name (starred) form of list, rather than the ListRef form, if the same hierarchical list has several representations and you need to insert relative to that representation's own current item; a starless ListRef call would be ambiguous in that case.

beforeItemRef may be an actual item reference number, 0 to mean the last item added to the list, or the * literal to mean the currently selected item; if no item matches the given reference number, the command does nothing.
Since 4D v16 R4, itemText can be the ak standard action title constant to automatically use the localized name of the associated standard action.

overloads.semanticRole: The INSERT MENU ITEM command inserts new menu items into the menu whose number or reference is passed in menu after the existing menu item whose number is passed in afterItem .

jointConstraints.rule: If menu is passed as a MenuRef (Text), process is ignored (the menu reference already identifies which menu bar/process the item belongs to); process only matters when menu is a plain Integer menu number.

constraints: Without the trailing *, several menu items can be inserted in a single call the same way APPEND MENU ITEM does; see that command's description of itemText and the * parameter for the shared item-definition syntax.
If subMenu is passed and the call inserts more than one menu item, the submenu is attached only to the first inserted item.
Newly inserted items have no associated method or action; SET MENU ITEM PROPERTY / SET MENU ITEM METHOD (or handling Menu selected in a form method) must be used afterward to make them do anything.
Since 4D v16 R3, itemText can be the ak standard action title constant to automatically use the localized name of the associated standard action.

params.name: integer
params.description: 2-byte Integer value to write into the BLOB.

params.name: blob
params.description: BLOB to receive the Integer value; the legacy Blob type only, not a 4D.Blob object, since this command alters the blob in place.

params.name: byteOrder
params.description: Byte ordering to use when writing the value.

sentinelValues.meaning: Native byte ordering (default if omitted).
Macintosh byte ordering.
PC byte ordering.

params.name: offset
params.description: In: byte offset (from the start of the BLOB) at which to write the value. Out: updated to the offset just past the bytes written, so it can be reused for a subsequent BLOB-writing call.
If passed, the value is appended after the BLOB's current end instead of written at a fixed position, growing the BLOB accordingly.

overloads.semanticRole: Writes a 2-byte Integer value into a BLOB, either overwriting its start (if neither offset nor * is passed), at a given byte offset (advancing that offset for reuse), or appended to its end.

jointConstraints.rule: offset and * are mutually exclusive: pass at most one of them. Passing neither writes the value at the beginning of the BLOB, overriding its previous contents.

constraints: Newly allocated bytes other than the ones being written (e.g. a gap before an offset beyond the current BLOB size) are initialized to zero.
It is up to the caller to manage byte-order swapping when exchanging BLOBs written this way between Macintosh and PC platforms.

params.name: pathName
params.description: Absolute or relative (to the database folder) path of the log file to integrate; pass an empty string to display an Open File dialog.

params.name: operationNum
params.description: In: number of the last operation already integrated (integration resumes at the next operation), or -2 to integrate the whole file. Out: updated to the number of the last operation integrated, for reuse in a subsequent call.

sentinelValues.meaning: Integrate all operations in the log file.

params.name: mode
params.description: Integration mode.

sentinelValues.meaning: Strict mode (default): integration stops at the first error.
Auto repair mode: non-critical errors are bypassed and auto-repaired; each is logged into errObject if passed.

params.name: errObject
params.description: Filled with an "operations" array describing every record auto-repaired during integration (only meaningful in auto repair mode).

overloads.semanticRole: Integrates a 4D Server mirror log file into the database starting after a given operation number, continuing to use the current log file afterward rather than replacing it.

constraints: Can only be executed on 4D Server, via the Execute on server command or from a stored procedure.

Unlike the legacy _o_INTEGRATE LOG FILE command, this command does not replace the current log file with the integrated one; the database's current log file continues to be used, and any changes made during integration are appended to it.
Since operationNum became a required parameter (versions after v15 R4), pass -2 explicitly to restore the old default behavior of integrating the whole file.

overloads.semanticRole: INTERSECTION compares set1 and set2 and selects only the records that are in both.

constraints: set1 and set2 must belong to the same table; resultSet is created on that same table.
resultSet replaces any existing set of the same name, including the case where resultSet has the same name as set1 or set2.
resultSet retains a current record only if the same record was the current record in both set1 and set2; otherwise it has no current record.
In Client/Server, all three sets must be visible on the same machine (visibility depends on set type -- interprocess/process/local -- and where each was created).

params.name: action
params.description: Standard action name (or a Standard Action theme constant), optionally with a parameter pattern such as "gotoPage?value=2".

params.name: target
params.description: Form context in which to execute the action.

sentinelValues.meaning: ak current form (default if omitted): the form where the action was invoked; execution is synchronous, in the current cycle.
ak main form: the frontmost document/dialog form of the process; execution is asynchronous, in the next cycle after the calling form object method returns.

overloads.semanticRole: Triggers a standard 4D action programmatically, in either the current form (synchronously) or the process's main form (asynchronously).

constraints: Standard edit actions (Cut, Copy, Paste, Select all, Clear, Undo/Redo) ignore target if passed; they always execute synchronously in the context of the currently focused editable object.
Does not generate an error if the requested action is unavailable in the current context; use Action info beforehand to validate that the action applies.

overloads.semanticRole: In break returns True for the In break execution cycle.
In footer returns True for the In footer execution cycle.
In header returns True for the In header execution cycle.
The In transaction command returns TRUE if the current process is in a transaction , otherwise it returns FALSE .
Inserts the string what before the character at position where in source, returning the resulting string (source itself is not modified).

constraints: If what is an empty string (""), the function returns source unchanged.
If where is greater than the length of source, what is appended to the end of source.
If where is less than one (1), what is inserted before source (i.e. at the start).
Differs from Change string: Insert string inserts characters without overwriting existing ones.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the integer portion of number by truncation (not rounding).

constraints: Truncates toward zero rather than flooring: a negative number is truncated away from zero (e.g. Int(-3.7) returns -3, not -4).

overloads.semanticRole: The Is Windows command returns True if the current operating system is Windows.
The Is a list command returns TRUE if the value you pass in list is a valid reference to a hierarchical list.
The Is a variable command returns True if the pointer you pass in aPointer references a defined variable.
Tests whether the calling database/component context (or, if * is passed from a component, the host database) is running in compiled (True) or interpreted (False) mode.

constraints: The optional * parameter is only meaningful in a components architecture: when called from a component method, passing * returns the running mode of the HOST database instead of the component; omitting it returns the component's own running mode.
When called from a method of the host database itself, always returns the host database's running mode regardless of *.

overloads.semanticRole: The Is data file locked command returns True if the data file of the open database or at least one of its segments is locked — i.e.
The Is editing text command returns True if the user is entering values in an input form object, and False in all other cases.

constraints: Only meaningful with these form object types: input (enterable or non-enterable listbox), and combo box; with any other object type it always returns False.
Cannot be used with 4D Write Pro or 4D View Pro areas.
Intended for use inside code triggered by the On Before Keystroke form event, to distinguish actual text entry from shortcut-key handling (e.g. listbox scrolling).

overloads.semanticRole: Tests, by table pointer, whether fieldNum designates a field that exists in the pointed-to table.

discriminatedBy.rule: First parameter passed as a Pointer to the table.

overloads.semanticRole: Tests, by table number, whether fieldNum designates a field that exists in that table.

discriminatedBy.rule: First parameter passed as an Integer table number.

constraints: Returns False if the table containing the field is in the Trash of the Explorer, even if the field number would otherwise be valid.
Useful for detecting field deletions, which leave gaps in the sequence of field numbers.

overloads.semanticRole: The Is field value Null command returns True if the field designated by the aField parameter contains the NULL value, and False otherwise.

constraints: The return value is only meaningful if the "Map NULL values to blank values" option is NOT checked in the field's definition in the Structure editor; if it is checked, this command always returns False.
Cannot be used with object fields or object properties; use the Null command instead for those.

overloads.semanticRole: The Is in print preview command returns True if the Preview on Screen option is checked in the printing dialog box and False otherwise.

constraints: The Preview on Screen setting is local to the current process.

Unlike Get print preview, this command reflects the final value of the option after the user has validated the printing dialog box, so it reliably indicates whether printing will actually occur in preview mode.

overloads.semanticRole: Is in set tests whether or not the current record for the table is in set .
The Is license available command lets you find out the availability of a plug-in.

constraints: license can be passed three ways: omitted (returns False only when the whole 4D application is in demonstration mode); one of the '"Is License Available" theme' plug-in constants (e.g. 4D Client SOAP license = 808465465, 4D Client Web license = 808465209, 4D for OCI license = 808465208, 4D ODBC Pro license = 808464946, 4D REST Test license = 808465719, 4D SOAP license = 808465464, 4D View license = 808465207, 4D Web license = 808464945, 4D Write license = 808464697); or a raw plug-in "4BNX" resource ID number.
Takes into account licenses attributed in Design mode or via SET PLUGIN ACCESS; returns False if the plug-in is operating in demo mode.

overloads.semanticRole: The Is macOS command returns True if the current operating system is macOS.

The Is new record command returns True when aTable ’s current record is being created and has not yet been saved in the current process.You can obtain the same information by using the existing Record number command, and

constraints: Prefer this over checking Record number = -3, since Is new record is guaranteed compatible with future 4D versions.

On 4D Server, within an On Validate form event, behavior differs by mode: in local mode returns False (record already considered created); in remote mode returns True because the record is created server-side but not yet sent to the client.

overloads.semanticRole: The Is nil pointer command returns True if the pointer you pass in aPointer is Nil ( ->[] ).
The Is picture file command tests the file designated by the filePath parameter and returns True if it is a valid picture file.

constraints: Returns False if filePath is an empty string (""), or if the file is not found, or is not of the picture type.
Without the * parameter, the file is tested only by its extension against the list of available codecs (fast, but cannot test extensionless files).
With the * parameter, the file header is additionally loaded/inspected and the codecs are queried for a thorough validation; this is slower but works on files without extensions.
Returns True for PDF files under Windows and for EMF files under macOS.

overloads.semanticRole: The Is record loaded command returns True if aTable ’s current record is loaded in the current process.command will return False in remote mode (it returns True in local mode).

constraints: Reflects whether aTable's current record is loaded in the CURRENT PROCESS: returns False in remote (4D Server client) mode even when the record is loaded server-side, but returns True in local mode.

overloads.semanticRole: The Is table number valid command returns True if the table whose number is passed in the tableNum parameter exists in the database and False otherwise.

constraints: Returns False if the table is in the Trash of the Explorer, even though its number may still exist.
Useful for detecting table deletions, which leave gaps in the sequence of table numbers.

overloads.semanticRole: The Is user deleted command tests the user account whose unique user ID number you pass in userID .
The Is waiting mouse up command returns True if the current object has been clicked and the mouse button has not been released, while the parent window has the focus.

constraints: Must be called in the context of the current form object; intended for use together with the On Mouse Up form event (available for picture fields/variables).

Returns False once the parent window has lost focus before the mouse button was released, even if no mouse-up event has actually occurred yet -- use this to detect and recover from an object left indefinitely 'waiting' due to an interrupting external event (e.g. an alert dialog).

overloads.semanticRole: The Is window maximized command returns True if the window whose reference number is passed in window is currently maximized, and False otherwise.
The Is window reduced command returns True if the window whose reference number is passed in window is currently reduced in the taskbar (Windows) or in the dock (macOS), and False otherwise.

constraints: "Reduced" means minimized to the taskbar on Windows, or to the Dock on macOS.

params.name: jsonString
params.description: JSON string to parse

params.name: array
params.description: Array containing result from parsing of JSON string

overloads.semanticRole: Deserializes a JSON-formatted string into the elements of a 4D array, whose declared type determines how the values are coerced.

constraints: jsonString must be well-formed JSON, otherwise a parsing error is generated.
Starting with 4D 16 R4, this command can usually be replaced by JSON Parse returning a collection, which allows mixed-type data (more flexible than a typed 4D array).

params.name: jsonString
params.description: JSON string to parse

params.name: type
params.description: Forces the type to convert the parsed value into (Field and Variable Types theme constant).

sentinelValues.meaning: Is Boolean
Is collection
Is date
Is longint
Is object
Is real
Is text
Is time

params.description: If the parsed value is an object, adds a __symbols property with line position and offset of each property; ignored otherwise.

overloads.semanticRole: Deserializes a JSON-formatted string into a 4D value (object, collection, or scalar), optionally forcing the result's type and optionally attaching source-position debug metadata.

constraints: Also usable purely to validate that a string is well-formed JSON (a parsing error is thrown otherwise).
If pointers were serialized, JSON Stringify must have been used to produce jsonString before calling JSON Parse.
Real values must fall within ±10.421e±10; text values must have all special characters (including quotes) escaped.
By default (type omitted), 4D infers the type from the target field/variable if one is defined, else infers it from the JSON value itself.

Date strings in "YYYY-MM-DD" format are returned as date values automatically when the database's date setting is Date type (the default); the 'Dates inside objects' setting of SET DATABASE PARAMETER controls whether JSON date strings are treated as local time or GMT.
Time values are parsed from numbers, interpreted by default as a number of seconds.

The * parameter is honored only when the returned value is of the object type; if passed, the result gains an extra __symbols property giving each property/sub-property's path, line number, and line offset -- useful for debugging, ignored for non-object results.

params.name: object
params.description: In: object containing JSON pointers to resolve. Out: object with JSON pointers resolved (only if the result is an object).

params.name: options
params.description: Options for pointer resolution (rootFolder, merge).

overloads.semanticRole: Resolves every JSON pointer found in object (embedding/reusing referenced document fragments), updating object in place when the resolution result is itself an object.

constraints: If the resolution result is an object, the source object is updated in place with the resolved content; if the result is a scalar value instead, object is left untouched and the scalar is returned only via the function result's "value" property.
To keep an unmodified copy of the original object, copy it beforehand (e.g. with OB Copy).
options.rootFolder (Text) sets the absolute path used to resolve relative pointers; defaults to the database Resources folder.
options.merge (Boolean) merges objects with their pointer targets instead of replacing them; defaults to false.
The function result always contains: value (the resolution result), success (Boolean), and errors (a collection of {code, message, pointerURI, referredPath} objects when unsuccessful).

overloads.semanticRole: The JSON Stringify array command converts the 4D array array into a serialized JSON array.

constraints: array may be of the text, real, Boolean, pointer, or object type.
If a scalar variable or field is passed instead of an array, the command still returns a valid JSON array string wrapping that single value in "[ ]".
The optional * parameter enables pretty formatting, improving readability when the result is displayed (e.g. in a Web page).

overloads.semanticRole: The JSON Stringify command converts the value parameter into a JSON string.

constraints: Dates are serialized as "yyyy-mm-dd" or "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ" text depending on the current database date setting.
Numbers must fall within ±10.421e±10; Booleans serialize as the literal strings "true"/"false"; times serialize as a Real number of seconds by default.
Picture attributes are converted to the literal string "[object Picture]" (not real picture data).
Pointers to a field, variable, or array are evaluated (dereferenced) before being stringified.
The optional * parameter enables pretty-printing (adds formatting whitespace) in the resulting string.

overloads.semanticRole: The JSON TO SELECTION command copies the contents of an array of JSON objects jsonArray to the selection of records of aTable .

constraints: jsonArray must be a JSON array of objects, e.g. "[{\"attr1\":val1,...},...]"; each element maps to one record by array/selection order.
If an existing selection exists for aTable, elements are copied into those records in order; if the JSON array has more elements than the current selection has records, new records are created.
Every touched record (new or existing) is automatically saved.
WARNING: this command overwrites existing record data, so it must be used with caution.
A record locked by another process during execution is left unmodified and added to the LockedSet system set, which can be tested afterward.
Supports Object type fields: JSON data for those fields is converted automatically.

overloads.semanticRole: The JSON Validate command checks the compliance of the vJson JSON contents with the rules defined in the vSchema JSON schema.

constraints: Validation (checking vJson against the rules in vSchema) is distinct from well-formedness checking, which JSON Parse performs instead.

4D supports two JSON Schema Validation draft versions: 2020-12 (recommended; all vocabulary supported except contentEncoding/contentMediaType/contentSchema and $dynamicRef/$dynamicAnchor and https:... references) and version 4 (legacy, more limited).

The schema draft version is selected via the vSchema "$schema" key (e.g. "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema" or "http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#"); if $schema is omitted, version 4 is used for compatibility. An unrecognized $schema value raises an error.
If vSchema itself is not a valid JSON schema, 4D returns a Null object and throws an error catchable by an on error call method.
The returned object always has a success Boolean; when false, it also includes an errors collection of error objects.

overloads.semanticRole: The KILL WORKER command posts a message to the worker process whose name or number you passed in process , asking it to ignore any pending messages and to terminate its execution as soon as the current task ends.

Returns the single character just entered by the user into the enterable area currently being edited; intended for use inside an On Before Keystroke/On After Keystroke form-event method (does not work in subforms).
LAST RECORD makes the last record of the current selection of aTable the current record and loads the record from disk.

Launches an external executable process (fileName plus arguments), optionally feeding it inputStream as stdin and capturing its stdout/stderr into outputStream/errorStream, and returning its system-level process id in pid.

constraints: outputStream and errorStream are not returned if the _4D_OPTION_BLOCKING_EXTERNAL_PROCESS environment variable was set to "false" (asynchronous execution) via SET ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE before the call.
pid is not returned if the process launch fails.
Under macOS, this command can only launch executable applications, not shell built-ins (e.g. echo) or shell indirections.

overloads.semanticRole: The LDAP LOGIN command opens a read-only connection to the LDAP server specified in the url parameter with the login and password identifiers provided.

overloads.semanticRole: The METHOD Get attribute command returns the value of the attribType attribute for the project method designated by the path parameter.

constraints: attribType accepts one of the documented "Design Object Access" theme constants: Attribute invisible (1), Attribute published Web (2), Attribute published SOAP (3), Attribute published WSDL (4), Attribute shared (5), Attribute published SQL (7), Attribute executed on server (8).

overloads.semanticRole: The METHOD Get path command returns the full internal pathname of a method.

jointConstraints.rule: Which of aTable/objectName/formObjectName are required depends on methodType: Path project form needs objectName (form name) and optionally formObjectName (form object name); Path table form needs aTable, objectName (form name), and optionally formObjectName (form object name); Path database method needs objectName (database method name); Path project method needs objectName (method name); Path trigger needs aTable; Path class needs objectName (class name).

constraints: methodType accepts one of the documented "Design Object Access" theme constants: Path project method (1), Path database method (2), Path project form (4), Path trigger (8), Path table form (16), Path class (32), Path volatile method (128).
The command does not check whether the method actually exists; an error is generated only when an invalid database method name is passed with Path database method.

overloads.semanticRole: The METHOD OPEN PATH command opens, in the 4D Method editor, the method whose internal pathname is passed in the path parameter.

constraints: The method must already exist; if path does not correspond to an existing method, error -9801 ("Cannot open method") is generated.
When called from a component, the * parameter is mandatory (component code is read-only); omitting it in that context generates error -9763.
The command is asynchronous: it returns immediately without waiting for the Method editor to finish opening.

params.name: path
params.description: Path to resolve

params.name: methodType
params.description: Object type selector parsed from path

params.name: ptrTable
params.description: Pointer to the table, filled in when path references a table-form method or a trigger; otherwise left unset.

params.name: objectName
params.description: Form name (for a table-form or project-form path) or database method name (for a database-method path).

params.name: formObjectName
params.description: Form object name, filled in when path references an object method.
If passed, path is considered to designate a host database method when called from a component (otherwise ignored).

constraints: methodType accepts one of the documented "Design Object Access" theme constants: Path project method (1), Path database method (2), Path project form (4), Path trigger (8), Path table form (16), Path class (32), Path volatile method (128).
The command does not check whether the method actually exists; an error is generated only when an invalid table name is passed.

overloads.semanticRole: The METHOD SET ACCESS MODE command sets the behavior for 4D when you attempt to write access an object already loaded for modification by another user or process.
The METHOD SET ATTRIBUTE command sets the value(s) of the attribType attribute(s) for the project method designated by the path parameter.

jointConstraints.rule: attribValue must be a Text (a folder name) only when attribType is the 'Attribute folder name' constant (1024); for every other attribType constant, attribValue must be a Boolean (True to select the option, False to deselect it). The same rule applies to each repeated attribType/attribValue pair.

constraints: Cannot be executed in compiled mode; doing so generates error -9762.
When called from a component you must pass the trailing '*' parameter, because component code is normally read-only; if you omit '*' in that context, error -9763 is generated.

overloads.semanticRole: The METHOD SET ATTRIBUTES command allows you to set the attributes values for the method(s) specified in the path parameter.

jointConstraints.rule: path and attributes must be passed as the same kind: either both a scalar (Text path, Object attributes) or both an array (Text array path, Object array attributes) of matching length; you cannot mix a scalar with an array.

constraints: This command only works with project methods.
If called from a component you must pass the trailing '*' parameter (by default it applies to the component's own methods); '*' redirects it to the host database's methods.

overloads.semanticRole: The METHOD SET CODE command modifies the code of the method(s) designated by the path parameter with the contents passed in the code parameter.

jointConstraints.rule: path and code must be passed as the same kind (both scalar Text variables, or both Text arrays of matching length); the two syntaxes cannot be mixed.

constraints: If path designates a method that does not exist, it is created with the given code contents (project databases only: only database methods, triggers, and project methods can be newly created this way).

When called, the method's attributes are reset by default unless the first line of code contains valid JSON metadata (as generated by METHOD GET CODE), in which case that metadata sets the attributes and the first line is not inserted as code.
If called from a component you must pass the trailing '*' parameter, because access to the component code is read-only; omitting it in that context generates error -9763.

overloads.semanticRole: The METHOD SET COMMENTS command replaces the documentation of the method(s) designated by the path parameter by those specified in the comments parameter.

jointConstraints.rule: path and comments must be passed as the same kind (both scalar Text variables, or both Text arrays of matching length); the two syntaxes cannot be mixed.

constraints: Forms and form methods share the same documentation.
If called from a component you must pass the trailing '*' parameter, because access to the component code is read-only; omitting it in that context generates error -9763.

overloads.semanticRole: The MINIMIZE WINDOW command sets the size of the window whose number is passed as window to the size it was before being maximized.

The MOBILE APP REFRESH SESSIONS command checks all mobile application session files located in the MobileApps folder of the server, and updates existing session contents in memory for any edited files.

overloads.semanticRole: Loads (if needed) and displays the current input form for the current record of aTable (or the default table), letting the user modify it interactively; does nothing if there is no current record.

constraints: The current record must have read-write access and must not be locked by another process/user.

The second '*' overrides only the scroll-bar-hiding part of the first '*''s effect, re-enabling scroll bars in the input form; the one-record-selection output-form behavior of the first '*' still applies.

constraints: Places all records of the selection in Read-Write mode (locked for writing in other processes) while displayed; records are freed when the command finishes.

The Method called on event command returns the name of the method installed by the ON EVENT CALL command.

Min returns the minimum value in series .

constraints: attributePath is only meaningful when series is an object field; it defines a dot-notation path (e.g. "company.address.number") to a nested attribute whose values are aggregated across the selection. Attribute names are case-sensitive.
Non-numeric values found at the attribute path are ignored; only numeric attribute values are computed.
Returns 0 if the series selection is empty.

Modified record returns True if the current record of aTable has been modified but not saved; otherwise it returns False.

The Month of command returns the month of aDate .
NEXT RECORD moves the current record pointer to the next record in the current selection of aTable for the current process.
The NO DEFAULT TABLE command is used to cancel the effect of the DEFAULT TABLE command.

Create a new collection, optionally prefilled with one or more values passed as parameters; omitting all parameters creates an empty collection.

Closes the current log file, renames it, and creates a new log file with the same name/location as the previous one; intended for setting up a backup system based on a logical mirror.

overloads.semanticRole: The New object command creates a new empty or prefilled object and returns its reference.

constraints: Passed values: numbers are always stored as reals; if a pointer is passed it is kept as-is (not evaluated until something like JSON Stringify resolves it); dates are stored as "yyyy-mm-dd" or ISO datetime strings per the 'dates inside objects' database setting; times are stored as a number of milliseconds (Real).

overloads.semanticRole: Start a new process on the same machine, running the given process method with an allocated stack size and optional name/parameters, and return its process number.

jointConstraints.rule: If any param is passed to the process method, name cannot be omitted; it must be explicitly provided so the parameter list can be positionally reached.

interactionNotes.note: When the trailing '*' is specified, 4D first checks whether a process named `name` is already running; if so, no new process is created and the process number of the already-running process is returned instead.

constraints: Standard Object/Collection parameters passed in param are passed by copy (a duplicate is created in the destination process); pass a shared object/collection instead to get pass-by-reference semantics.

Pointers to variables (especially local/process variables) are not recommended as param values since the pointed-to variable may no longer exist when the process method accesses it; pointers to tables/fields are fine.
Arrays cannot be passed as parameters to the new process method.

overloads.semanticRole: Create a new shared collection, optionally prefilled with one or more values, whose elements can be safely accessed from multiple processes/workers under Use...End use.

constraints: Adding an element via the assignment operator (e.g. mySharedCol[i]:=...) must be wrapped in Use...End use, otherwise an error is generated; this is not required when adding elements via collection methods that already implement their own thread-safety.

overloads.semanticRole: The New shared object command creates a new empty or prefilled shared object and returns its reference.

constraints: Adding or editing a property on the shared object must be wrapped in Use...End use, otherwise an error is generated; reading a property, however, is possible without Use...End use.

Passed values: numbers are always stored as reals; a pointer is kept as-is; dates are stored as "yyyy-mm-dd" or ISO datetime strings per the 'dates inside objects' database setting; times are stored as a number of milliseconds (Real).

overloads.semanticRole: The New signal command creates a 4D.Signal object.

constraints: The returned 4D.Signal object is itself a shared object, intended to be passed as a parameter between workers/processes so the receiver can update it and the sender can wait on it (via the signal's own API) without consuming CPU.

overloads.semanticRole: The Next window command returns the window reference number of the window “behind” the window you pass in window (based on the front-to-back order of the windows).
The Not function returns the negation of boolean , changing True to False or False to True.
Null returns the Null type value null .

Return the numeric form of expression, using separator (if passed) as the decimal separator when expression is a Text; Boolean/Integer expressions convert directly (True/False to 1/0, or pass through).

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the optional trailing parameter is a Text decimal separator (or omitted entirely); mutually exclusive with the base syntax.

overloads.semanticRole: Return the numeric form of a Text expression parsed in the given base/radix (2-36), e.g. for hexadecimal or binary string conversion.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the second parameter is a required Integer radix between 2 and 36; mutually exclusive with the separator syntax.

overloads.semanticRole: The OB Class command returns the class of the object passed in parameter.

constraints: Returns null (rather than raising an error) if object is not an existing/valid object.

overloads.semanticRole: Return a deep copy of object, optionally resolving any pointer values into their evaluated targets during the copy (resolvePtrs).

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the second parameter is a plain Boolean (or omitted); mutually exclusive with the option/groupWith syntax.

overloads.semanticRole: Return a deep copy of object with fine-grained control via option (bitwise ck constants: ck shared to return a shared object, ck resolve pointers to resolve pointers before copying), optionally grouped into an existing shared object/collection's shared group via groupWith.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the second parameter is an Integer options bitfield rather than a plain Boolean; groupWith is only meaningful together with this syntax.

constraints: If object contains pointer values, the copy keeps them as-is by default (not evaluated) unless pointer resolution is requested via resolvePtrs (overload 1) or the ck resolve pointers option (overload 2).

overloads.semanticRole: The OB Entries command returns a collection of objects containing the contents of the object as key / value property pairs.

constraints: Only first-level property names/values are returned; property names of sub-objects are not flattened into the result.

overloads.semanticRole: Retrieve, in array, the values stored in the named array property of object.

constraints: property is case-sensitive.

overloads.semanticRole: Return, in arrProperties (and optionally arrTypes), the names (and value types) of the properties contained in object.
The OB Get type command returns the type of value associated with the property of the language object .can be an object varialble or a 4D object field..

constraints: property is case-sensitive.

overloads.semanticRole: The OB Get command returns the current value of the property of the object , optionally converted into the type specified.can be an object varialble or a 4D object field.

constraints: property is case-sensitive.

overloads.semanticRole: The OB Instance of command returns true if object belongs to class or to one of its child classes, and false otherwise.

constraints: If class is not a valid Class object, error -10745 is generated.

overloads.semanticRole: Check whether object itself is defined (initialized) when property is omitted, or whether the named property is defined on object when property is passed.
The OB Is empty command returns True if object is undefined or empty, and False if object is defined (initialized) and contains at least one property.can be an object varialble or a 4D object field.
The OB Is shared command returns True if the toCheck object or collection is shared, and False otherwise (see Shared objects and shared collections ).
The OB Keys command returns a collection of strings containing all of the enumerable property names of the object .

constraints: Only first-level property names are returned (sub-object property names are not included); the returned collection is ordered by property definition order, not alphabetically.

overloads.semanticRole: The OB REMOVE command removes the property of the language object designated by the object parameter.

constraints: property is case-sensitive.

overloads.semanticRole: The OB SET ARRAY command defines the array to be associated with the property in the language object designated by the object parameter.can be an object varialble or a 4D object field.

constraints: property is case-sensitive.
If property already exists in object its value is updated (overwritten with the new array); otherwise it is created.

overloads.semanticRole: The OB SET NULL command stores the null value in the language object designated by the object parameter.can be an object varialble or a 4D object field.

constraints: property is case-sensitive.
If property already exists in object its value is updated (overwritten with null); otherwise it is created.

overloads.semanticRole: The OB Values command returns a collection of variants containing all of the enumerable property values of the object .

constraints: The returned collection is ordered by property definition order, not alphabetically.

overloads.semanticRole: Creates a copy of the form object designated by object in the currently-executing form (Application mode); the source form from Design mode is left unmodified.

jointConstraints.rule: When the trailing '*' (useAbsoluteCoordinates) is passed, moveH, moveV, resizeH, and resizeV all become required and specify absolute coordinates/size for the copy; when omitted, all four remain optional and specify relative deltas from the source object's position/size (0/omitted = superimposed on the source).

constraints: Only one button in a form can have the 'Default button' property; duplicating such a button assigns the property to the copy and removes it from the source.
The keyboard shortcut of the source object is not duplicated; it is left blank on the copy.

If newName is omitted or empty, the copy's name is auto-generated by incrementing the source object's name; if the given/generated name is invalid or already used, the command does nothing and sets the OK system variable to 0.

Cannot be called from an object method's On Load event, from On Unload, or from printing-context form events (e.g. On Header, On Printing Detail); in an unsupported context OK is set to 0, and calling it in a printing context additionally raises error -10601.

params.description: Trailing '*', independent of the leading one: if passed, moveH/moveV/resizeH/resizeV are absolute coordinates/size instead of relative deltas.

overloads.semanticRole: Moves, and optionally resizes, the designated form object(s) in the current form, either relative to their previous position or (with the trailing '*') to absolute coordinates/size.

interactionNotes.note: Two independent, non-mutually-exclusive '*' flags in the same call: the leading '*' selects how object is addressed (name string vs variable/field reference); the trailing '*' (renamed here to 'absolute' to disambiguate from the leading one, since the schema keys params by name) switches moveH/moveV/resizeH/resizeV from relative deltas to absolute coordinates/size.

discriminatedBy.rule: When '*' is passed, object is an object name (Text) identifying the target by name; when '*' is omitted, object must be a direct Variable or Field reference.

constraints: Positive moveH/moveV move right/down respectively; negative move left/up.
By default, moveH/moveV/resizeH/resizeV are relative to the object's previous position; passing the trailing '*' makes them absolute instead.
If object is a name matched via the '@' wildcard against multiple objects, all matching objects are moved/resized.
Only functions in: input forms in entry mode, forms displayed via DIALOG, headers/footers of output forms displayed by MODIFY SELECTION/DISPLAY SELECTION, and form printing events.

params.description: Trailing '*'. If present, forces the target line (and column, if hPosition is passed) to be placed in the first visible position even if it was already visible; for pictures, places the requested point at the picture's origin (0,0) even if already shown.

overloads.semanticRole: Scrolls the visible content (rows/columns of a subform, list form, hierarchical list, or list box; or the pixel offset of a picture) of the object(s) designated by object and * to the position given by vPosition/hPosition, or, if these are omitted, auto-scrolls just enough to reveal the first highlighted line.

jointConstraints.rule: hPosition can only be passed if vPosition is also passed, since it is nested inside vPosition's optional group in the signature.

constraints: Uses the list box's 'standard' (non-hierarchical) row numbering for vPosition even when the list box is displayed in hierarchical mode, so results can differ between standard and hierarchical display.
For pictures, the object must be displayed in the 'Truncated (non-centered)' format for vPosition/hPosition to apply.
