overloads.semanticRole: Establishes and loads the related-many selection using the pre-modification (old) value of aField instead of its current value, then selects the first record of the resulting selection as current record.

constraints: Operates the same as RELATE MANY, except the relation is established using the old value of the one field (as returned by the Old function/command), not its current value.
Changes the selection of the related table and makes the first record of the new selection the current record.

overloads.semanticRole: Loads the record previously related to the current record, establishing the relation using the pre-modification (old) value of aField instead of its current value.

constraints: Operates the same as RELATE ONE, except the relation is established using the old value of aField (the many field, as returned by the Old function/command), not its current value.
To modify and save the loaded old related record, you must call SAVE RELATED ONE.
There is no old related record for a newly created record.

sentinelValues.meaning: Stops trapping errors for the given scope instead of installing a handler.

params.name: scope
params.description: Execution context for which errorMethod traps errors; a constant from the '4D Environment' theme.

sentinelValues.meaning: ek local: errors in the local execution context (current process); this is the default if scope is omitted.
ek global: errors in the global execution context of the project.
ek errors from components: errors generated from installed components.

overloads.semanticRole: Installs errorMethod as the error-catching method for the execution context designated by scope (local process, global, or components), or stops trapping errors for that scope if errorMethod is an empty string.

constraints: If scope is omitted, the local execution context (the current process) is used.
If a local (ek local) error handler is also defined for a process, the global (ek global) handler is not called for that process.
If ON ERR CALL is called from a process running in preemptive mode (compiled), errorMethod must be thread-safe or the compiler raises an error.
ON ERR CALL cannot be called from within the error-handling method itself.
Error-handling methods are installed per project: components and host projects each have their own, and only the method of the project where the error occurred is called.

sentinelValues.meaning: Stops intercepting events instead of installing a handler.

params.name: processName
params.description: Name of the process created for the event-handling method; defaults to '$Event Manager' if omitted.

overloads.semanticRole: Installs eventMethod as the event-catching method run in a dedicated process (named by processName, or '$Event Manager' by default), or stops catching events if eventMethod is an empty string.

constraints: The scope of this command is the current working session; only one event-handling method can be active at a time.
By default the event-handling method runs in a separate local process named '$Event Manager' if processName is omitted.
If processName is prefixed with a dollar sign ($), a local process is started (usually what you want).
Do not call commands that generate events from within the event-handling method, or it becomes very difficult to exit that method's execution.

overloads.semanticRole: ONE RECORD SELECT reduces the current selection of aTable to the current record.

constraints: If there is no current record for aTable, or the current record is not loaded into memory, the command has no effect.

overloads.semanticRole: The OPEN ADMINISTRATION WINDOW command displays the server administration window on the machine that executes it.

constraints: Must be called in the context of a connected 4D application or 4D Server; does nothing if called in a local (non-connected) 4D application.
Does nothing (and generates error -9991) if executed by a user other than the Designer or the Administrator.

sentinelValues.meaning: Apply the selected color to the text (also the default if omitted).
Apply the selected color to the text background.

overloads.semanticRole: Displays the system color picker dialog box and applies the selected color to either the text or the text background of the focused object's current selection, according to textOrBackground.

constraints: The picked color is applied to the current text selection in the object with focus only if that object's 'Allow Font/Color Picker' property is checked; otherwise the command has no visible effect.
This dialog box is modal under Windows but not under macOS.
If the color was changed, the On After Edit form event is generated for the object.

overloads.semanticRole: The OPEN DATA FILE command allows changing the data file opened by the 4D application on-the-fly.

constraints: If accessPath is only a file name (not a full path), the file must be located next to the current database's structure file.
Passing an empty string re-opens the database without changing the data file.

The command executes asynchronously: after the call, 4D continues executing the rest of the method, then the application quits (as if Quit had been selected) and re-opens with the specified data file; open processes get 10 seconds to finish before being terminated.
Should be used with caution in the On Exit database method (or a method it calls), since it causes the application to quit before re-opening -- risk of an infinite loop.
With 4D Server (v13+), this command makes an internal call to QUIT 4D on the server before opening the designated file.

overloads.semanticRole: Closes the current 4D database and opens on-the-fly the database designated by filePath, useful for automated testing or letting a merged remote application choose which database server to connect to.

constraints: filePath may use a .4db, .4dc, .4dbase, .4dproject, .4dz, or .4dlink extension; if only a file name is passed, the file must be located next to the current database's structure file.

The command executes asynchronously: after the call, 4D continues executing the rest of the method, then quits the currently open database (as if Quit had been selected) and opens the specified database; open processes get 10 seconds to finish before being terminated.

In single-user mode, the On Exit database method of the closing database and the On Startup database method (or On Server Open Connection database method) of the opening database are called successively.
Should generally not be used in the On Startup database method (or a method it calls), since it causes the application to quit before re-opening.
If the target database file is not found or invalid, a standard file system error is returned and 4D does nothing.

overloads.semanticRole: The OPEN FONT PICKER command displays the system font picker dialog box.

constraints: The selected font and/or style changes are applied to the current text selection in the object with focus only if that object's 'Allow Font/Color Picker' property is checked; otherwise the command does nothing.
This dialog box is modal under Windows but not under macOS.
If the font was changed, the On After Edit form event is generated for the object.

overloads.semanticRole: The OPEN PRINTING JOB command opens a print job and stacks all the subsequent printing orders there until the CLOSE PRINTING JOB command is called.

constraints: Must be balanced by a later CLOSE PRINTING JOB call to terminate the print job and actually send the document to the printer; if omitted, the print document remains stacked and unsent.
Print-setting commands (e.g. SET PRINT OPTION) must be called before OPEN PRINTING JOB, otherwise an error is generated (exception: the Orientation option can be changed within an open print job).
The print job is local to the process; each process has its own printing settings. Several print jobs can be open at the same time across different processes.
Starting with 4D v20 R4, printing jobs are non-blocking in new projects.

overloads.semanticRole: The OPEN RUNTIME EXPLORER command displays the Runtime Explorer in a floating window.
The OPEN SECURITY CENTER command displays the Maintenance and Security Center (MSC) window.

constraints: Cannot be executed on a remote 4D application.
Behaves like a call to DIALOG with the * parameter: the Maintenance and Security Center window is displayed and the command immediately returns control to the calling code.
If the current process finishes, the window is automatically closed by simulating a Cancel.

params.name: selector
params.description: Path key designating a theme, page, or group of parameters in the Preferences or Settings dialog box (e.g. "/Database/Compiler"); a lone "/" opens the first page of the Database Settings dialog box.

sentinelValues.meaning: Lock every other page of the dialog box; only the page named by selector remains active/modifiable.
Leave all pages of the dialog box accessible (default if omitted).

params.name: settingsType
params.description: Only meaningful for databases configured in 'User settings' mode; a constant from the '4D Environment' theme.

sentinelValues.meaning: Structure settings (default if omitted).
User settings.
User settings for data file.

overloads.semanticRole: Opens the 4D Preferences or the current application's Settings dialog box, displaying the theme/page/parameters designated by the selector path key, optionally locking the other pages (access) and choosing which settings store to target (settingsType).

constraints: selector is a path key of the form '/Dialog{/Page{/Parameters}}' (Dialog is '4D' for Preferences or 'Database' for Database Settings); passing an invalid key displays the first page of the Database Settings dialog box.
The set of valid selector keys differs between standard ('Structure settings') mode and 'User settings'/'User settings for data file' mode (settingsType 1/2 only accept a restricted subset of keys).

overloads.semanticRole: Opens the file or URL passed in path, using the application named in appName if specified (otherwise letting the system/default browser choose), optionally leaving the URL's special characters untranslated when '*' is passed.

constraints: If appName is omitted, 4D first tries to interpret path as a file pathname and opens it with the most suitable application; in this case the '*' parameter is ignored.
If path is a standard URL (mailto:, news:, http:, etc.) and appName is omitted, 4D starts the default web browser to open it.
If appName is specified but no matching installed application is found, no error is returned and the command runs as if appName had not been specified.
Does not work when called from a Web process.

overloads.semanticRole: The ORDER BY ATTRIBUTE command sorts (reorders) the records of the current selection of aTable for the current process based on the contents of the objectField 's attributePath .

constraints: Each ORDER BY ATTRIBUTE call sorts on exactly one level (one objectField/attributePath pair); for multi-level sorts, call the command repeatedly with the optional trailing '*' on every call except the last, which starts the actual sort.
Can be combined with ORDER BY calls in the same multi-level sort chain.
Only attributes containing scalar values (number, text, boolean, date) can be sorted; an array element in attributePath is an error.
attribute names are case-sensitive.
If the field attribute is null for a record, null values sort first in ascending order (>) and last in descending order (<).
If a single indexed field is specified (one-level sort), the index is used; otherwise (unindexed field, or more than one level) the sort is performed sequentially.
If aTable is omitted, the command applies to the default table if one is set, otherwise to the table of the first field passed.

overloads.semanticRole: The Object to path command returns a pathname (string) based upon path information you passed in the pathObject parameter.

constraints: pathObject must contain the properties: parentFolder (Text, directory info; last character must be a folder separator -- '/' selects a Posix-style path, otherwise the system separator is used), name (Text, final file/folder name without extension), extension (Text, starts with '.', can be omitted, empty string '' if none) and isFolder (Boolean, defaults to false).
Only builds a string: it does not validate the path's syntax against the chosen path type, nor check that any file or folder actually exists.
pathObject is typically produced by Path to object, but can be built by any means.

overloads.semanticRole: The Old command returns the value held in aField before the field was programmatically assigned a value or modified in data entry.

constraints: For a new (not-yet-saved) record, Old returns the default empty value for the field's type (e.g. empty string for Alpha, zero for numeric).
For Picture and BLOB type fields, the value returned by Old cannot be used directly as a parameter to another command for technical reasons; it must first be assigned to an intermediate variable.
To restore a field's original (on-disk) value, assign it the value returned by Old.

overloads.semanticRole: The Open datastore command connects the application to the remote datastore identified by the connectionInfo parameter and returns a matching 4D.DataStoreImplementation object associated with the localID local alias.

constraints: connectionInfo must describe a remote datastore whose Web Server is running with http/https enabled and which is exposed as a REST server; a 4D Client license may be required.
All connectionInfo properties are optional except hostname (host/IP + mandatory port number).

If tls is true, HTTPS is only actually used when HTTPS is enabled on the remote datastore, the port is the configured HTTPS port, and a valid certificate/private key are installed; otherwise error 1610 is raised.

If localID already names an existing local session, that session is reused; otherwise a new one is created (lazily, when the datastore object is first used). Calling ds(localID) afterwards returns a reference to the same datastore object.
Returns Null if no matching datastore is found.

sentinelValues.meaning: Presents the standard Open File dialog box for interactive selection instead of opening a named document.

params.name: fileType
params.description: Semicolon-separated list of file type(s)/UTIs/extensions to filter the Open dialog by.

sentinelValues.meaning: Do not restrict the displayed files to any type (".*" is also accepted).

params.name: mode
params.description: Constant from the 'System Documents' theme selecting the open mode.

sentinelValues.meaning: Read and Write (default if omitted).
Write Mode.
Read Mode.
Get Pathname.

overloads.semanticRole: Opens the document named by document (or presents the Open File dialog if document is an empty string), filtered by fileType, in the mode specified by mode, and returns its document reference number.

constraints: If the document is already open in Read mode and mode is omitted, it is reopened in Read/Write mode by default.
If the document is already open in Read/Write mode, attempting to open it in Write mode generates error -43; opening it Read-only instead succeeds.
Under Windows, if the user forces display of all file types (*.*) in the Open dialog and selects an unauthorized type, the command returns an error.
Sets OK to 0 (and returns a null DocRef) if the user cancels the Open File dialog; sets OK to 1 on success.

overloads.semanticRole: Opens a new window sized/positioned per the form formName's resizing properties (formName may be a form name, a POSIX path to a .json form description file, or a form-description object), returning the window reference number.

constraints: The window is not displayed automatically: a command that loads a form (e.g. ADD RECORD) must still be called to actually show the form in the window.
'Form has full screen mode Mac' and 'Form has no menu bar' are modifier constants that must be added to one of the other type constants, not used alone.
hPos/vPos are only used the first time the window is opened when the '*' parameter is passed (position/size are then remembered across closes/reopens).
Position parameters are expressed relative to the top-left of the application window's content area (Windows MDI mode) or the main screen (macOS and Windows SDI mode).

sentinelValues.meaning: Presents the standard Open File dialog box for interactive selection instead of opening a named resource file.

params.name: fileType
params.description: macOS file type (4-character string) or Windows file extension (1-3 characters) used to filter the Open dialog; if omitted, all files are shown.

overloads.semanticRole: Opens the resource file named or pathed by resFilename (or presents the Open File dialog if resFilename is an empty string, filtered by fileType), returning its resource file reference number.

constraints: If resFilename is an empty string, the standard Open File dialog box is presented for interactive selection.

If a resource file already open within the current 4D session is reopened, the existing reference number is returned instead of erroring (unlike Open document); attempting to open a resource file already open in another application raises an I/O error.

Each successful open (even of an already-open file) must still be matched by one CLOSE RESOURCE FILE call to actually close it; all opened resource files are auto-closed when quitting the application or opening another database.

overloads.semanticRole: Opens a new window at the pixel coordinates given by left/top/right/bottom (or auto-sized if right and bottom are -1), of the given type, with the given title and optional Control-menu-box/Close-Box method, returning the window reference number.

constraints: Kept only for compatibility; new code should use Open form window instead, which better suits current interfaces.
Passing -1 for both right and bottom auto-sizes the window from the form's Sizing Options, but only if FORM SET INPUT was called beforehand for that form with its optional '*' parameter.
Passing an empty string for title uses the form's designed Window Title, but again only if FORM SET INPUT was called beforehand with its '*' parameter.
A negative window type value opens a floating window (only supported by some window types).
If more than one window is open for a process, the most recently opened window is the active (frontmost) window for that process.

overloads.semanticRole: Outside call returns True for the After execution cycle.

constraints: Only returns True for a form's/object's 'After execution cycle' event; requires the 'On Outside Call' event property to be enabled for the form and/or object in the Design environment, otherwise the cycle is never generated.
Equivalent to testing whether Form event code returns the On Outside Call event.

overloads.semanticRole: Cancels the print job started with Print form, immediately stopping the print job in progress (most effective when the printer's 'Start printing after last page is spooled' property is set).

params.description: Continue-and-prioritize flag: holds the print job open (until PAGE BREAK is called again with no parameter) and gives it priority over other printing, guaranteeing the job spools to a single file.

overloads.semanticRole: Holds the current print job open and gives it exclusive priority (no other printing can occur) until PAGE BREAK is called again without a parameter, so the whole job spools to one file.

constraints: Used with Print form (in the On Printing Detail form event) to force page breaks and print the last page built in memory; do not use with PRINT SELECTION (use Subtotal or BREAK LEVEL's optional parameter instead).
The '*' and '>' forms are mutually exclusive alternatives, not combinable in a single call.
When the user clicks Cancel in the screen print preview dialog box, PAGE BREAK sets the system variable OK to 0.

overloads.semanticRole: The PAUSE INDEXES command temporarily disables all the indexes of aTable , except for the index of the primary key.

constraints: Cannot be executed from a 4D remote application.

Indexes are not physically deleted (unlike DELETE INDEX): they are only invalidated and stop being updated, and their internal index numbers are preserved (avoiding automatic reindexing on RESUME INDEXES, unlike a DELETE INDEX/CREATE INDEX cycle).
If the database is quit while indexes for a table remain paused (RESUME INDEXES was never called), all of that table's indexes are automatically rebuilt the next time the database starts.

overloads.semanticRole: PAUSE PROCESS suspends the execution of process until it is reactivated by the RESUME PROCESS command.

constraints: Silently does nothing if process is already paused, if process does not exist, or if process refers to the calling/main process (it only affects processes the caller has started).
A process delayed via DELAY PROCESS is also considered paused by this command.
Windows belonging to the paused process become non-enterable while it is suspended; the process itself stays in memory.

params.name: codecArray
params.description: IDs of available picture Codecs.

params.name: namesArray
params.description: Names of picture Codecs, parallel/synchronized to codecArray.
If passed, also return codecs that can only decode (read) pictures.

overloads.semanticRole: The PICTURE CODEC LIST command fills the codecArray array with the list of picture Codec IDs that are available on the machine where it is executed.

discriminatedBy.rule: By default (no '*'), only encoding-capable (write) codecs are returned; passing '*' additionally includes read-only (decoding) codecs in the result.

constraints: Codec IDs returned can be a file extension (e.g. ".gif"), a Mime type (e.g. "image/jpeg"), or, if QuickTime is enabled, a 4-character QuickTime code; the exact form depends on how the codec is registered at the OS level.
Codec IDs returned by this command are valid values for the format/codec parameter of WRITE PICTURE FILE and PICTURE TO BLOB.

params.name: picRefs
params.description: Reference numbers of the Picture Library graphics.

params.name: picNames
params.description: Names of the Picture Library graphics, synchronized with picRefs.

overloads.semanticRole: warning This command cannot be used in projects because the Picture library is only available in binary databases.

constraints: Cannot be used in projects because the Picture Library is only available in binary (.4DB) databases.
picRefs and picNames are synchronized: the nth element of picRefs is the reference number of the Picture Library graphic whose name is the nth element of picNames.
Both arrays are automatically created/resized by the command, and are returned empty if the Picture Library contains no pictures.
Maximum length of a Picture Library graphic name is 255 characters.

params.name: picture
params.description: Picture for which to get information.

params.name: width
params.description: Width of the picture expressed in pixels.

params.name: height
params.description: Height of the picture expressed in pixels.

params.name: hOffset
params.description: Horizontal offset when displayed on background.

params.name: vOffset
params.description: Vertical offset when displayed on background.

params.name: mode
params.description: Transfer mode when displayed on background.

overloads.semanticRole: The PICTURE PROPERTIES command returns information about the picture you pass in picture .

constraints: hOffset, vOffset and mode only have meaning for a picture displayed 'On Background' in a form; they are otherwise not meaningful.

params.name: picture
params.description: Picture field or variable to convert.

params.name: pictureBlob
params.description: BLOB to receive the converted picture.

params.name: codec
params.description: Picture Codec ID (extension, e.g. ".gif", or Mime type, e.g. "image/jpeg").

overloads.semanticRole: The PICTURE TO BLOB command converts a picture stored in a 4D variable or field to another format and places the resulting picture in a BLOB.

constraints: On success, the OK system variable is set to 1 and pictureBlob contains the converted picture; on failure (converter not available) OK is set to 0 and pictureBlob is returned empty (0 byte).
Valid codec values can be obtained via the PICTURE CODEC LIST command.

overloads.semanticRole: The PLAY command plays sound or multimedia files.

constraints: On macOS, sound is always played asynchronously regardless of whether async is passed.
The async parameter only affects behavior on Windows: if passed with 0 (or any longint value) playback is asynchronous, otherwise playback is synchronous by default.
Passing an empty string in objectName stops an asynchronous sound currently playing.
On macOS, objectName can also name a system sound instead of a file path.

params.name: numbersArray
params.description: Numbers of plug-ins.

params.name: namesArray
params.description: Names of plug-ins, synchronized with numbersArray.

overloads.semanticRole: The PLUGIN LIST command fills in the numbersArray and namesArray arrays with the numbers and names of the plug-ins loaded and usable by the 4D application.

constraints: Values returned in numbersArray can be compared with the constants of the 'Is License Available' theme.
Includes all plug-ins usable by the application, both integrated ones (e.g. 4D Chart) and third-party plug-ins.

overloads.semanticRole: POP RECORD pops a record belonging to aTable from the table’s record stack, and makes the record the current record.

constraints: Pushing a record that was unlocked keeps it locked for all other processes/users until it is popped (POP RECORD).
If any command moves the record pointer before the pushed/current record is saved, the copy held on the stack is lost.

overloads.semanticRole: The POP3 New transporter command configures a new POP3 connectionaccording to the server parameter and returns a new POP3 transporter object.

constraints: The parameter object's .host property is mandatory; all other properties are optional and default as documented (e.g. .port defaults to 995, .connectionTimeOut to 30s, .acceptUnsecureConnection to False).

If .accessTokenOAuth2 is passed but .authenticationMode is omitted, the OAuth2 protocol is used (if allowed by the server); .authenticationMode otherwise defaults to the most secure mode supported by the server.
.accessTokenOAuth2 and .password are consumed for authentication but are not echoed back on the returned POP3Transporter object.

overloads.semanticRole: The POST CLICK command simulates a mouse click.

constraints: If process is 0 or omitted, the click is posted at the application level and dispatched by the 4D scheduler to the appropriate process.

The '*' flag selects the coordinate system: if passed, mouseX/mouseY are expressed relative to the screen (global); if omitted, they are relative to the frontmost window of the destination process (local).

overloads.semanticRole: The POST EVENT command simulates a keyboard or mouse event.

jointConstraints.rule: If what designates a mouse-related event (Mouse down/Mouse up), message must be 0 (zero); if what designates a keyboard-related event (Key down/Key up/Auto key), message must hold the code of the simulated character.
mouseX/mouseY only carry meaningful click coordinates when what is a mouse-related event.

constraints: when is normally the value returned by Tickcount.
modifiers takes one or a combination of the Events (Modifiers) theme constants.
If process is 0 or omitted, the event is posted at the application level and dispatched by the 4D scheduler to the appropriate process.

overloads.semanticRole: The POST KEY command simulates a keystroke.

constraints: modifiers takes one or a combination of the Events (Modifiers) theme constants.
If process is 0 or omitted, the keystroke is posted at the application level and dispatched by the 4D scheduler to the appropriate process.

overloads.semanticRole: POST OUTSIDE CALL calls the form displayed in the frontmost window of process .

constraints: Only works between processes running on the same machine.
Does nothing if the target process does not exist or is not currently displaying a form.
Requires the On Outside Call form event to be enabled (in Form Properties) and handled in the target form's method, otherwise nothing happens.

Has an immediate, non-blocking effect: the caller process does not wait for a reply; a reply must be implemented manually (e.g. via interprocess/process variables read/written with GET PROCESS VARIABLE and SET PROCESS VARIABLE).

overloads.semanticRole: PREVIOUS RECORD moves the current record pointer to the previous record in the current selection of aTable for the current process.

constraints: No effect if the current selection is empty, or if the record pointer is already before/at end of selection (Before selection or End selection is True).
If moving before the current selection, End selection returns True and there is no current record; use FIRST RECORD, LAST RECORD or GOTO SELECTED RECORD to move back into the selection.

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table to print, or the default table if omitted.

params.name: document
params.description: Name of disk label document; if omitted, prints the current selection as labels using the current output form.
Do not reinitialize the current print parameters.
Suppress the printing dialog box.

overloads.semanticRole: Prints labels using the data of the selection of aTable, either via the current output form (no document) or via the Label Wizard / an existing label document on disk (document specified).

constraints: Cannot be used to print subforms.
If the user cancels the Print job dialog box (when not suppressed), the command is canceled and no labels are printed.

params.name: option
params.description: Option number: one of the 'Print Options' theme constants (e.g. Paper option, Paper source option).

params.name: namesArray
params.description: Names of the values available for the specified option.

params.name: info1Array
params.description: Additional info (1) for each name, meaning depends on option (e.g. paper format heights).

params.name: info2Array
params.description: Additional info (2) for each name, meaning depends on option (e.g. paper format widths).

overloads.semanticRole: The PRINT OPTION VALUES command returns in namesArray a list of names available for the print option defined.

discriminatedBy.rule: The meaning of info1Array/info2Array depends on option: for Paper option (1), info1Array holds paper format heights and info2Array holds paper format widths; for Paper source option (5, Windows only), the arrays carry different option-specific info. To apply a value with SET PRINT OPTION, pass either the corresponding namesArray entry or its info1Array/info2Array counterparts.

constraints: Only operates with PostScript printers.
Obtaining paper format information requires the print driver to have access to a valid PPD file for the printer.
Paper source option can only be used under Windows.

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table for which to print the current record, or the default table if omitted.
Suppress the printing dialog box, using the current print parameters.

overloads.semanticRole: PRINT RECORD prints the current record of aTable , without modifying the current selection.
overloads.note: tool4d-lsp-stdio rejects 'PRINT RECORD([T];*;>)' -- confirmed by live cross-check that '*' and '>' are mutually exclusive alternatives (two distinct doc syntax lines, 'PRINT RECORD(aTable{;*})' vs 'PRINT RECORD(aTable{;>})'), not two independently-combinable flags on one overload. A prior overlay revision incorrectly merged them into a single 3-param overload; reverted to keeping the two doc syntax lines as separate overloads, only correcting aTable's optionality (the parameter table documents it as defaulting to the default table when omitted, despite the doc syntax line omitting braces around it).

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table for which to print the current record, or the default table if omitted.
Do not reinitialize the current print parameters (useful across successive calls, e.g. inside a loop).

overloads.semanticRole: PRINT RECORD prints the current record of aTable , without modifying the current selection.
overloads.note: Second doc syntax line ('...{;>}'); autoparse dropped the '>' param here because its name ('>') doesn't match the parser's identifier pattern. Restored it explicitly.

constraints: Does nothing if there is no current record for aTable.
Prints unsaved modifications to the record (in-memory values), not the values on disk.
Unlike Print form, this command can print subforms.
If the user cancels the Print job dialog box (when not suppressed), the command is canceled and the record is not printed.

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table for which to print the selection, or the default table if omitted.
Suppress the printing dialog box, using the current print parameters.

overloads.semanticRole: PRINT SELECTION prints the current selection of aTable .
overloads.note: tool4d-lsp-stdio rejects 'PRINT SELECTION([T];*;>)' -- confirmed by live cross-check that '*' and '>' are mutually exclusive alternatives (two distinct doc syntax lines, 'PRINT SELECTION({aTable}{;*})' vs 'PRINT SELECTION({aTable}{;>})'), not two independently-combinable flags on one overload. A prior overlay revision incorrectly merged them into a single 3-param overload; reverted to keeping the two doc syntax lines as separate overloads.

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table for which to print the selection, or the default table if omitted.
Do not reinitialize the current print parameters (useful across successive calls, e.g. inside a loop).

overloads.semanticRole: PRINT SELECTION prints the current selection of aTable .
overloads.note: Second doc syntax line ('...{;>}'); autoparse dropped the '>' param here because its name ('>') doesn't match the parser's identifier pattern. Restored it explicitly.

constraints: Does nothing if the current selection of aTable is empty.
Performs the same action as the Print menu command in the Design environment.
If the user cancels the Print job dialog box (when not suppressed), the command is canceled and the report is not printed.

overloads.semanticRole: PRINT SETTINGS displays a printing dialog box.

constraints: Must be called before a series of Print form commands or the OPEN PRINTING JOB command.

overloads.semanticRole: The Print form command simply prints form with the current values of fields and variables of aTable .

jointConstraints.rule: If both aTable and form are passed alone (areaStart/areaEnd omitted), only the Detail area of the form is printed. If only areaStart is passed, it is treated as a Form Area theme marker constant (e.g. Form header, Form detail, Form footer) selecting a named section to print. If both areaStart and areaEnd are passed, they are pixel offsets delimiting an arbitrary section of the form to print, overriding the single-marker interpretation of areaStart.

constraints: Does not perform record processing, break processing, or page breaks; the caller is responsible for those.
Does not issue a page break after printing, so multiple forms/tables can be combined onto the same page; use PAGE BREAK to force one.

Builds each page in memory; you must call PAGE BREAK to flush/print the final page, except when running inside an OPEN PRINTING JOB, where PAGE BREAK must NOT be called for the last page (CLOSE PRINTING JOB prints it automatically; calling PAGE BREAK anyway prints a blank page).
Printer dialog boxes never appear; print settings must be set beforehand via PRINT SETTINGS (interactive) or SET PRINT OPTION/GET PRINT OPTION (programmatic).
Only the On Printing Detail form event is generated; subforms are not printed (use PRINT RECORD for subforms).
The returned height is the printed area's height, and is what Get printed height reports.
formData properties become available in the form context via the Form command during the On Printing Detail event.

overloads.semanticRole: Saves the current 4D print settings (layout and print parameters, including platform-specific driver settings) into printSettings so they can be persisted and restored later via BLOB to print settings; returns 1 on success or 0 if no printer is currently selected.

constraints: Must be used in conjunction with BLOB to print settings, which reloads a BLOB previously produced by this command; the generated BLOB must not be modified by programming.

The printSettings BLOB mixes cross-platform and platform-specific (driver-dependent) data; sharing one BLOB between Windows and macOS can lose platform-specific parts, so it is recommended to keep separate BLOBs per platform in heterogeneous environments.

overloads.semanticRole: The Printing page command returns the printing page number.

The Process aborted command returns True if the process in which it is called is about to be interrupted unexpectedly, which means that the execution of the command was unable to reach its “normal” completion.

constraints: This condition (the process being unexpectedly interrupted before its 'normal' completion) happens very rarely; processes are usually stopped before code can even observe the 'process aborted' status, so this can only realistically occur in compiled loops that are not executing any 4D command.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns a full, unfiltered snapshot: an object with a "processes" collection (all running processes) and, on 4D Server, a "sessions" collection (all connected user sessions).

discriminatedBy.rule: Called with no arguments.

Processes only - returns only the "processes" list
Sessions only - returns only the "sessions" list

discriminatedBy.rule: Called with a single Integer argument (no sessionID).

Returns a null object if sessionID is invalid.

discriminatedBy.rule: Called with a single Text argument (no options).

constraints: sessionID and options are honored only on 4D Server; when executed on 4D in remote or local mode, Process activity always returns the list of all running processes regardless of the parameters passed.
This command returns all processes, including internal processes not reachable by Process info.
Passing an invalid sessionID returns a null object.

If passed, retrieve from a remote 4D the number of a process executing on the server (returned value is negative, unless executed with * from the server machine itself).

overloads.semanticRole: Looks up a running process by its process name and returns its process number, or 0 if no matching process is found.

discriminatedBy.rule: Intended lookup key is a process name (not statically distinguishable from the 'id' overload -- both take a single required Text argument; which overload applies depends on the caller's intent, not on the argument's declared type).

params.name: id
params.description: ID of process for which to retrieve the process number
If passed, retrieve from a remote 4D the number of a process executing on the server (returned value is negative, unless executed with * from the server machine itself).

overloads.semanticRole: Looks up a running process by its unique process ID (as returned by Process info's "ID" property) and returns its process number, or 0 if no matching process is found.

discriminatedBy.rule: Intended lookup key is a process ID (not statically distinguishable from the 'name' overload -- both take a single required Text argument; which overload applies depends on the caller's intent, not on the argument's declared type).

constraints: The optional * flag retrieves, from a remote 4D machine, the number of a process executing on the server; the returned value is then negative, unless the command is executed with * from the server machine itself, in which case it is positive.
Returns 0 if no process is found matching the given name or id.

params.name: process
params.description: Process number

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the current run state of the given process (one of the documented state constants), or -100 ("Does not exist") if process is not a valid process number in the range 1 to Count tasks.

constraints: Return value is one of: Does not exist (-100), Aborted (-1), Executing (0), Delayed (1), Waiting for user event (2), Waiting for input output (3), Waiting for internal flag (4), Paused (5).
If process does not exist (i.e. is not in the range 1 to Count tasks), the command returns Does not exist (-100) rather than raising an error.

overloads.semanticRole: The QR DELETE OFFSCREEN AREA command deletes in memory the Quick Report offscreen area whose reference was passed as parameter.

constraints: area must reference an offscreen area previously created by QR New offscreen area; it is released from memory by this command and can no longer be used afterward.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): Quick Report offscreen area lifecycle: QR New offscreen area creates an in-memory area -> QR-SET-*/QR-GET-*/QR-Get-* commands configure and inspect its columns, sorts, totals, formatting and destination -> QR RUN or QR REPORT generates the output -> QR DELETE OFFSCREEN AREA releases the area from memory.

params.description: Composite (additive) value of the QR Borders theme constants indicating which side(s) of the cell to affect (e.g. left=1, top=2, right=4, bottom=8, inside vertical=16, inside horizontal=32); values can be summed to affect several borders at once.

params.description: Line thickness: 0=no line, 1=1/4 point, 2=1/2 point, 3=1 point, 4=2 points

overloads.semanticRole: Sets which border(s) of a given report cell are drawn, along with their line thickness and color.
The QR SET DESTINATION command sets the output type of the report for the area whose reference was passed in area .

constraints: The meaning of specifics depends on the value passed in type: for qr printer, specifics is "*" to suppress the print dialog; for qr HTML file / qr text file, specifics is the target file pathname (an empty string for qr text file triggers a Save file dialog).
Passing an empty string in specifics for qr text file output displays a Save file dialog instead of writing directly to a path.

For qr text file output, the default field/record delimiters are the FldDelimit/RecDelimit system variables (Tab / carriage return by default), which are shared with other commands such as IMPORT TEXT.

overloads.semanticRole: The QR SET DOCUMENT PROPERTY command displays the printing dialog or sets the unit used for the document.

constraints: The meaning of value depends on property: for qr printing dialog (1), value is 0 (hidden) or 1 (displayed, default); for qr unit (2), value is 0=points, 1=centimeters, 2=inches; for qr field separator (3) / qr record separator (4), value is a character code (defaults to FldDelimit/RecDelimit).

overloads.semanticRole: The QR SET HEADER AND FOOTER command sets the contents and size of the header or footer.

constraints: selector chooses which element is set: 1=header, 2=footer.
pictAlignment only applies when picture is passed: 1=left, 2=centered, 3=right.

overloads.semanticRole: The QR SET HTML TEMPLATE command sets the HTML template currently used for the Quick Report area .

constraints: QR SET DESTINATION must first be called to set the area's output type to HTML file for the template to be used.

qr cross report -- cross-table report

overloads.semanticRole: Sets (or changes) the report type of an area; changing the type on an existing report discards its previous settings and creates a new empty report.

constraints: Setting a new type on an area that already has a report removes the previous settings and creates a new, empty report.

overloads.semanticRole: The QR SET REPORT TABLE command sets the current table for the report area whose reference was passed in area to the table whose number was passed in aTable .

constraints: A table must be assigned to the report area because the editor uses that table's current selection to display data, perform computations, and propagate relations.

params.name: area
params.description: Reference of the area

params.description: Left boundary column number

Part of the all-(-1) combination that clears the selection

overloads.semanticRole: Highlights (or clears the highlight of) a cell, row, column, or the whole area, as if selected with the mouse.

jointConstraints.rule: If both left and top are 0, the entire area is highlighted.
To clear the current selection (select nothing), pass -1 for all four of left, top, right, and bottom.

overloads.semanticRole: The QR SET SORTS command sets the sort orders for the columns in the report whose reference is passed in area .

constraints: aColumns and aOrders are parallel arrays: aOrders{i} gives the sort order for the column number stored in aColumns{i}.
Each aOrders element must be 1 (ascending) or -1 (descending).
In cross-table mode, the arrays cannot have more than two items: only columns (1) and rows (2) can be sorted, not the data at their intersection.

params.name: area
params.description: Reference of the area

params.description: Number of the cell column (still required, even if unused, when rowNum is -4 or -5)

params.description: Reference of the cell row, or a negative constant designating a special report area

sentinelValues.meaning: qr title -- title area of the report
qr detail -- detail area of the report
qr grand total -- grand total area
qr header -- page header
qr footer -- page footer

params.name: property
params.description: Text attribute to assign, from the QR Text Properties theme (e.g. qr bold, qr font size, qr justification, qr font name, qr background color, qr alternate background color)

params.name: value
params.description: New value for the attribute selected by property; its concrete type (Integer flag/size/color number, or Text font name) depends on which property is targeted

overloads.semanticRole: Sets a single text-display attribute (font, size, style, color, justification, ...) of the cell identified by colNum/rowNum.

constraints: In cross-table mode, row values used in rowNum are always positive (the negative title/detail/grand total/header/footer constants are a list-mode-only convention).

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the break/subtotal cell at colNum/breakNum to display the result of one or more accumulated operators (sum, average, count, min, max, standard deviation) instead of literal text.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the cell should display a computed aggregate rather than literal/templated text.

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the break/subtotal cell at colNum/breakNum to a literal text template, which may embed placeholders (#, ##S, ##A, ##C, ##X, ##N, ##D, ##<colNum>) that are substituted with the break value or computed aggregates.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the cell should display literal/templated text rather than a raw computed aggregate.

constraints: operator and value are mutually exclusive: a single call sets either an operator (aggregate) or a text template for the cell, never both.
operator is an additive combination of the QR Operators theme constants (qr sum=1, qr average=2, qr count=16, qr max=8, qr min=4, qr standard deviation=32); 0 means no operator.
For the grand total, breakNum is -3 (qr grand total); for a subtotal, breakNum is the sort/break number.
This command cannot create a new subtotal, only set the details of an existing break.

params.name: area
params.description: Reference of the area

params.name: subtotal
params.description: Subtotal (break) level to affect

params.name: value
params.description: Spacing below the subtotal row: a positive value is pixels, a negative value is a percentage of the row height (e.g. -100 = 100%)

sentinelValues.meaning: No space is added
Inserts a page break

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the vertical spacing (or forces a page break) below a given subtotal row; applies only to list-mode reports.

constraints: If the added space pushes the next row onto a following page, no space is inserted above that row on the new page.

overloads.semanticRole: Opens the current input form as an interactive Query by Example window for aTable, using indexed fields automatically to optimize the resulting query.

constraints: The input form must contain the fields the user should be able to query on.
The trailing '*' here only suppresses the scrolling status bar during the query; unlike QUERY's trailing '*', it is not a multi-call continuation flag -- QUERY BY EXAMPLE is always a single call.

overloads.semanticRole: Applies a Boolean formula to every record of aTable (the whole table, not just its current selection), building a new selection from the records where the formula evaluates to True.

constraints: Scope differs from QUERY SELECTION BY FORMULA: QUERY BY FORMULA queries every record in the table, while QUERY SELECTION BY FORMULA queries only the records in aTable's current selection; otherwise the two commands work identically.
queryFormula must evaluate to a Boolean (True/False); it can be a simple field/value comparison or an arbitrarily complex expression/method, including evaluating a related table.
Parameters ($1...$n) are not supported inside queryFormula.
If queryFormula is omitted, 4D displays the interactive query dialog box instead.
Wildcards (@) and the "contains" keyword operator (%) can be used in queryFormula the same way as in QUERY.

When queryFormula reduces to a simple comparison equivalent to a QUERY call (e.g. [table]field=value), 4D executes it the same optimized, index-capable way as that QUERY call; more complex formulas can still have their optimizable parts executed first and combined with the rest.

overloads.semanticRole: Applies a SQL-syntax WHERE-clause formula (evaluated via 4D's built-in SQL engine) to every record of aTable, building a new selection from the records where it evaluates True.

constraints: sqlFormula is only the WHERE-clause fragment of an implicit "SELECT * FROM table WHERE ..." query; aTable supplies the FROM table.
Cannot be used in the context of an external SQL connection; it always connects directly to 4D's integrated SQL engine.
sqlFormula must be a valid SQL-2-compliant boolean search condition (True/False/NULL per the SQL standard); all rows where it evaluates True are included in the new current selection.
sqlFormula can embed references to 4D expressions/variables using the same <> or :MyVar syntax used in the integrated SQL commands or inside Begin SQL/End SQL blocks.
Compatible with the SET QUERY LIMIT and SET QUERY DESTINATION commands, like QUERY BY FORMULA.
Behaves like QUERY BY FORMULA otherwise: it changes aTable's current selection and makes the new selection's first record current.

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table for which to return a selection of records, or the default table if omitted

params.name: conjOp
params.description: Conjunction operator used to join this call to a preceding call in the same multi-query sequence; omitted on the first/only call

params.name: objectField
params.description: Object field whose attribute is queried

params.name: attributePath
params.description: Name or dot path of the object attribute to query

params.name: queryOp
params.description: Comparison operator between the attribute and value; can also be passed as an alphanumeric Text expression instead of a symbol (e.g. from a variable) to build configurable queries

params.name: value
params.description: Value the attribute is compared against
If passed, more calls follow in this multi-query sequence; omitted on the final call, which executes the accumulated query

overloads.semanticRole: Queries an object/entity attribute (objectField.attributePath) of the records currently selected in aTable, restricting the current selection to those matching the comparison, and can be chained across multiple calls joined by conjOp/'*'.

constraints: Scope differs from QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE: QUERY SELECTION BY ATTRIBUTE only searches within aTable's current selection, whereas QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE searches every record in the table; otherwise both commands work the same way.
Most useful when a query needs to run against a current selection that did not itself come from a previous QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE/QUERY call (e.g. one produced by USE SET).

overloads.semanticRole: Applies a Boolean formula to the records currently selected in aTable, building a new selection from the records where the formula evaluates to True.

constraints: Scope differs from QUERY BY FORMULA: QUERY SELECTION BY FORMULA only queries the records currently selected in aTable, whereas QUERY BY FORMULA queries every record in the table; otherwise the two commands work identically (see QUERY BY FORMULA for the queryFormula rules).

overloads.semanticRole: Searches only within the current selection of the table containing targetField for records whose value matches at least one element of array, replacing the current selection with the matches.

constraints: Functions identically to QUERY WITH ARRAY except for scope: this command only searches the current selection of the table containing targetField, whereas QUERY WITH ARRAY searches every record of that table.

overloads.semanticRole: Runs an interactive or programmatic query against the records currently selected in the explicitly given aTable, replacing its current selection.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the target table is passed explicitly rather than relying on the default table.

overloads.semanticRole: Runs an interactive or programmatic query against the records currently selected in the default table, replacing its current selection.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when aTable is omitted; applies to the default table.

params.name: field
params.description: The field to query; may belong to another table related to aTable via a One-side relation.

params.name: comparator
params.description: The comparison symbol (=, #, <, >, <=, >=, %) passed as its own alphanumeric-expression argument instead of embedded inside a single queryArgument string.

params.name: value
params.description: The value field is compared against.

overloads.semanticRole: Runs a programmatic query, over the records currently selected in aTable, using an alphanumeric-comparator calling form -- field, comparator, and value passed as three separate arguments after aTable -- instead of a single queryArgument expression string. Same calling-form variant as QUERY's third overload; the docs state QUERY SELECTION 'works and performs the same actions as QUERY' and defer entirely to QUERY's own description for queryArgument syntax.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the comparison operator itself needs to be a runtime value (e.g. a variable holding "#" or "="), letting callers build configurable query sequences or custom query UIs (see QUERY's Example 21). Using this form makes it mandatory to separate every item of the query with semicolons rather than embedding the comparator symbol inside one expression string.

constraints: Scope differs from QUERY: QUERY SELECTION only searches within aTable's current selection, whereas QUERY searches every record in the table; otherwise both commands share the same queryArgument syntax and multi-call '*' chaining behavior (see QUERY).
Most useful when a query needs to run against a current selection that did not itself come from a previous QUERY call (e.g. one produced by USE SET).

overloads.semanticRole: Searches all records of the table containing targetField for those whose value matches at least one element of array, replacing the current selection with the matches.

constraints: Cannot be used with fields of the Picture or BLOB type.
targetField and array must be of the same data type, except that a Longint array may be compared against a field of the Time type.
Scope differs from QUERY SELECTION WITH ARRAY, which restricts the search to the current selection instead of the whole table.

overloads.semanticRole: Runs an interactive or programmatic query against every record of the explicitly given aTable, replacing its current selection.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the target table is passed explicitly rather than relying on the default table.

overloads.semanticRole: Runs an interactive or programmatic query against every record of the default table, replacing its current selection.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when aTable is omitted; applies to the default table (error if none is set).

params.name: field
params.description: The field to query; may belong to another table related to aTable via a One-side relation.

params.name: comparator
params.description: The comparison symbol (=, #, <, >, <=, >=, %) passed as its own alphanumeric-expression argument instead of embedded inside a single queryArgument string.

params.name: value
params.description: The value field is compared against.

overloads.semanticRole: Runs a programmatic query using an alphanumeric-comparator calling form -- field, comparator, and value passed as three separate arguments after aTable -- instead of a single queryArgument expression string.

discriminatedBy.rule: Chosen when the comparison operator itself needs to be a runtime value (e.g. a variable holding "#" or "="), letting callers build configurable query sequences or custom query UIs (see the command's Example 21). Using this form makes it mandatory to separate every item of the query with semicolons rather than embedding the comparator symbol inside one expression string.

constraints: queryArgument is written as {conjunction ;} field comparator value: conjunction joins this call to a preceding QUERY call in the same multi-query sequence and is one of & (AND), | (OR), # (AND EXCEPT); it is omitted on the first/only call of a sequence and defaults to & (AND) if omitted elsewhere.

comparator is one of the symbols = # < > <= >= % (% means "contains keyword"); it can alternatively be passed as its own alphanumeric-expression argument (the third overload above) instead of embedded in queryArgument, which requires separating every item of the query with semicolons.
field may belong to another table if that table is related to aTable via a One-side automatic or manual relation.

To build a multi-criteria query, call QUERY repeatedly, passing the trailing '*' flag on every call except the last; the final call (no '*') actually executes the accumulated query and updates the current selection.

If queryArgument and '*' are both omitted, QUERY displays the interactive Query editor for aTable instead of running a programmatic query (except when this call is the closing call of a multi-query sequence).

The OK system variable is set to 1 if the query completes normally, or 0 if the user cancels the interactive editor (or, in 'query and lock' mode, if the query encounters at least one locked record, which also updates the LockedSet system set).

overloads.semanticRole: The QUIT 4D command exits the current 4D application and returns to the Desktop.

constraints: In 4D local mode or remote mode, the time parameter is ignored/cannot be used; it is only honored when QUIT 4D is called on 4D Server (in a stored procedure).

With 4D local/remote mode: if an On Exit database method exists, 4D runs it in a newly created local process before quitting (it can delay but not cancel the quit); if no On Exit method exists, 4D aborts every running process immediately, discarding any unsaved data entry.

With 4D Server: QUIT 4D is asynchronous (the calling method is not interrupted), time sets a timeout in seconds before the server actually quits (waits for all clients to disconnect if omitted), and it triggers a client-side dialog plus, after the delay, the On Server Shutdown database method.

overloads.semanticRole: Sets aTable (or the default table if omitted) to read-only state for the calling process; subsequently loaded records of that table cannot be modified.
Sets every table to read-only state for the calling process, using the '*' form instead of naming a single table.

constraints: Not retroactive: a record's read-only/read-write status is fixed at the moment it is loaded, based on the table's state at that time. To load a record from a read/write table in read-only mode, change the table's state before loading it.

params.name: fileName
params.description: Full pathname or bare file name of the picture file to read, or an empty string to show the standard Open file dialog.

params.name: picture
params.description: Field or variable receiving the loaded picture.
If passed, accept any type of file rather than only formats with an available codec.

overloads.semanticRole: Opens the picture file named by fileName from disk and loads it into the picture field or variable.

constraints: If fileName is a bare file name (no path), the file must be located next to the database structure file; under Windows the file extension must be included.
If fileName is an empty string, the standard Open file dialog box appears and the user selects both the file and the format.
The available picture formats/codecs can be enumerated with PICTURE CODEC LIST; without the trailing '*', only files matching a known codec are accepted.

overloads.semanticRole: Sets aTable (or the default table if omitted) to read/write state for the calling process; subsequently loaded records become unlocked (if not already locked by another user).
Sets every table to read/write state for the calling process, using the '*' form instead of naming a single table.

constraints: Only affects subsequently loaded records; it does not change the lock status of the record already loaded as current.
Read/write is the default state for all tables; this command is needed to revert a table from a prior READ ONLY call.

params.name: real
params.description: Real value to write into the BLOB.

params.name: blob
params.description: BLOB to receive the Real value; its size is adjusted to fit the written value.

params.name: realFormat
params.description: Internal format/byte-ordering constant for the written value: 0 Native, 1 Extended, 2 Macintosh Double, 3 Windows/PC Double.

sentinelValues.meaning: Native real format
Extended real format
Macintosh Double real format
Windows/PC Double real format

params.name: offset
params.description: Byte offset (from zero) within blob at which to write; on return, incremented by the number of bytes written so it can be reused for a subsequent BLOB write.
If passed, append the Real value at the end of blob instead of writing at the start or at offset.

overloads.semanticRole: Writes real into blob in the byte format/ordering selected by realFormat, either at the start of the BLOB, at a caller-supplied offset, or appended at the end.

jointConstraints.rule: offset and '*' are mutually exclusive alternate tails of the call; at most one of them may be passed. If neither is passed, the value is written at the start of blob, overwriting its previous contents.

constraints: New bytes allocated by extending the BLOB (other than the value being written) are zero-initialized.
Does not support blob objects (4D.Blob type); it mutates the classic BLOB parameter in place, so blob must be a legacy BLOB, not a 4D.Blob.

params.name: receiveVar
params.description: Variable receiving whatever characters are currently in the serial buffer; empty if the buffer is empty.

overloads.semanticRole: Immediately drains and clears whatever characters are currently sitting in the serial port buffer (opened via SET CHANNEL) into receiveVar, without waiting for a stop character or byte count.

constraints: Differs from RECEIVE PACKET: RECEIVE BUFFER takes whatever is currently in the buffer and returns immediately, while RECEIVE PACKET waits until a stop character is found or a requested number of bytes has accumulated.

On Windows the serial buffer is capped at 10 KB; on both Windows and macOS, once full, new incoming characters overwrite the oldest buffered characters, so the buffer must be drained promptly to avoid data loss.
The read interrupts on Ctrl-Alt-Shift (Windows) / Command-Option-Shift (macOS), raising error -9994, catchable via an ON ERR CALL method.

params.name: docRef
params.description: Reference number of a document opened via Open document/Create document/Append document; if omitted, reads from the serial port or document opened via SET CHANNEL instead.

params.name: receiveVar
params.description: Variable receiving the characters read; its type must match the type used by the corresponding SEND PACKET call.

params.name: stopChar
params.description: String at which to stop reading; the stop string itself is not included in receiveVar.

overloads.semanticRole: Reads characters from the serial port or document until the stopChar string is encountered (or, if not found, until end of document / until the reception is interrupted or times out on a serial port).

params.name: docRef
params.description: Reference number of a document opened via Open document/Create document/Append document; if omitted, reads from the serial port or document opened via SET CHANNEL instead.

params.name: receiveVar
params.description: Variable receiving the characters read; its type must match the type used by the corresponding SEND PACKET call.

params.name: numBytes
params.description: Exact number of bytes to read into receiveVar.

overloads.semanticRole: Reads exactly numBytes bytes/characters from the serial port or document into receiveVar.

constraints: When the received packet is a BLOB, it is returned unmodified regardless of any USE CHARACTER SET setting.

When the received packet is Text, RECEIVE PACKET detects and strips a leading Byte Order Mark if the current character set is Unicode (UTF-8/16/32), switching to the BOM's encoding instead of the current character set.

Reading a document with docRef always starts at the beginning on the first call and resumes after the last byte read on subsequent calls; Get document position / SET DOCUMENT POSITION can be used to inspect or change that position.
Reading past end-of-file returns the data read so far with OK set to 1; the following call then returns an empty string with OK set to 0.

The read interrupts on Ctrl-Alt-Shift (Windows) / Command-Option-Shift (macOS), raising error -9994, catchable via an ON ERR CALL method (mainly relevant when reading a serial port, since a document read without a stopChar match simply stops at EOF).

overloads.semanticRole: RECEIVE RECORD receives a record into table from the serial port or document opened by the SET CHANNEL command.

constraints: Only works with a channel opened by SET CHANNEL; documents opened via Open document/Create document/Append document are not supported.
The record must have been sent by a matching SEND RECORD call; if the source and destination table structures differ, 4D converts values according to the destination table's field definitions.
Automatically creates a new record for aTable (or the default table); the caller must call SAVE RECORD afterward to persist it.
The complete record is transferred, including any pictures and BLOBs stored in or with it.
The read interrupts on Ctrl-Alt-Shift (Windows) / Command-Option-Shift (macOS), raising error -9994, catchable via an ON ERR CALL method.

params.name: variable
params.description: Variable that receives the value; in interpreted mode it is created/typed on the fly if it doesn't already exist, in compiled mode it must already match the received type.

overloads.semanticRole: Receives a scalar variable previously sent by SEND VARIABLE from the document or serial port opened via SET CHANNEL, replacing variable's contents with the received value.

constraints: Only works with a channel opened by SET CHANNEL; documents opened via Open document/Create document/Append document are not supported.
Does not support array variables; use the BLOB commands to send/receive arrays instead.
In interpreted mode, an undeclared variable is created and typed based on what is received; in compiled mode, variable must already be of the same type as what is received.
The read interrupts on Ctrl-Alt-Shift (Windows) / Command-Option-Shift (macOS), raising error -9994, catchable via an ON ERR CALL method.

overloads.semanticRole: The REDRAW WINDOW command provokes a graphical update of the window whose reference number you pass in window .

constraints: 4D already handles graphical updates automatically on window move/resize/front-bringing and on form/value changes, so this command is rarely needed directly.

overloads.semanticRole: Forces a graphical refresh of the subform displaying aTable after its data was changed programmatically.
Forces a graphical refresh of the given Field/Variable form object; for a list box in selection mode, refreshes the data displayed by that list box.
The REDUCE RESTORE WINDOW command reduces/expands the window whose reference number was passed in window to/from the taskbar on Windows or the dock on macOS.

constraints: Toggles rather than sets a fixed state: if window is currently displayed, it is reduced to the taskbar/dock; if window is currently reduced, it is restored to its previous state instead.
On macOS the command is asynchronous.

overloads.semanticRole: REDUCE SELECTION creates a new selection of records for aTable .

constraints: Passing 0 for number empties the selection entirely, leaving aTable with no selection and no current record.
The new selection's first record becomes the current record for aTable in the current process.

overloads.semanticRole: The REGENERATE MISSING TABLE command rebuilds the missing table whose name is passed in the tableName parameter.

constraints: If tableName does not designate an actual missing table (data present in the data file but absent at the structure level), the command silently does nothing.
Use GET MISSING TABLE NAMES to enumerate the missing tables available to regenerate.

overloads.semanticRole: Registers a 4D client station under clientName on 4D Server, creating a named process on the client that other clients (or the server) can target via EXECUTE ON CLIENT.

jointConstraints.rule: The trailing '*' is only meaningful when clientName is also passed; it prepends '$' to clientName for compatibility with older naming conventions.

constraints: Has no effect when called from 4D running in local mode; it only does something on a 4D client connected to 4D Server.
More than one client station can be registered under the same clientName; names are not required to be unique.
A client's registered name cannot be changed while it is registered; you must call UNREGISTER CLIENT first, then REGISTER CLIENT again with the new name.
Clients can also be auto-registered at connection time via the "Register Clients at Startup..." option in the Properties dialog box.
The process created on the client station by this command can only be aborted by UNREGISTER CLIENT.

overloads.semanticRole: The REJECT NEW REMOTE CONNECTIONS command specifies whether or not the application server accepts new remote user connections.

constraints: Only takes effect on 4D Server; if the calling method executes locally on a remote client or in 4D single-user mode, the command does nothing.

overloads.semanticRole: Forces the user to remain in the current data-entry form (if aField is omitted) or in aField specifically (if passed), rejecting an attempt to accept/exit.

constraints: Two behaviors share one optional parameter: called with no argument, it rejects the entire data entry and keeps the user in the form; called with aField, it rejects only that field and keeps the user in it.
Docs recommend considering built-in data validation tools before reaching for this command.

overloads.semanticRole: The RELATE MANY SELECTION command generates a selection of records in the Many table, based on a selection of records in the One table, and loads the first record of the Many table as the current record.RELATE MANY SELEC

constraints: Also changes the current record of the One table (the table on the other end of aField's relation), not only the Many table's selection.

overloads.semanticRole: Establishes every One-to-Many relation for oneTable at once, regenerating the current selection of each related Many table based on the current value of each related field in the One table.
Establishes the single One-to-Many relation for oneField, regenerating the current selection of the related Many table.

constraints: Each call regenerates the current selections of the affected Many tables from scratch, and loads the first record of each new selection as the current record.

overloads.semanticRole: The RELATE ONE SELECTION command creates a new selection of records for the table oneTable , based on the selection of records in the table manyTable and loads the first record of the new selection as the current record.

constraints: Requires an existing relation path from manyTable to oneTable; the path can span several intermediate related tables and can be manual or automatic (automatic relations are preferred whenever both exist).

overloads.semanticRole: Establishes every automatic Many-to-One relation for manyTable at once, loading each related table's related record as its current record.

Looks up the (not necessarily automatic) relation for manyField and loads the related record as current; if choiceField is given and multiple candidates match, shows a selection list to the user instead of failing.

constraints: choiceField must be an Alpha, Text, Numeric, Date, Time, or Boolean field in the related table; Picture, BLOB, and Object type fields are not supported for choiceField, and this command does not support Object type fields for manyField either.

More than one matching record can occur when manyField ends with the wildcard character '@'; the resulting selection list shows related-field values in the left column and choiceField values in the right column, and is skipped automatically when only one match exists.
Passing choiceField is equivalent to specifying a wildcard choice when defining the table relation itself.

overloads.semanticRole: The RELEASE MENU command removes the menu whose ID is passed in menu from memory.

constraints: Every menu created via Create menu must eventually be matched by a corresponding RELEASE MENU call.

Removes every instance of the menu from every menu bar and process; if a menu bar using it is currently in use, the menu keeps working (but can no longer be modified) until that menu bar's last use ends, at which point it is actually freed from memory.

params.name: aField
params.description: Field for which to reload the storage location. Must be an actual field reference (e.g. [Table]FieldName) of type Text, BLOB, Picture, or Object -- the doc's own Type column names the field's data type, not the shape of a value that can be passed here; a same-typed variable or literal is rejected by the compiler ("The function expects a field not a variable or constant.").

overloads.semanticRole: The RELOAD EXTERNAL DATA command reloads the contents in memory of an external storage file associated with a BLOB, Picture, or Text type field.

constraints: Only useful for BLOB, Picture, or Text type fields that use an external storage file, when that file has been modified on disk (e.g. by an external editor) after the record was already loaded into memory.

overloads.semanticRole: The RELOAD PROJECT command reloads the source file definitions (methods, forms, etc.) from the disk for the running project in the current 4D environment.

constraints: Only usable with 4D projects running in interpreted mode.
Execution is asynchronous.

4D normally reloads a project automatically when it detects a source file was added/modified/deleted (e.g. edited from the 4D Developer IDE, or when the app window returns to the foreground); this command is only necessary when that automatic detection doesn't apply.

overloads.semanticRole: REMOVE FROM SET removes the current record of aTable from set .

constraints: set must already exist; if it does not, an error occurs.
If aTable (or the default table) has no current record, the command silently does nothing.

overloads.semanticRole: Removes the Picture Library graphic identified by picRef; does nothing if no picture has that reference number.
Removes the Picture Library graphic identified by picName; does nothing if no picture has that name.

constraints: Cannot be used in projects; the Picture Library only exists in binary (.4DB) databases.
Has no effect when called from a method executed on the 4D Server machine (stored procedure or trigger); the call is silently ignored there.

overloads.semanticRole: The RESIZE FORM WINDOW command lets you change the size of the current form window.

constraints: width/height are deltas (pixels to add), not absolute sizes; pass 0 to leave a dimension unchanged, or a negative value to shrink it.
Produces the exact same result as a manual resize via the resize box (when the window type allows resizing), so it still respects each object's resize properties and the form's size limitations.

params.name: aliasPath
params.description: Name or access path of the alias/shortcut to resolve.

params.name: targetPath
params.description: Receives the full path to the alias/shortcut's target file or folder.

overloads.semanticRole: Resolves aliasPath to the full path of the file or folder it points to, writing the result into targetPath.

constraints: Sets the OK system variable to 1 when aliasPath was a genuine alias/shortcut successfully resolved.
If aliasPath is actually a plain file (not an alias/shortcut), targetPath returns that file's own path and OK is set to 0.

params.name: aPointer
params.description: Pointer for which to retrieve the referenced object

params.name: varName

sentinelValues.meaning: referenced object is NIL, a table, or a field

params.description: Name of referenced variable or empty string

params.name: tableNum

sentinelValues.meaning: referenced object is NIL
referenced object is a variable, array, or array element (not a table/field)

params.description: Number of referenced table or array element or 0 or -1

params.name: fieldNum

sentinelValues.meaning: referenced object is NIL or a table
referenced object is a variable, array, or array element

params.description: Number of referenced field or 0

overloads.semanticRole: Retrieves what an existing pointer references (NIL, a variable, an array, an array element, a table, or a field) and decodes that identity into varName/tableNum/fieldNum.

constraints: aPointer must be an actual pointer expression, or a syntax error occurs.
Does not work with pointers to local variables, since several local variables with the same name can exist in different locations.

params.name: resType
params.description: 4-character resource type

params.name: resIDs
params.description: Resource ID numbers for resources of this type

params.name: resNames
params.description: Resource names for resources of this type

params.name: resFile
params.description: Resource file reference number, or all open resource files, if omitted

overloads.semanticRole: Populates resIDs and resNames with the IDs and names of all resources of type resType across open resource files (or one file if resFile is given).

constraints: resType must be a 4-character string.
If resFile is a valid resource file reference number, only that file's resources are listed; if omitted, all currently open resource files are listed.
If predeclared, resIDs must be a Longint array and resNames a String/Text array; otherwise the command creates them as Longint and Text arrays respectively.

params.name: resTypes
params.description: List of available resource types
