params.name: resFile
params.description: Resource file reference number, or all open resource files, if omitted

overloads.semanticRole: Populates resTypes with the distinct resource types present across the currently open resource files (or one file if resFile is given).

constraints: If resFile is a valid resource file reference number, only that file's resource types are listed; if omitted, all currently open resource files are used.
resTypes may be predeclared as a String/Text array; otherwise the command creates it as a Text array.

overloads.semanticRole: The RESTART 4D command restarts the current 4D application.

constraints: time and message are only taken into account with server applications; they are ignored if executed in single-user or remote applications.
If time is omitted, the server waits up to 10 minutes for all client applications to disconnect before automatically disconnecting them.

Restart is combined with SET UPDATE FOLDER: if update information was specified in the current session, the new version designated by SET UPDATE FOLDER automatically replaces the current version at restart; otherwise, 4D simply restarts with the current structure and data files.
Sets the OK system variable to 1 if the command executed correctly, or 0 (and the application still restarts) otherwise.

params.name: selector

sentinelValues.meaning: Last Restore Date -- info1 returns the date and info2 the time of the last automatic database restore.
Last Restore Status -- info1 returns the status number and info2 the status text of the last automatic database restore.

params.description: Type of information to get

params.name: info1
params.description: Value 1 of the selector (Date if selector=0, status-number Integer if selector=2)

params.name: info2
params.description: Value 2 of the selector (Time if selector=0, status-text Text if selector=2)

overloads.semanticRole: Gets information about the last automatic database restore, with the concrete meaning/type of info1 and info2 selected by selector.

jointConstraints.rule: selector=0 (Last Restore Date) yields info1=Date, info2=Time; selector=2 (Last Restore Status) yields info1=Integer status number, info2=Text status description.

constraints: This command does not take manual (only automatic) database restores into account.

overloads.semanticRole: The RESTORE command can be used to restore the file(s) included in a 4D archive.

jointConstraints.rule: destFolderPath is only meaningful when archivePath is also passed; passing destFolderPath suppresses the destination-folder chooser step of the restore dialog.

constraints: If archivePath is omitted, an open-file dialog box lets the user select the archive to restore.
archivePath/destFolderPath must be expressed with system syntax (absolute, or relative to the database structure file).

If destFolderPath is omitted (but archivePath given), the standard restore dialog appears with the archive pre-selected so the user can choose the destination folder; if destFolderPath is also passed, a preconfigured dialog appears where the user can only launch or cancel.
Sets the OK and Document system variables: OK=1 and Document set to the restore folder pathname on success; OK=0 otherwise.

overloads.semanticRole: The RESUME INDEXES command reactivates all the indexes of aTable when they have been paused previously using the PAUSE INDEXES command.

constraints: Can only be called from 4D Server or a local 4D application; if executed from a remote 4D machine, error -10513 is generated (interceptable via ON ERR CALL).
If the indexes of aTable were not previously paused (via PAUSE INDEXES), this command does nothing.
Without the * parameter, index rebuilding blocks execution of the calling method until complete; with * passed, rebuilding runs asynchronously and the method continues immediately.

overloads.semanticRole: RESUME PROCESS resumes a process whose execution has been paused or delayed.

constraints: If process is not paused or delayed, or does not exist, the command does nothing.
Cannot be used from a client machine to resume a stored procedure on the server (process < 0).

overloads.semanticRole: The RESUME TRANSACTION command resumes the transaction that was paused using SUSPEND TRANSACTION at the corresponding level in the current process.
Returns a random integer value between 0 and 32,767 (inclusive).

constraints: To pick a random integer in an arbitrary range [vStart, vEnd], use the formula (Random % (vEnd-vStart+1)) + vStart.

overloads.semanticRole: This function tests whether or not the state of aTable is read-only for the process in which it is called.
Record number returns the physical record number for the current record of aTable .

constraints: Returns -1 (No current record constant) if there is no current record (e.g. the record pointer is before/after the current selection).
Returns -3 (New record constant) if the current record is a new record that has not yet been saved.
Record numbers can change over time; deleted records' numbers are reused.
4D Server: for the On Validate form event, returns a real record number in local mode but -3 in remote mode, because the record is already created server-side but not yet sent to the client.
Prefer Is new record to test whether a record is currently being created.

overloads.semanticRole: Records in selection returns the number of records in the current selection of aTable .

constraints: Distinct from Records in table, which returns the total number of records in the table regardless of the current selection.

overloads.semanticRole: Records in set returns the number of records in set .

constraints: Returns 0 if set does not exist or contains no records.

overloads.semanticRole: Records in table returns the total number of records in aTable.

constraints: Distinct from Records in selection, which returns the count of only the current selection.
If called within a transaction, records created during that transaction are included in the count.

overloads.semanticRole: Connects to the 4D customer database and activates any new or updated licenses for the current 4D Server license, returning a status object.

constraints: Can only be executed on 4D Server; if called locally on a remote client or in 4D single-user, the command does nothing.
Returned Object has properties: success (boolean, True if the refresh succeeded), status (number, status code), statusText (text, status description), tips (text, suggestions to resolve an error).

overloads.semanticRole: Generates a data encryption key from a passphrase string and adds it to the 4D keychain.

discriminatedBy.rule: First parameter is Text: a passphrase from which the encryption key is generated.

overloads.semanticRole: Adds an already-generated data encryption key (e.g. produced by New data key), passed as an object with an encodedKey property, to the 4D keychain.

discriminatedBy.rule: First parameter is Object: a pre-built data key (with an encodedKey property), such as one returned by New data key.

constraints: The 4D keychain is a set of one or more data encryption keys loaded in memory; 4D automatically scans it whenever a key is needed to decrypt/encrypt a data file.
Returns False (not an error) if the same encryption key was already present in the 4D keychain.

overloads.semanticRole: Replace string replaces howMany occurrences of oldString in source with newString .

discriminatedBy.rule: Presence of the trailing literal '*' switches the comparison mode used to find oldString from linguistic (default) to character-code-based.

constraints: If newString is an empty string, each occurrence of oldString in source is deleted.
If oldString is an empty string, the unchanged source is returned.
By default (without *), comparisons are linguistic (accent/diacritic-insensitive, e.g. a=A, a=à, æ=ae) and ignore characters with code < 9.

Passing * as the last parameter switches to character-code-based comparison (case- and accent-sensitive), needed to match special delimiter characters (e.g. Char(1)) or to force case/accent sensitivity; this mode does not account for variant word spellings.

overloads.semanticRole: The Request command displays a request dialog box composed of a message, a text input area, an OK button, and a Cancel Button.

constraints: If message does not fit the display area (roughly 50 characters, varies by system/font), it may appear truncated.
Default button titles are "OK" and "Cancel" unless overridden by OKButtonTitle/CancelButtonTitle; buttons are resized to fit custom titles.
Sets the OK system variable to 1 if the user clicks OK (or presses Enter), or 0 if the user clicks Cancel.
Returns the entered text on OK, or an empty string on Cancel; convert with Num or Date if a numeric/date value is expected.
Must not be called from a form/object method's On Activate or On Deactivate event handler, since that causes an endless loop.
For gathering multiple pieces of information, prefer a custom form presented with DIALOG rather than chaining several Request dialogs.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns True if the right mouse button was clicked (within an On Clicked event), otherwise False.

constraints: Should only be used within the On Clicked form event; verify in Design mode that this event is enabled on the form and/or the specific object.

overloads.semanticRole: Round returns number rounded to the number of decimal places specified by places .

constraints: Positive places rounds to that many decimal places; negative places rounds to the left of the decimal point.
If the digit following the rounding position is 5-9, Round rounds away from zero (toward +infinity for positive numbers, -infinity for negative numbers); if 0-4, Round rounds toward zero.

overloads.semanticRole: The SAVE LIST command saves the list whose reference number you pass in list , within the Design environment List Editor, under the name you pass in listName .

constraints: If a list with the given listName already exists in the Design environment List Editor, its contents are replaced.
Cannot be used in a structure loaded read-only, such as a .4dz project (including remote projects) or a component.

overloads.semanticRole: SAVE RECORD saves the current record of aTable in the current process.

constraints: If there is no current record for aTable, the command is ignored.
If no field was actually modified in the record, the command does nothing (no trigger call).
Must not be called during the On Validate event of a form that has already been accepted, or the record will be saved twice.
Saving a record with edited Object field(s) usually requires explicitly notifying 4D before calling this command (see Saving Object fields).

overloads.semanticRole: SAVE RELATED ONE saves the record related to aField .

constraints: Will not save a locked record: if the record related to aField is locked, the command is silently ignored (no error returned).

overloads.semanticRole: SAVE SET saves set to document , a document on disk.

constraints: If document is an empty string, a Create File dialog box lets the user name the document.
Sets the OK system variable to 0 if the user cancels the save dialog or an error occurs, otherwise 1.
A set is a snapshot of a selection at save time and does not save field values; it can become inaccurate if underlying records are modified/deleted or the defining criteria changes.

overloads.semanticRole: The SAVE VARIABLES command saves one or more variables in the document whose name you pass in document .

constraints: Each variable must be of type String, Text, Real, Integer, Long Integer, Date, Time, Boolean, or Picture; array variables are not supported (use the BLOB commands instead).
If document is an empty string, a Save File dialog box lets the user choose the document; the Document system variable is set to the created document's name.
Sets the OK system variable to 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
Uses an internal data format: saved documents can only be reloaded with LOAD VARIABLES, not RECEIVE PACKET or RECEIVE VARIABLE.

overloads.semanticRole: Writes a document-level XML processing instruction (e.g. an xml-stylesheet declaration) into the SAX document referenced by document.

constraints: Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX XML document-write lifecycle: obtain a document reference (e.g. via Create document/OPEN DOCUMENT) -> optionally SAX SET XML DECLARATION and document-level SAX ADD XML DOCTYPE/PROCESSING INSTRUCTION/COMMENT calls -> SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT / SAX ADD XML ELEMENT VALUE / SAX ADD XML CDATA for element content (nested opens require matching SAX CLOSE XML ELEMENT) -> CLOSE DOCUMENT.

overloads.semanticRole: Writes a CDATA section (automatically framed by <![CDATA[ ... ]]>) containing text or BLOB data inside the currently open element of the SAX document referenced by document.

constraints: An XML element must already be open (via SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT) for this command to succeed; otherwise an error is generated.
To encode data's contents, pass a BLOB (encoded via BASE64 ENCODE); the data type (Blob vs Text) selects how the CDATA payload is produced.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX XML document-write lifecycle: obtain a document reference (e.g. via Create document/OPEN DOCUMENT) -> optionally SAX SET XML DECLARATION and document-level SAX ADD XML DOCTYPE/PROCESSING INSTRUCTION/COMMENT calls -> SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT / SAX ADD XML ELEMENT VALUE / SAX ADD XML CDATA for element content (nested opens require matching SAX CLOSE XML ELEMENT) -> CLOSE DOCUMENT.

overloads.semanticRole: Writes an XML comment (unparsed text) into the SAX document referenced by document.

constraints: Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX XML document-write lifecycle: obtain a document reference (e.g. via Create document/OPEN DOCUMENT) -> optionally SAX SET XML DECLARATION and document-level SAX ADD XML DOCTYPE/PROCESSING INSTRUCTION/COMMENT calls -> SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT / SAX ADD XML ELEMENT VALUE / SAX ADD XML CDATA for element content (nested opens require matching SAX CLOSE XML ELEMENT) -> CLOSE DOCUMENT.

overloads.semanticRole: Writes a DocType statement (identifying the DTD used) into the SAX document referenced by document.

constraints: Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX XML document-write lifecycle: obtain a document reference (e.g. via Create document/OPEN DOCUMENT) -> optionally SAX SET XML DECLARATION and document-level SAX ADD XML DOCTYPE/PROCESSING INSTRUCTION/COMMENT calls -> SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT / SAX ADD XML ELEMENT VALUE / SAX ADD XML CDATA for element content (nested opens require matching SAX CLOSE XML ELEMENT) -> CLOSE DOCUMENT.

overloads.semanticRole: In the XML document referenced by document , the SAX ADD XML ELEMENT VALUE command adds data directly without converting them.

constraints: An element must already be open (via SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT) before this command is called, otherwise an error is generated.
If data evaluates to undefined, 4D substitutes an empty string.

By default, special characters (< > ” ’...) in data are encoded, unless encoding was disabled for the current process via XML SET OPTIONS (XML string encoding = XML raw data); passing the optional * parameter forces encoding of special characters even when that raw-data mode is active.
To insert pre-encoded binary content, base64-encode it yourself with BASE64 ENCODE and pass the resulting BLOB in data.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX write document lifecycle: SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT (or the ARRAYS variant) opens an element -> SAX ADD XML ELEMENT VALUE adds its content while it remains open -> SAX CLOSE XML ELEMENT closes the most recently opened element (or the document itself is closed, which auto-closes any still-open elements).

overloads.semanticRole: The SAX CLOSE XML ELEMENT command writes the statements necessary for closing the last element opened using the SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT command in the XML document referenced by document .

constraints: Closes only the most recently opened (innermost) unclosed element, i.e. matches SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT calls in stack (LIFO) order.
Use of this command is optional: 4D automatically adds the necessary end tags for any still-open elements when the XML document itself is closed.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX write document lifecycle: SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT (or the ARRAYS variant) opens an element -> SAX ADD XML ELEMENT VALUE adds its content while it remains open -> SAX CLOSE XML ELEMENT closes the most recently opened element (or the document itself is closed, which auto-closes any still-open elements).

overloads.semanticRole: Retrieves the CDATA value of the XML element currently being parsed, into the value output parameter.

constraints: Must be called while handling the XML CDATA SAX event returned by SAX Get XML node.
Pass a Text-typed value variable (not Blob) to retrieve data larger than 32 KB (requires Unicode mode).
Since 4D v12, base64-encoded CDATA content is automatically decoded; it is not necessary to call BASE64 DECODE.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX event-driven read loop: call SAX Get XML node repeatedly to advance through the parser events for the document; dispatch on the returned event code to the matching accessor -- SAX GET XML ELEMENT for Start/End Element, SAX GET XML ELEMENT VALUE for XML DATA, SAX GET XML CDATA for XML CDATA, SAX GET XML COMMENT for XML Comment, SAX GET XML ENTITY for XML Entity, SAX GET XML PROCESSING INSTRUCTION for XML Processing Instruction, and SAX GET XML DOCUMENT VALUES for XML Start Document.

overloads.semanticRole: Retrieves the text of the XML comment currently being parsed, into the comment output parameter.

constraints: Must be called while handling the XML Comment SAX event returned by SAX Get XML node.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX event-driven read loop: call SAX Get XML node repeatedly to advance through the parser events for the document; dispatch on the returned event code to the matching accessor -- SAX GET XML ELEMENT for Start/End Element, SAX GET XML ELEMENT VALUE for XML DATA, SAX GET XML CDATA for XML CDATA, SAX GET XML COMMENT for XML Comment, SAX GET XML ENTITY for XML Entity, SAX GET XML PROCESSING INSTRUCTION for XML Processing Instruction, and SAX GET XML DOCUMENT VALUES for XML Start Document.

overloads.semanticRole: Retrieves the character-set encoding, XML version, and standalone flag declared in the document's XML header, into the three output parameters.

constraints: Must be called while handling the XML Start Document SAX event returned by SAX Get XML node.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX event-driven read loop: call SAX Get XML node repeatedly to advance through the parser events for the document; dispatch on the returned event code to the matching accessor -- SAX GET XML ELEMENT for Start/End Element, SAX GET XML ELEMENT VALUE for XML DATA, SAX GET XML CDATA for XML CDATA, SAX GET XML COMMENT for XML Comment, SAX GET XML ENTITY for XML Entity, SAX GET XML PROCESSING INSTRUCTION for XML Processing Instruction, and SAX GET XML DOCUMENT VALUES for XML Start Document.

overloads.semanticRole: Retrieves the value (Text or BLOB) of the XML element currently being parsed, into the value output parameter.

constraints: Must be called while handling the XML DATA SAX event returned by SAX Get XML node.
Pass a Text or BLOB type variable or field in value; if a BLOB is passed, the command automatically attempts to decode it from base64.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX event-driven read loop: call SAX Get XML node repeatedly to advance through the parser events for the document; dispatch on the returned event code to the matching accessor -- SAX GET XML ELEMENT for Start/End Element, SAX GET XML ELEMENT VALUE for XML DATA, SAX GET XML CDATA for XML CDATA, SAX GET XML COMMENT for XML Comment, SAX GET XML ENTITY for XML Entity, SAX GET XML PROCESSING INSTRUCTION for XML Processing Instruction, and SAX GET XML DOCUMENT VALUES for XML Start Document.

overloads.semanticRole: Retrieves the name, namespace prefix, and attribute name/value arrays of the element currently being parsed, into the four output parameters.

constraints: Must be called while handling the XML Start Element or XML End Element SAX event returned by SAX Get XML node.
For the XML End Element event, the attrNames/attrValues attribute parameters are not populated.
prefix is returned as an empty string if no namespace is linked to the element.
attrNames and attrValues are created and sized automatically by the command as needed.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX event-driven read loop: call SAX Get XML node repeatedly to advance through the parser events for the document; dispatch on the returned event code to the matching accessor -- SAX GET XML ELEMENT for Start/End Element, SAX GET XML ELEMENT VALUE for XML DATA, SAX GET XML CDATA for XML CDATA, SAX GET XML COMMENT for XML Comment, SAX GET XML ENTITY for XML Entity, SAX GET XML PROCESSING INSTRUCTION for XML Processing Instruction, and SAX GET XML DOCUMENT VALUES for XML Start Document.

overloads.semanticRole: Retrieves the name and value of the XML entity currently being parsed, into the two output parameters.

constraints: Must be called while handling the XML Entity SAX event returned by SAX Get XML node.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX event-driven read loop: call SAX Get XML node repeatedly to advance through the parser events for the document; dispatch on the returned event code to the matching accessor -- SAX GET XML ELEMENT for Start/End Element, SAX GET XML ELEMENT VALUE for XML DATA, SAX GET XML CDATA for XML CDATA, SAX GET XML COMMENT for XML Comment, SAX GET XML ENTITY for XML Entity, SAX GET XML PROCESSING INSTRUCTION for XML Processing Instruction, and SAX GET XML DOCUMENT VALUES for XML Start Document.

overloads.semanticRole: Retrieves the name and value of the XML processing instruction currently being parsed, into the two output parameters.

constraints: Must be called while handling the XML Processing Instruction SAX event returned by SAX Get XML node.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX event-driven read loop: call SAX Get XML node repeatedly to advance through the parser events for the document; dispatch on the returned event code to the matching accessor -- SAX GET XML ELEMENT for Start/End Element, SAX GET XML ELEMENT VALUE for XML DATA, SAX GET XML CDATA for XML CDATA, SAX GET XML COMMENT for XML Comment, SAX GET XML ENTITY for XML Entity, SAX GET XML PROCESSING INSTRUCTION for XML Processing Instruction, and SAX GET XML DOCUMENT VALUES for XML Start Document.

overloads.semanticRole: The SAX Get XML node command returns a long integer that indicates the type of SAX event returned while the XML document referenced in document is parsed.

constraints: The returned Integer is one of the 'XML' theme event constants: XML Start Document=1, XML Comment=2, XML Processing Instruction=3, XML Start Element=4, XML End Element=5, XML DATA=6, XML CDATA=7, XML Entity=8, XML End Document=9.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX event-driven read loop: call SAX Get XML node repeatedly to advance through the parser events for the document; dispatch on the returned event code to the matching accessor -- SAX GET XML ELEMENT for Start/End Element, SAX GET XML ELEMENT VALUE for XML DATA, SAX GET XML CDATA for XML CDATA, SAX GET XML COMMENT for XML Comment, SAX GET XML ENTITY for XML Entity, SAX GET XML PROCESSING INSTRUCTION for XML Processing Instruction, and SAX GET XML DOCUMENT VALUES for XML Start Document.

overloads.semanticRole: Adds a new element, optionally passing one or more attribute-name/attribute-value pairs as parallel arrays (attribNamesArray a Text array, attribValuesArray a typed Array of text/date/number/boolean/picture elements).

discriminatedBy.rule: Trailing repeat-group members are arrays (Text array / typed Array) -- the array-based syntax.

overloads.semanticRole: Documented as the '*'-suffixed variant of this command: adds a new element passing a single scalar attribName/attribValue Text pair, identical in effect to SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT's own pair syntax rather than to the array-based form.

discriminatedBy.rule: Trailing repeat-group members are scalar Text values, not arrays -- selects the non-array (single pair) syntax.

constraints: Identical to SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT except for array support; see that command for tag naming rules and element-closing behavior.
attribValuesArray accepts arrays of text, date, number, Boolean, or picture type; 4D performs the necessary conversions automatically, configurable via XML SET OPTIONS.
The attribNamesArray/attribValuesArray arrays must be created beforehand and operate as attribute/attribute-value pairs; as many pairs of arrays (and items per pair) as desired may be passed.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX write document lifecycle: SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT (or the ARRAYS variant) opens an element -> SAX ADD XML ELEMENT VALUE adds its content while it remains open -> SAX CLOSE XML ELEMENT closes the most recently opened element (or the document itself is closed, which auto-closes any still-open elements).

overloads.semanticRole: The SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT command adds a new element in the XML document referenced by document as well as, optionally, attributes and their values.

constraints: tag may only contain letters, numbers, and the characters '.', '-', '_', ':'; an invalid character generates an error.
The added element is left open (no end tag) until SAX CLOSE XML ELEMENT is called for it or the document is closed.
Any number of attribName/attribValue pairs may be passed as a trailing repeating group.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX write document lifecycle: SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT (or the ARRAYS variant) opens an element -> SAX ADD XML ELEMENT VALUE adds its content while it remains open -> SAX CLOSE XML ELEMENT closes the most recently opened element (or the document itself is closed, which auto-closes any still-open elements).

overloads.semanticRole: The SAX SET XML DECLARATION command initializes the XML document referenced in document using the specified encoding .

constraints: Must be called exactly once per document, before the first XML SET command in the document, otherwise an error is generated.
encoding defaults to UTF-8 if this command is never called, or falls back to UTF-8 if an unsupported character set is passed.
standalone defaults to False (document is not standalone) if omitted or if the command is not called.
indentation is obsolete and should not be used; document indentation is instead configured via the XML SET OPTIONS command.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): SAX write document lifecycle: SAX SET XML DECLARATION initializes document-level encoding/standalone settings once, before any other SAX write command -> SAX OPEN XML ELEMENT (or the ARRAYS variant) opens an element -> SAX ADD XML ELEMENT VALUE adds its content while it remains open -> SAX CLOSE XML ELEMENT closes the most recently opened element.

sentinelValues.meaning: Scan from the beginning of the index.
Scan from the end of the index.

overloads.semanticRole: SCAN INDEX returns a selection of number records from the table containing the aField field, scanning the index from the beginning (default, or explicit >) or from the end (<).

sentinelValues.meaning: Screen size -- the coordinates of the entire screen (default).
Screen work area -- the usable area, excluding the taskbar/menu bar/Dock.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the global screen coordinates (left, top, right, bottom) of the screen designated by screenID and screenArea.

constraints: If screenID is omitted, coordinates for the main screen are returned.
If an invalid screenID or screenArea value is given, zero is returned for all four coordinates.
If the taskbar/dock is set to auto-hide, the command always returns the entire screen size regardless of screenArea.

sentinelValues.meaning: Is color -- the monitor is set to display in color.
Is gray scale -- the monitor is set to display in gray scale (Macintosh only).

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the color depth (as an exponent of 2, i.e. number of colors = 2^depth) and color/gray-scale status of the monitor designated by screen.

constraints: If screen is omitted, the command returns information for the main screen.
The color value's gray-scale distinction (0) is only significant on the Macintosh platform.

overloads.semanticRole: Selects item(s) by position within the hierarchical list identified by its object name (list is a Text form-object name) -- selected via the leading '*' parameter.

discriminatedBy.rule: Passing the leading literal '*' selects this object-name form: list is a Text list object name rather than a numeric ListRef.

overloads.semanticRole: Selects item(s) by position within the hierarchical list identified by its reference number (list is an Integer ListRef) -- no leading '*' passed.

discriminatedBy.rule: Omitting the leading '*' selects this reference-number form: list is an Integer hierarchical list reference (ListRef).

constraints: The object-name form (leading '*') is required rather than optional if the same list has several representations (each with its own expanded/collapsed configuration) in the current form; if the list has only one representation, either syntax works.
If the @ wildcard is used in the list object name and several matching list objects exist on the form, the command applies only to the first matching object.
itemPos must be a value between 1 and the value returned by Count list items, expressed using the list's current expanded/collapsed state.

overloads.semanticRole: The SELECT LIST ITEMS BY REFERENCE command selects the item(s) whose item reference number is passed in itemRef and, optionally, in refArray , within the list whose reference number is passed in list .

constraints: If there is no item with the given itemRef, the command does nothing.
Passing 0 in itemRef designates the last item added to the list.
If an item is not currently visible (in a collapsed sublist), the command expands the sublist(s) needed to make it visible.
When refArray is passed, itemRef additionally sets the new current item of the list among the resulting multi-selection (it may or may not belong to the set of items in refArray).

overloads.semanticRole: Creates (or schedules the creation of) a new log file for the database using the given name or full pathname; passing an empty string prompts the user with a Save File dialog.

discriminatedBy.rule: Pass a Text file name/pathname to create a new log file.

overloads.semanticRole: Closes the current log file for the database when the sentinel '*' parameter is passed instead of a file name.

discriminatedBy.rule: Passing the literal '*' symbol instead of a file name closes the current log file.

constraints: If only a name (not a full pathname) is passed, the file is created in the database's 'Logs' folder next to the structure file.

The new log file is not generated immediately; it takes effect after the next backup (via BACKUP) or a call to New log file, and the pending change persists in the data file even if the database is closed in the meantime.
The OK system variable is set to 1 on success (file created, or closed when '*' is passed) and to 0 if the user cancels the Save File dialog or the log file could not be created.

overloads.semanticRole: Copies field values (or record numbers, if a Table is passed instead of a Field) from the selected-record range [start, end] of the current selection into one or more output arrays.

constraints: Requires 1 <= start <= end <= Records in selection([...]); the command still works if start = end (loads/returns data for that single selected record).
If end exceeds Records in selection([...]), returns values from the selected record at start through the last selected record.
If start > end, returns values only from the record at start.
If both start and end are inconsistent with the size of the selection, returns empty arrays.

Applies to the current selection of the table specified by the first data/table parameter's table; passing a Table instead of a Field for data loads record numbers into a Long Integer array instead of field values.
Values can be loaded from related fields via an automatic Many-to-One relation (including through several relation levels), including relations made automatic via SET AUTOMATIC RELATIONS.
Calling with only start and end (omitting every data/array pair) is a special syntax to launch, on a limited range, a previously deferred SELECTION TO ARRAY sequence.

members.name: selection
members.description: Field to use for retrieving data, or Table to use for retrieving record numbers

members.name: array
members.description: Array to receive field data or record numbers

params.description: If present, defer execution of this statement and stack it with other SELECTION TO ARRAY(...; *) lines until a final call without *.

overloads.semanticRole: Copies field values or record numbers from the current selection into one or more parallel arrays (in selection order); the optional trailing * defers execution so several such statements can be stacked and run together.

constraints: Each array is typed according to the source field's type; loading record numbers (via the [table];array syntax) produces a Longint array.
Values can be loaded through several levels of a Many-to-One relation (automatic, or manual made automatic via SET AUTOMATIC RELATIONS), reading the related field's values.

If an array was already explicitly typed (e.g. via ARRAY LONGINT) before the call, SELECTION TO ARRAY does not retype it even when loading from a Time field; it keeps loading data coerced into the array's existing type.

Passing the trailing * defers execution: 4D stores the statement in memory instead of running it immediately, letting several SELECTION TO ARRAY lines (like QUERY) stack up and execute together as one final call without *; the command can therefore also be called with no parameters at all to run the stacked lines.

overloads.semanticRole: The SEND MESSAGE TO REMOTE USER command sends a message to all remote users or to a specific remote user.

constraints: If userSession is omitted, the message is sent to all remote users.
Can only be executed on 4D Server; if the calling method runs locally on a remote client or 4D single-user, this command does nothing.

overloads.semanticRole: SEND PACKET sends a packet to a serial port or to a document.

constraints: If docRef is omitted, the packet is written to the serial port or document previously opened by SET CHANNEL; a serial port or document must have been opened via SET CHANNEL (or a document opened via one of the document commands) before calling this command.
Passing a BLOB in packet bypasses character-encoding conversion for text mode and ignores any character set defined by USE CHARACTER SET -- the BLOB is sent unmodified.

When writing to a document, the first call begins writing at the start of the document (unless it was opened with USE CHARACTER SET); each subsequent call appends to previously sent packets until the document is closed.

overloads.semanticRole: SEND RECORD sends the current record of aTable to the serial port or document opened by the SET CHANNEL command.

constraints: If aTable is omitted, the default table is used.
If no current record exists in the table, the command has no effect.
Requires a serial port or document previously opened via SET CHANNEL; cannot be used with a document opened via Open document, Create document, or Append document.

The record is sent in a special internal format readable only by RECEIVE RECORD; source and destination table structures must be compatible or 4D converts values per the destination table definitions.
Beginning with 4D v11, this command no longer supports subtables.

overloads.semanticRole: SEND VARIABLE sends variable to the document or serial port previously opened by SET CHANNEL .

constraints: Requires a serial port or document previously opened via SET CHANNEL; cannot be used with a document opened via Open document, Create document, or Append document.
Sends the complete variable, including its type and value, in a special internal format readable only by RECEIVE VARIABLE.
Does not support array variables; use the BLOB Commands to send/receive arrays over a document or serial port.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET ABOUT command changes the About 4D menu command in the Help menu (Windows) or in the Application menu (macOS) menu to itemText .

constraints: method is called when the user selects the About 4D menu command after this call, in both Design and Application mode.
On Windows, this command modifies the "About 4D" line in the Help menu created by SET HELP MENU.
A new process is created when this command is run on a server machine.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET ALLOWED METHODS command designates the project methods that can be entered via the application.

constraints: If this command is never called, no method is enterable and using an unauthorized method in an expression causes an error.

Allowed methods affect the formula editor, the label editor's Apply menu (if shared with the component), ST INSERT EXPRESSION-inserted expressions in styled text/4D Write Pro documents, and (as a fallback only, when VP SET ALLOWED METHODS has never been called in the session) 4D View Pro formulas.

sentinelValues.meaning: The application uses the Default Light Theme.
The application uses the Default Dark Theme.
The application inherits the scheme from the higher-priority level (e.g. Settings).

overloads.semanticRole: Defines the color scheme ('light', 'dark', or 'inherited') to use at the application level for the current session.

constraints: Has no effect on forms that already declare their own color scheme; a form-level scheme takes priority over the application-level scheme.
Does nothing on Windows with the Classic theme, where only "light" is available.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET ASSERT ENABLED command can be used to disable or re-enable any assertions inserted into the 4D code of the application.

constraints: By default, assertions are enabled in both interpreted and compiled mode.
By default this command affects all processes of the application (existing or created subsequently); pass the optional * parameter to restrict the effect to the current process only.
When assertions are disabled, expressions passed to ASSERT commands are no longer evaluated at all -- the calling lines have no effect on behavior or performance.

overloads.semanticRole: SET AUTOMATIC RELATIONS temporarily changes all the manual relations into automatic relations for the entire database in the current process.

constraints: Change is temporary (applies only for the current process) and persists until a subsequent call to SET AUTOMATIC RELATIONS, not permanently to the Design-environment relation settings.
one controls all manual Many-to-One relations for the entire database; many controls all manual One-to-Many relations, following the same True=automatic / False=revert-to-manual semantics as one.
Relations already set as automatic in the Design environment are not affected by this command.

Passing True 'locks' automatic mode for all manual relations during the session: subsequent calls to SET FIELD RELATION during the same session are ignored, regardless of whether they occur before or after this call.

overloads.semanticRole: SET BLOB SIZE resizes the BLOB blob according to the value passed in size .

constraints: filler accepts a value in the 0..255 range (an ASCII/byte code) used to initialize newly allocated bytes when the BLOB grows.
Since this command mutates the blob passed as a parameter, it does not support blob objects (4D.Blob type) -- only classic BLOB fields/variables.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET BLOBS CACHE PRIORITY command sets a specific priority to the "blobs" data related to aTable in cache for all processes in the current session.

constraints: Only works in local mode (4D Server and 4D single-user); cannot be used in 4D remote mode.
Should be called in the On Startup or On Server Startup database method to affect the whole session.
Applies to BLOB, text, picture, and object data fields of aTable, and only when they are stored in the data file (not externally).

overloads.semanticRole: The SET CACHE SIZE command sets the database cache size dynamically and, optionally, sets the mininum byte size at which to start to free memory.This command only works in local mode (4D Server and 4D); it cannot be used

constraints: Only works in local mode (4D Server and 4D single-user); cannot be used in 4D remote mode.
The new size is applied dynamically when the command executes.
If minFreeSize is omitted, 4D unloads at least 10% of the cache when space is needed.

overloads.semanticRole: Opens a serial port for communication, optionally passing port settings.

discriminatedBy.rule: First overload: port is a serial port number, opening/configuring that port.

sentinelValues.meaning: closes the currently opened serial port or document

overloads.semanticRole: Performs a document-oriented channel operation (e.g. open/close) on the named document.

discriminatedBy.rule: Second overload: operation is a document-operation code (e.g. 11 closes the current channel), with document naming the target document.

constraints: Only one serial port or one document can be open at a time via this command.
To close a previously opened channel, call SET CHANNEL(11).

sentinelValues.meaning: use the current printer defined in the system
use the generic PDF driver, regardless of platform

overloads.semanticRole: The SET CURSOR command changes the mouse cursor to the system cursor whose ID number you pass in cursor .

constraints: Must be called in the context of the On Mouse Move form event.
Calling with no argument (cursor omitted) restores the standard mouse cursor.

params.description: By default (omitted), the command applies to all open databases and components, for all processes. If passed, the command applies only to the database that called it (useful to set the language of a component separately from the host database).

constraints: languageCode uses the standard specified by RFC 3066, ISO 639, and ISO 3166 (e.g. "fr", "es", "en-us").
Does not affect forms already loaded; only elements displayed after the call take the new language into account.

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table to which the parameter applies. Only meaningful for table-scoped selectors (e.g. Query By Formula On Server); ignored/omittable for global selectors.

params.name: value
params.description: New value for the selected parameter; accepted shape depends entirely on selector -- see discriminatedBy. Confirmed missing from the original draft by the LSP cross-check (tool4d rejected a selector-only call site with a parameter-count/type mismatch) and against the real doc syntax examples (e.g. "SET DATABASE PARAMETER(4D Server Timeout;-60*3)", "SET DATABASE PARAMETER(Dates inside objects;0)"), which always pass two arguments (three when aTable is also given).

overloads.semanticRole: The SET DATABASE PARAMETER command allows you to modify various internal parameters of the 4D database.

discriminatedBy.rule: value's accepted range/type is selected by which DatabaseParameterSelector constant is passed; some selectors expect a sub-enum value (see that selector's description), others a plain Real/Integer or Text setting.

constraints: If aTable is omitted, the command applies to the default table.

selector must be one of the DatabaseParameterSelector enum constants; the meaning, scope, and valid values of the value parameter depend entirely on which selector constant is passed (several selectors -- Direct2D status, Diagnostic log level, Min TLS version, Times inside objects, Dates inside objects -- draw value from their own dedicated sub-enum; see each DatabaseParameterSelector entry's description).

overloads.semanticRole: The SET DEFAULT CENTURY command specifies the default century and the pivot year used by 4D when you enter a date with only two digits for the year.

constraints: century is the century value minus one (e.g. pass 20 to switch to the 21st century).
Default (if never called): century 20 (20th century) with pivotYear 30.
pivotYear rule: if the two-digit year is >= pivotYear, 4D uses the current default century; if it is < pivotYear, 4D uses the next century.

overloads.semanticRole: This command operates only on a document currently open whose document reference number you pass in docRef .sets the position you pass in offset where the next read ( RECEIVE PACKET ) or write ( SEND PACKET ) will occur.

jointConstraints.rule: The sign/range of valid offset values depends on which anchor is chosen (e.g. a negative offset is meaningful when anchored to the end or current position, but not when anchored to the beginning).

constraints: Operates only on a document that is currently open (docRef from a prior Open document/Create document call).
If anchor is omitted, offset is relative to the beginning of the document.
anchor values: 1 = relative to the beginning of the file, 2 = relative to the end of the file, 3 = relative to the current position.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET DOCUMENT PROPERTIES command changes the information about the document whose name or pathname you pass in document .
The SET DOCUMENT SIZE command sets the size of a document to the number of bytes you pass in size .

constraints: Operates only on a document that is currently open, identified by docRef.
On macOS, changes the size of the document's data fork.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET DRAG ICON command associates the icon picture with the cursor during drag and drop operations that are managed by programming.

constraints: Must be called in the context of the On Begin Drag Over form event.
icon's maximum size is 256x256 pixels; larger pictures are automatically resized.
If horOffset/vertOffset are omitted, the cursor is placed at the center of the icon.
horOffset: positive = offset towards the left, negative = offset towards the right.
vertOffset: positive = offset upwards, negative = offset downwards.

sentinelValues.meaning: reset the variable to its default value

constraints: Intended for use together with LAUNCH EXTERNAL PROCESS.
Windows and macOS only.

params.name: aField
params.description: Field for which to set the storage location. Must be an actual field reference (e.g. [Table]FieldName) of type Text, BLOB, or Picture -- the doc's own Type column names the field's data type, not the shape of a value that can be passed here; a same-typed variable or literal is rejected by the compiler ("The function expects a field not a variable or constant.").

sentinelValues.meaning: use the structure definition
use the default folder

constraints: The setting only takes effect when the current record is saved to disk; if the record is canceled, the command has no effect.
path can be a custom pathname (relative to the data file, or absolute, in system syntax) or one of the documented numeric constants.

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the automatic/manual status of all Many-to-One/One-to-Many relations starting from every Many field of manyTable.

discriminatedBy.rule: First overload: first parameter is a Table -- applies to all relations starting from that table's Many fields.

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the automatic/manual status of the single Many-to-One/One-to-Many relation starting from the specific manyField.

discriminatedBy.rule: Second overload: first parameter is a Field -- applies only to the relation starting from that specific Many field.

constraints: Sets automatic/manual relation status for the current process only, independent of the relation's design-time status.
If there is no relation starting from the given field/table, syntax error 16 is generated and OK is set to 0.
one/many values use the "Relations" theme constants: 0 = do not modify, 1 = use the structure configuration, 2 = manual, (and further documented values for automatic).

overloads.semanticRole: SET FIELD TITLES lets you mask, rename, and reorder the fields of the table passed in aTable when they appear in standard 4D dialog boxes, such as the Query editor, within the Application environment (i.e.

constraints: fieldTitles and fieldNumbers arrays must be synchronized element-by-element (same index = same field).
Fields whose name/title is omitted from fieldTitles are not shown in standard dialog boxes.
Fields appear in the order given by fieldTitles/fieldNumbers.
The trailing '*' makes the custom names apply in the formula editor as well.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET FIELD VALUE NULL command assigns the NULL value to the field designated by the aField parameter.

constraints: The Null value can be disallowed for a given field at the Structure editor level, in which case this command cannot be used on it.
For an object field, this command erases the field's contents.

params.description: If omitted, the pasteboard's contents are replaced by file's pathname. If passed, file's pathname is added to the pasteboard's existing stack of pathnames.

constraints: If file is a simple name (no pathname), the file must be located next to the database structure file.
The pasteboard cannot be modified (read-only) during the On Drag Over form event.
If non-pathname data was already in the pasteboard, it is erased regardless of whether '*' is passed.

sentinelValues.meaning: the 4D user account will no longer belong to any group
resets the account's group memberships to those stored on disk

constraints: Can only be called from 4D remote or 4D single-user applications; not allowed on 4D Server.
Scope is the current session only; a later CHANGE CURRENT USER call resets memberships defined by this command.
Group names that do not exist are silently ignored.
A license used via a "serialized" group membership stays attached to the user account until the session ends, even if that membership is later canceled by this command.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET HELP MENU command allows you to replace the default 4D Help menu with the menuCol collection of menu items in the application mode.

constraints: The "Help" label itself is managed by the system and cannot be customized.
Customized Help menus do not support submenus, checkmarks, styles, or icons.
Items display in the same order as the collection; a null entry or empty object inserts a separator line.

menuCol's menu-object properties (title, method, worker, action, shortcutKey, shortcutShift, shortcutAlt) follow the same object shape as other menu-building commands (e.g. SET MENU ITEMS / APPEND MENU ITEM); if 'method' is passed, 'action' is ignored, and vice versa.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET INDEX CACHE PRIORITY command sets a specific priority to the index(es) related to the aField in cache for all processes in the current session.

constraints: Only works in local mode (4D Server and 4D single-user); cannot be used in 4D remote mode.
Should be called in the On Startup or On Server Startup database method.
Applies to all indexes related to aField, including keyword indexes; composite index priorities cannot be customized separately.

sentinelValues.meaning: create an index of the default type for the field
delete all standard indexes associated with the field
create a Keywords index (Text/Alpha fields only)
create an index using the 4D-chosen default index type
create a Standard B-Tree index
create a Cluster B-Tree index

params.description: If passed, the indexing operation is performed asynchronously.

constraints: index's declared type (Boolean vs Integer) selects the operation: Boolean creates/deletes the field's default-type index; Integer creates an index of the specified type.
Passing False for index deletes all standard (non-composite, non-keyword) indexes associated with the field.
If the index already exists (True case) or does not exist (False case), the call has no effect.

params.description: If present, 'list' below is an object name (string) referring to a form representation of the list; if omitted, 'list' is a hierarchical list reference number (ListRef).

the current item of the list (requires the object-name syntax, since each form representation can have its own current item)
reapply the default font of the hierarchical list

params.name: asObjectName
params.description: If present, 'list' below is an object name (string) referring to a form representation of the list; if omitted, 'list' is a hierarchical list reference number (ListRef).

the current item of the list (requires the object-name syntax, since each form representation can have its own current item)

interactionNotes.note: The literal symbol '*' means two unrelated things depending on position: leading = 'list is a name, not a ref number'; in itemRef's slot = 'operate on the current item'. Using the itemRef '*' sentinel requires the object-name syntax (leading '*' passed).

constraints: Unlike SET LIST ITEM PROPERTIES (which only accepts static picture references), this command's icon parameter also accepts a Pointer, so dynamic pictures can be used.

params.name: asObjectName
params.description: If present, 'list' below is an object name (string) referring to a form representation of the list; if omitted, 'list' is a hierarchical list reference number (ListRef).

params.name: list

sentinelValues.meaning: the last item appended to the list (via APPEND TO LIST)
the current item of the list (requires the object-name syntax, since each form representation can have its own current item)

params.name: selector
params.description: One of the documented "Hierarchical Lists" theme constants (e.g. Additional text), or a custom property name.

params.name: value
params.description: Value of the parameter; its concrete type depends on which selector is passed.

interactionNotes.note: The literal symbol '*' means two unrelated things depending on position: leading = 'list is a name, not a ref number'; in itemRef's slot = 'operate on the current item'. Using the itemRef '*' sentinel requires the object-name syntax (leading '*' passed).

constraints: value's concrete type (Text/Boolean/Real) may still depend on selector when a custom (non-enum) property name is passed; for the two documented HierarchicalListItemSelector constants (Additional text, Associated standard action name), value is Text.
