the current item of the list (requires the object-name syntax, since each form representation can have its own current item)
detach the current sublist, if any (no sublist)
no change to the current sublist attachment

interactionNotes.note: The literal symbol '*' means two unrelated things depending on position: leading = 'list is a name, not a ref number'; in itemRef's slot = 'operate on the current item'. Using the itemRef '*' sentinel requires the object-name syntax (leading '*' passed).

sentinelValues.meaning: replace the full method text
replace only the highlighted (selected) method text

constraints: If no text is currently selected in the method, textParam is simply inserted at the insertion point (selector has no effect).

params.name: menuBar
params.description: Number of the menu bar, or its name (Text), or a 16-character MenuRef menu ID (Text).

params.name: process
params.description: Process reference number whose menu bar is to be changed; if omitted, applies to the current process.
If passed, preserves the current enabled/disabled state of menu commands instead of reinitializing the menu bar.

interactionNotes.note: When menuBar is a MenuRef, both process and '*' are ignored.

constraints: A menu bar name may contain up to 31 characters and must be unique.
If menuBar is a MenuRef (menu ID), the process parameter serves no purpose and is ignored.
If menuBar is a MenuRef, the trailing '*' parameter serves no purpose and is ignored.

params.name: menu
params.description: Menu number, or a MenuRef menu ID (Text).

sentinelValues.meaning: the last item added to the menu

params.name: iconRef
params.description: Picture file reference (Text, "path:..." recommended, "file:..." deprecated), or a library picture name/number (binary databases only).

constraints: If menu is a MenuRef, the command applies to all instances of the menu in all processes, and process is ignored if passed.
If menu is a menu number, the command applies only to the menu in the current process's main menu bar unless process names another process.
For a picture file reference, the recommended "path:" syntax (e.g. "path:/RESOURCES/icon.png") should be used; the "file:" syntax is deprecated.
Library picture references (name or number) only work with binary databases; the Picture library is deprecated and unsupported in 4D project databases.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET MENU ITEM MARK command changes the check mark of the menu item whose menu number or reference is passed in menu and whose item number is passed in menuItem to the first character of the string passed in mark .

constraints: Only the first character of mark is used as the check mark; passing an empty string removes any existing mark from the menu item.
Passing -1 in menuItem designates the last item added to menu.
If menu is a MenuRef, the process parameter serves no purpose and is ignored.

On Macintosh, the first character of mark becomes the raw mark glyph (typically Char(18), the check mark character); on Windows, any non-empty mark assigns the standard check mark regardless of which character is passed.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET MENU ITEM METHOD command modifies the 4D project method associated with the menu item designated by the menu and menuItem parameters.

constraints: Passing -1 in menuItem designates the last item added to menu.

If menu is a MenuRef, the command applies to all instances of the menu across all processes and the process parameter is ignored; if menu is a menu number, it applies to the main menu bar of the current process (or of process, if given).
If the menu item is the title of a hierarchical sub-menu, methodName is not called when the item is selected.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET MENU ITEM PARAMETER command associates a custom character string with a menu item designated by the menu and menuItem parameters.

constraints: param is mainly intended to be read back by the Dynamic pop up menu command as a custom string associated with the menu item; it has no other built-in effect.
Passing -1 in menuItem designates the last item added to menu.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET MENU ITEM PROPERTY command sets the value of the property for the menu item designated by the menu and menuItem parameters.

constraints: property accepts either a standard property name (a constant from the 'Menu Item Properties' theme, e.g. 4D_access_group, 4D_standard_action, 4D_execute_without_validating, 4D_start_new_process) or any custom string that does not begin with '4D_'; the accepted type/shape of value depends on which property is passed.

For the 'Associated standard action' standard property, value is a standard action name (Text) chosen from the Standard Action theme/Standard actions list; pre-4D v16 R3 code passing the deprecated Value for Associated Standard Action constants (Longint) is still supported for compatibility.
A custom property's value (Text, Longint, or Boolean) is stored with the menu item and can be retrieved with GET MENU ITEM PROPERTY.

If menu is a MenuRef, the command applies to all instances of the menu across all processes and process is ignored; if menu is a menu number, it applies to the main menu bar of the current process (or of process, if given).
Passing -1 in menuItem designates the last item added to menu.
If the menu item is the title of a hierarchical sub-menu, an associated standard action is not called when the item is selected.

overloads.semanticRole: Assigns a keyboard shortcut to a menu item using a letter/string key (current syntax), optionally combined with extra modifier keys.

discriminatedBy.rule: itemKey is Text: a shortcut letter/string, or an F-key spec like "[F4]".

params.name: menu
params.description: Menu number or Menu reference

params.name: menuItem
params.description: Menu item number or -1 for last item added

params.name: itemKey
params.description: Character code of keyboard shortcut (former syntax)

sentinelValues.meaning: Removes any existing shortcut from the menu item.

params.name: process
params.description: Process reference number

overloads.semanticRole: Compatibility (former syntax): assigns a keyboard shortcut to a menu item using a raw character code; the shortcut always uses the default Ctrl/Cmd modifier and this form has no way to add extra modifiers.

discriminatedBy.rule: itemKey is Integer: a character code (former syntax); this overload has no modifiers parameter.

constraints: In the primary (Text itemKey) form, the shortcut automatically includes the Ctrl (Windows)/Cmd (macOS) modifier unless itemKey is an F-key spec such as "[F4]", in which case no modifier is added by default; modifiers lets you add extra modifiers (Shift/Option/Command) on top, and 0 means no extra modifiers.
If menu is a MenuRef (16-character alphanumeric), the process parameter serves no purpose and is ignored.
Passing -1 in menuItem designates the last item added to menu.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET MENU ITEM STYLE command changes the font style of the menu item whose menu number or reference is passed in menu and whose item number is passed in menuItem according to the font style passed in itemStyle .

constraints: itemStyle is a sum/combination of Font Styles constants: Plain=0, Bold=1, Italic=2, Underline=4.
The Underline style is not supported on Windows when the Fluent UI theme is enabled; it is silently ignored in that rendering context.
If menu is a MenuRef, the process parameter serves no purpose and is ignored.
Passing -1 in menuItem designates the last item added to menu.

params.name: menu
params.description: Menu number, or a MenuRef menu ID (Text).

sentinelValues.meaning: the last item added to the menu

params.description: If omitted, metacharacters in itemText (e.g. '(', ';', '!', '<B') are interpreted as formatting/instruction characters (as in APPEND MENU ITEM). If passed, those characters are treated as standard literal characters.

constraints: If a MenuRef is passed in menu, the process parameter serves no purpose and is ignored.
If the process parameter is omitted, the command applies to the menu bar of the current process.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET PICTURE FILE NAME command sets or changes the default file name for the picture passed as parameter.

constraints: The default file name set here is used when the picture is subsequently exported to a disk file; the name is copied along with the picture's contents if the field/variable's value is copied elsewhere.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET PICTURE METADATA command lets you set or modify the contents of the metadata (or meta-tags) found in the picture (4D picture field or variable), when they are modifiable.

constraints: metaName selects how metaContents is interpreted: a tag-path constant from the Picture Metadata Names theme (metaContents is then the value to set, of the Text/Longint/Real/Date/Time type matching that tag, an array if the tag holds multiple values, or an XML/XMP-formatted string), a block name ("TIFF", "EXIF", "GPS" or "IPTC"), or an empty string (metaContents is then the XML DOM reference of the element containing the metadata to set; an empty metaName modifies all metadata). If metaName is undefined, an empty string is used.
Passing an empty string ("") in metaContents for a tag-path metaName erases the existing metadata designated by that tag.
Only certain picture formats (notably JPEG and TIFF) support metadata; formats such as GIF or BMP do not, and converting a picture with metadata to a non-supporting format loses that metadata.
Some metadata are read-only and cannot be modified by this command, e.g. TIFF XResolution/YResolution, EXIF Color Space, EXIF Pixel X/Y Dimension.
On Windows, a failed metadata write sets the OK system variable to 0; on macOS, metadata write errors are not detected and OK is not modified.
Repeated (metaName;metaContents) pairs set several metadata items in one call.

overloads.semanticRole: warning This command cannot be used in projects because the Picture library is only available in binary databases.

constraints: This command cannot be used in projects because the Picture Library is only available in binary (classic) databases.
If a Picture Library graphic with reference picRef already exists, its contents are replaced and it is renamed according to picture/picName; otherwise a new picture is added to the Picture Library.
If picture is empty, or picRef is negative or zero, the command does nothing.
Cannot be used from within a method executed on the 4D Server machine (stored procedure or trigger); calling it there is silently ignored.

overloads.semanticRole: SET PICTURE TO PASTEBOARD clears the pasteboard and puts a copy of the picture passed in picture into it.

constraints: Clears the pasteboard before placing picture; the picture is stored in its native format (JPEG, TIFF, PNG, etc.) and can be retrieved with GET PICTURE FROM PASTEBOARD or GET PASTEBOARD DATA (e.g. "com.4d.private.picture.gif").

overloads.semanticRole: The SET PLUGIN ACCESS command sets, by programming, the user group allowed to use each “serialized” plug-in that is installed in the database.

constraints: Only one group at a time can be authorized to use a given plug-in license; assigning a new group revokes access from whichever group previously held it.
Plug-in licenses already checked out by members of group remain attached to those 4D user accounts for the rest of the session even if their group membership or the group's plug-in access changes.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET PRINT MARKER command enables the definition of the marker position during printing.

interactionNotes.note: Without the trailing '*', markNum cannot be moved past the position of the marker immediately preceding or following it. With '*', markNum can be moved beyond the initial position of the markers that follow it, and every marker below markNum (along with any objects in the areas below it) is shifted the same distance and direction as markNum.

constraints: Only valid during the On Header form event (in the context of PRINT SELECTION/PRINT RECORD) or the On Printing Detail form event (in the context of Print form); it has no visible effect on screen and the form itself is not modified/saved.
Only repositions an existing marker; it does not add new markers, and if markNum does not designate a marker that exists in the form, the command does nothing.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET PRINT OPTION command is used to modify, by programming, the value of a print option.

constraints: The number and meaning of value1/value2 depend on option: Paper option (1) — value1 alone is the paper name, or value1/value2 together are the paper width/height in points; Orientation option (2) — value1 only, 1=Portrait/2=Landscape, and can be changed mid print-job; Scale option (3) — value1 only, a percentage (an invalid value is reset to 100% at print time); Number of copies option (4) — value1 only; Paper source option (5, Windows only) — value1 only, a tray index from PRINT OPTION VALUES; Destination option (9) — value1 is 1=Printer/2=File(PS on Mac)/3=PDF file/5=Screen(macOS), and value2 is the destination pathname when value1 isn't 1 or 5; Double sided option (11) — value1 is 0=Single-sided/1=Double-sided, and value2 (if value1=1) is 0=Left binding/1=Top binding; Spooler document name option (12) — value1 only, a document name (empty string restores the standard name); Page range option (15) — value1=first page (default 1), value2=last page (default -1=end of document); Legacy printing layer option (16, Windows only) — value1 only, 1=GDI legacy layer/0=D2D layer; Print preview option (18, Windows only) — value1 sets the preview format, value2 is read-only via GET PRINT OPTION.

Each option set via this command applies to the current 4D printing settings until another command that modifies print parameters (e.g. PRINT SETTINGS, or PRINT SELECTION/PRINT RECORD/PAGE BREAK without the '>' parameter) is called.

If a print job has been opened (e.g. with OPEN PRINTING JOB), an option set for that job cannot be modified until the job terminates, except for the Orientation option which remains modifiable mid-job.

overloads.semanticRole: SET PRINT PREVIEW allows you to programmatically check or uncheck the Preview on Screen option of the Print dialog box.

constraints: The Preview on Screen setting is local to the calling process and does not affect the printing of other processes or users.

params.name: left
params.description: Left margin

sentinelValues.meaning: Use the paper margins.
Use the printer margins.

params.name: top
params.description: Top margin

sentinelValues.meaning: Use the paper margins.
Use the printer margins.

params.name: right
params.description: Right margin, relative to the right edge of the paper

sentinelValues.meaning: Use the paper margins.
Use the printer margins.

params.name: bottom
params.description: Bottom margin, relative to the bottom edge of the paper

sentinelValues.meaning: Use the paper margins.
Use the printer margins.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET PRINTABLE MARGIN command sets the values of various printing margins by using the Print form , PRINT SELECTION and PRINT RECORD commands.

constraints: By default 4D bases printouts on the printer margins; once set, the values are retained for the entire session in the calling process.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET PROCESS VARIABLE command writes the dstVar process variables ( dstVar2 , etc.) of the destination process whose number is passed in process using the values passed in expr1 ( expr2 , etc.).

constraints: dstVar cannot be a local variable; it must be a process/interprocess variable of the destination process, or an element of such an array (arrays as a whole and pointers are not accepted as destination variables — use VARIABLE TO VARIABLE to write a whole array, or SET PROCESS VARIABLE only for a single element).
Writing the element of an array of pointers or of a two-dimensional array is not supported.
Each expr must be of a type compatible with its paired dstVar, otherwise the destination variable may end up with a meaningless value.
In interpreted mode, if a destination variable does not already exist it is created and assigned the expression's value; the destination process is never notified that its variable was written.
The destination process must be a user process, not a kernel process; if it does not exist, an error is generated (catchable with ON ERR CALL).

From a 4D Client, pass a negative value in process to write interprocess variables of the 4D Server machine (prefixing the process ID with a minus sign targets that stored procedure specifically); this communication direction only works from client to server.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET QUERY AND LOCK command can be used to request the automatic locking of records found by all queries that follow the calling of this command in the current transaction.

constraints: Must be called within a transaction; if called outside of a transaction it is ignored.

While active (lock=True), a query that encounters an already-locked record stops immediately: OK is set to 0, the current selection is cleared, and the LockedSet system set contains the record that caused the stop.

Locked records stay locked until the transaction is validated or cancelled (except the current record, which stays locked afterward too); call SET QUERY AND LOCK(False) to disable the mechanism afterward.

Only affects the query commands (QUERY, QUERY SELECTION, QUERY BY EXAMPLE, QUERY BY FORMULA, QUERY BY SQL, QUERY SELECTION BY FORMULA, QUERY SELECTION WITH ARRAY, QUERY WITH ARRAY, QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE, QUERY SELECTION BY ATTRIBUTE); it does not affect other selection-changing commands such as ALL RECORDS or RELATE MANY.

overloads.semanticRole: SET QUERY DESTINATION enables you to tell 4D where to put the result of any subsequent query for the current process.

jointConstraints.rule: destinationObject and destinationPtr are interpreted according to destinationType: if destinationType=0 (current selection), destinationObject/destinationPtr must be omitted; if destinationType=1 (set) or 2 (named selection), destinationObject is the name of the set/named selection and destinationPtr is unused; if destinationType=3 (variable), destinationObject is either the name of an existing numeric variable, or an empty string paired with destinationPtr as a pointer to the local variable to receive the result.

constraints: Affects all subsequent queries in the current process until counterbalanced by a call to SET QUERY DESTINATION(0); only the query commands are affected (QUERY, QUERY SELECTION, QUERY BY EXAMPLE, QUERY BY FORMULA, QUERY BY SQL, QUERY SELECTION BY FORMULA, QUERY SELECTION WITH ARRAY, QUERY WITH ARRAY, QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE, QUERY SELECTION BY ATTRIBUTE), not other selection-changing commands like ALL RECORDS or RELATE MANY.

When destinationType is 1 (set) or 2 (named selection), the current selection and current record for the queried table are left unchanged; a named selection that doesn't already exist is created automatically at the end of the query, and — like CUT NAMED SELECTION — only a reference is kept, so the named selection no longer exists once consumed.

When destinationType is 3 (variable) and destinationObject is a numeric variable name, that variable must already be defined or an error is returned; passing an empty string in destinationObject instead defers to destinationPtr (a pointer to the local variable to receive the count), which facilitates joint use with GET QUERY DESTINATION.

params.name: limit
params.description: Number of records, or 0 for no limit

sentinelValues.meaning: Restore queries with no limit (default state).

overloads.semanticRole: SET QUERY LIMIT allows you to tell 4D to stop any subsequent query for the current process as soon as at least the number of records you pass in limit has been found.

constraints: Affects all subsequent queries in the current process until counterbalanced by a call to SET QUERY LIMIT(0); only the query commands are affected (QUERY, QUERY SELECTION, QUERY BY EXAMPLE, QUERY BY FORMULA, QUERY BY SQL, QUERY SELECTION BY FORMULA, QUERY SELECTION WITH ARRAY, QUERY WITH ARRAY, QUERY BY ATTRIBUTE, QUERY SELECTION BY ATTRIBUTE), not other selection-changing commands like ALL RECORDS or RELATE MANY.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET REAL COMPARISON LEVEL command sets the epsilon value used by 4D to compare real values and expressions for equality.

constraints: The default epsilon is 10^-6; epsilon must always be positive.
Two real numbers a and b are considered equal for comparison purposes when Abs(a-b) does not exceed epsilon.
Only affects real-value equality comparisons in the 4D language; it has no effect on other real computations, on the display of real values, or on queries/sorts performed on fields of the Real type.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET RECENT FONTS command modifies the list of fonts displayed in the context menu of the "recent fonts".

constraints: Replaces the contents of the "recent fonts" context menu, used in particular by Programming Notes areas, with the font names supplied in fontsArray.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET TABLE CACHE PRIORITY command sets a specific priority to the data related to aTable in cache for all processes in the current session.

constraints: Should be called from the On Startup or On Server Startup database method; the priority is set in cache for all processes in the current session.
Only works in local mode (4D Server and single-user 4D); it cannot be used in 4D remote mode.
Applies to scalar-typed fields only (date, number, string); priority for binary-type fields (BLOBs, texts, pictures, objects) is handled by SET BLOBS CACHE PRIORITY instead.

overloads.semanticRole: SET TABLE TITLES lets you mask, rename, and reorder the tables of your database that appear in standard 4D dialog boxes within the Application environment (i.e.

jointConstraints.rule: tableTitles and tableNumbers must be passed together or not at all: they are parallel/synchronized arrays (same length; tableNumbers[i] is the actual table number for the display name tableTitles[i]), and a table omitted from tableTitles is hidden from the standard dialogs.

constraints: Calling SET TABLE TITLES with no parameters at all resets the whole virtual structure (custom table and field names) for the session.

Scope is the current worksession; it does not change the actual database structure, only subsequent standard-editor/dynamic-name display in the Application environment, and it does not override a table's Invisible property.

By default, formulas cannot use the custom names defined here (the real table names must be used); passing the trailing '*' lets formulas/expressions (e.g. formula editor, 4D Write Pro documents) use the custom names instead — but those custom names must not contain characters forbidden by the 4D language interpreter (e.g. -?*%!).

overloads.semanticRole: SET TEXT TO PASTEBOARD clears the pasteboard and then puts a copy of the text you passed in text into the pasteboard.

constraints: Clears the pasteboard before placing text; the text can be retrieved with Get text from pasteboard or GET PASTEBOARD DATA (e.g. "com.4d.private.text.native"); 4D text expressions can hold up to 2GB.
The pasteboard is read-only during the On Drag Over form event; this command cannot be used in that context.

params.name: seconds
params.description: Seconds until the timeout

sentinelValues.meaning: Cancel a previous timeout setting and stop monitoring serial port communication.

overloads.semanticRole: SET TIMEOUT specifies how much time a serial port command has to complete.

constraints: seconds is the total time allowed for the affected serial port command to execute, not the time between characters received; on expiry the serial port command is canceled, error -9990 is generated, and OK is set to 0 (catchable with ON ERR CALL).
Only affects RECEIVE PACKET, RECEIVE RECORD, and RECEIVE VARIABLE.

params.name: tickCount
params.description: Tickcount or -1=Trigger as soon as possible

sentinelValues.meaning: Activate the On Timer form event as soon as possible, i.e. as soon as the 4D application hands control back to the event manager (useful to ensure a form is fully displayed before further processing).

overloads.semanticRole: The SET TIMER command activates the On Timer form event and sets, for the current form and process, the number of ticks elapsed between each On Timer form event.

constraints: Applies to the current form and process; if called in a context where no form is displayed, it has no effect.
When called from a subform's form method, the On Timer event is generated in the subform, not the parent form.

params.name: folderPath
params.description: Pathname of folder (package under macOS) containing updated application

sentinelValues.meaning: Reset the update information held for the current session.

params.name: silentErrors
params.description: False (default) = report errors visibly, True = do not report them

overloads.semanticRole: The SET UPDATE FOLDER command specifies the folder containing the update of the current merged 4D application.

constraints: Only works with 4D Server or a single-user application merged with 4D Volume Desktop.

The update is placed 'on hold' in the session until RESTART 4D is called; calling this command several times before that only the last valid call is used, and the setting is not kept if the application is exited manually instead.

When silentErrors is False or omitted, errors are recorded in the update journal and shown in a warning dialog; when True, errors are only recorded in the journal — except if the journal file itself cannot be created, in which case a warning dialog is always shown regardless of silentErrors.
Sets OK to 1 if the command executes correctly, 0 otherwise; errors can be caught with ON ERR CALL.

params.name: alias
params.description: Alternate user name for 4D user account or "" to reset

sentinelValues.meaning: Remove the alias for the current 4D user (restores the real account name).

overloads.semanticRole: The SET USER ALIAS command defines an alternate, custom name to use in place of the current 4D user account name for the current session.

constraints: Can only be called from 4D remote or 4D single-user applications; it is not allowed on 4D Server.

In client/server environments, must be executed on each remote application so every user is individually identified on the server (e.g. via Current user), even if all remote applications share the same 4D user account.

The alias is used wherever the current 4D user account name would otherwise be shown or returned, e.g. Current user, Process activity, LOCKED BY, and the Users page of the 4D Server administration window.
Calling CHANGE CURRENT USER resets the alias for the current user.

params.name: winRef
params.description: Window reference number

sentinelValues.meaning: In an MDI application on Windows, targets the main window; ignored (does nothing) on macOS or in an SDI application on Windows.

overloads.semanticRole: Removes the window's custom icon, restoring the platform default (no icon on macOS, the application icon on Windows).

discriminatedBy.rule: Called with winRef only (no image, no file).

params.name: winRef
params.description: Window reference number

sentinelValues.meaning: In an MDI application on Windows, targets the main window; ignored (does nothing) on macOS or in an SDI application on Windows.

params.name: image
params.description: Custom icon

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the window's icon to a custom image; the window's menu does not show a file path.

discriminatedBy.rule: Called with winRef and image only (no file).

params.name: winRef
params.description: Window reference number

sentinelValues.meaning: In an MDI application on Windows, targets the main window; ignored (does nothing) on macOS or in an SDI application on Windows.

params.name: file
params.description: File path or folder path

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the window's icon from a file/folder's type, and shows that file's path in the window's menu.

discriminatedBy.rule: Called with winRef and file only (no image).

params.name: winRef
params.description: Window reference number

sentinelValues.meaning: In an MDI application on Windows, targets the main window; ignored (does nothing) on macOS or in an SDI application on Windows.

params.name: image
params.description: Custom icon

params.name: file
params.description: File path or folder path

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the window's icon to a custom image while showing the given file's path in the window's menu.

discriminatedBy.rule: Called with winRef, image, and file together.

constraints: If only file is passed, the window shows the icon matching the file's type and the file's path in the window's menu; if only image is passed, the passed image is used as the icon and no path is shown; if both are passed, the file's path is shown in the window's menu while the passed image is used as the icon.
If only winRef is passed, or image is empty, the icon is removed on macOS and the default (application) icon is shown on Windows.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET WINDOW RECT command changes the global coordinates of the window whose reference number is passed in window .

interactionNotes.note: By default, executing this command moves the designated window to the foreground. Passing '*' as the last parameter disables that: the window's original level (z-order) is left unchanged.

constraints: If window does not designate an existing window, the command does nothing.

Coordinates are relative to the top-left corner of the application window's contents area (Windows MDI mode) or to the main screen (macOS and Windows SDI mode), and describe the window's contents area (excluding title bar/borders); using Screen width/Screen height to double-check values is recommended since the command lets you move a window beyond the main window's or screen's limits.
Does not move or resize the form objects contained in the window regardless of their resizing properties; use RESIZE FORM WINDOW to also account for object resizing properties.

overloads.semanticRole: The SET WINDOW TITLE command changes the title of the window whose reference number is passed in window to the text passed in title (max.

constraints: title is truncated to a maximum of 80 characters.
If the window reference number does not correspond to an existing window, SET WINDOW TITLE does nothing.

In the Design environment, 4D manages window titles automatically and is likely to override a title set by this command; in the Application (compiled/runtime) environment, 4D never changes window titles itself.

overloads.semanticRole: The SHOW MENU BAR command makes the menu bar visible.
The SHOW ON DISK command displays the file or folder whose pathname was passed in the pathname parameter in a standard window of the operating system.

constraints: By default, if pathname designates a folder, only the folder's own location/level is shown, not its contents.
If the optional * parameter is passed and pathname designates a folder, the folder is opened and its contents are displayed.
If pathname designates a file (not a folder), the * parameter is ignored.

overloads.semanticRole: SHOW PROCESS displays all the windows belonging to process .

constraints: Only makes the process's windows visible; it does not bring them to the frontmost level (use BRING TO FRONT for that).
If the process's windows are already displayed, the command has no effect.

overloads.semanticRole: The SHOW TOOL BAR command handles the display of custom toolbars created by the Open form window command for the current process.

constraints: Only affects a custom toolbar window previously created via Open form window with the Toolbar form window option, for the current process.
If the toolbar window was already visible, or no toolbar window has been created for the current process, the command does nothing.

overloads.semanticRole: The SHOW WINDOW command displays the window whose number was passed in window .

constraints: The target window must have previously been hidden using HIDE WINDOW; if the window is already displayed, the command does nothing.

overloads.semanticRole: The SMTP New transporter command configures a new SMTP connection according to the server parameter and returns a new SMTP transporter object object.

constraints: The parameter object's .host property is mandatory; all other properties are optional and default as documented (e.g. .port defaults to 587, .connectionTimeOut to 30s, .sendTimeOut to 100s, .keepAlive to True, .acceptUnsecureConnection to False).

If .accessTokenOAuth2 is passed but .authenticationMode is omitted, the OAuth2 protocol is used (if allowed by the server); .authenticationMode otherwise defaults to the most secure mode supported by the server.
.accessTokenOAuth2 and .password are consumed for authentication but are not echoed back on the returned SMTP transporter object.

This command only configures the transporter; it does not open a connection to the SMTP server. The connection is actually opened when .send() is called, and is closed either when the transporter object is destroyed (if .keepAlive is true) or after each .send() call (if .keepAlive is false).

overloads.semanticRole: The SOAP DECLARATION command explicitly declares the type of parameters used in a 4D method published as a Web Service.

constraints: variable may only refer to a process variable or a 4D method argument ($0 to $n); local and interprocess variables cannot be used.
This command does not support blob objects (4D.Blob type) as the declared variable's value.
In input_output, pass 1 (SOAP input) for a value received by the method, or 2 (SOAP output) for a value returned by the method.
If alias is omitted, 4D uses the variable's name (or FourD_argN for method arguments $0-$n) as the published name by default.
alias must be unique across all input and output parameters declared for the same RPC call; if it is not, only the last declaration with that alias is taken into account.
alias must not begin with a number or contain spaces, and extended/accented characters are discouraged.
This command must be called from within the method published as the Web Service itself; it cannot be called from another method.
Incoming SOAP arguments referred to via 4D variables (rather than method arguments) must first be declared in the COMPILER_WEB project method.

overloads.semanticRole: The SOAP Get info command retrieves, in the form of a character string, the different types of information concerning a SOAP request.

constraints: infoNum selects which piece of SOAP request metadata to retrieve, e.g. 1 = name of the Web Service method about to execute, 2 = name of the Web Service the method belongs to.
Intended to be called from within the On Web Authentication Database Method to inspect an incoming SOAP request (e.g. for security checks) before it is otherwise available.

overloads.semanticRole: The SOAP REJECT NEW REQUESTS command specifies whether or not the Web Services server accepts new SOAP requests.

constraints: This command only has an effect when executed on 4D Server; if the calling method runs locally on a remote client or in 4D single-user, the command does nothing.

overloads.semanticRole: The SOAP Request command returns True if the code being executed is part of a SOAP request.
The SOAP SEND FAULT command returns an error to a SOAP client indicating the origin of the fault: client or server.

constraints: faultType selects the origin of the error reported to the SOAP client: 1 = client fault (e.g. an invalid request), 2 = server fault (e.g. a server-side resource error).
Using this command lets the Web Service method report an error to the client without returning a normal result.

overloads.semanticRole: The SORT ARRAY command sorts one or more arrays into ascending or descending order.

constraints: The order symbol is counterintuitive: > sorts ascending, < sorts descending; if omitted, the sort is ascending.
Pointer and Picture arrays cannot be sorted.
For a two-dimensional array, only an element (e.g. a2DArray{i}) can be sorted, not the two-dimensional array itself.

When multiple arrays are passed, they are all reordered together following the sort order computed from the first array only; this is a single-level sort, not a multi-level sort (use MULTI SORT ARRAY for synchronized multi-level sorting).

overloads.semanticRole: The SORT LIST command sorts the list whose reference number is passed in list .

constraints: The order symbol is counterintuitive: > sorts ascending, < sorts descending; if omitted, the sort is ascending.
Sorts all levels of the list: first the top-level items, then the items of each sublist, recursively through all levels.
Does not change the current list item or the current expanded/collapsed state, but the current item's position may change as a result of the sort.

overloads.semanticRole: The SPELL ADD TO USER DICTIONARY command adds one or more words to the current user dictionary.

constraints: The check scans forward from checkPos and stops at the first unknown word found (if any).

The OK system variable is set to 0 if the check completes without an initialization error and an unknown word is found; OK is set to 1 if an initialization error occurs, or if no unknown words are found.
macOS: when the native spell checker is enabled, this command does not support grammar correction.

overloads.semanticRole: The SPELL CHECKING command triggers the spell check of the field or variable having the focus in the currently displayed form.

constraints: langID receives the automatically generated dictionary IDs (unique, based on file names) used with SPELL SET CURRENT DICTIONARY.
langFiles receives the dictionary file names without extensions.

langNames receives the language names in the current application language, suffixed with "- Hunspell"; unrecognized/custom dictionary files return "N/A - Hunspell" (the dictionary can still be used via its returned ID).

overloads.semanticRole: The SPELL Get current dictionary command returns the ID number of the dictionary being used.
The SPELL SET CURRENT DICTIONARY command causes the replacement of the current dictionary with the one specified by the dictionary parameter.
The SQL CANCEL LOAD command ends the current SELECT request and initializes the parameters.
The SQL EXECUTE SCRIPT command is used to execute a series of SQL statements placed in the script file designated by scriptPath .

constraints: This command can only be executed on a local machine (local 4D or a stored procedure on 4D Server); it cannot be used with an external connection opened directly or via ODBC.
If scriptPath is an empty string (""), a standard Open document dialog box is displayed so the user can select the script file.

In the current version, only one attribName/attribValue pair is meaningful: attribName = SQL_Use_Access_Rights (the "SQL use access rights" constant), with attribValue = 1 meaning 4D restricts execution to the current 4D user's access rights, and attribValue = 0 (or the pair omitted) meaning Designer rights are used without restriction.

The OK system variable reflects the outcome: it is set to 1 if the script executes with no error; on error, OK is set to 0 if errorAction is SQL On error abort (1), to 0 or 1 depending on the user's choice if errorAction is SQL On error confirm (2), and per the continue behavior if errorAction is SQL On error continue (3).

overloads.semanticRole: The SQL EXPORT DATABASE command exports in SQL format all the records of all the tables in the database.

constraints: This command cannot be used with an external connection opened directly or via ODBC.
The export files are placed in a folder named "SQLExport" created inside folderPath; if an "SQLExport" folder already exists there, it is replaced without any warning.
If folderPath is an empty string, a standard folder-selection dialog box is displayed (defaulting to the current user's Documents folder).
The generated Export.sql file(s) can be fed directly into SQL EXECUTE SCRIPT to import the data into another 4D database.

overloads.semanticRole: The SQL EXPORT SELECTION command exports in SQL format the records of the current selection of the 4D table designated by the aTable parameter.

constraints: Unlike SQL EXPORT DATABASE, this command only works with the main (internal) database, not an external SQL database, and it does not support Object type fields.
Exports only the current selection of aTable, not the entire database; if the current selection is empty, the command does nothing and the destination folder is not emptied.
The OK system variable is set to 1 if the export completes correctly, otherwise 0.
If folderPath is an empty string, a standard folder-selection dialog box is displayed, as for SQL EXPORT DATABASE.

overloads.semanticRole: The SQL End selection command is used to determine if the boundaries of the result set have been reached.

constraints: This command does not take file type data sources into account.
Requires the 4D ODBC Driver to be installed on the machine when connecting to an external 4D data source via ODBC.
This command must generally be called within an error-handling method installed via ON ERR CALL.
errODBC and errSQLServer are only filled when the error originates from the ODBC source; otherwise they are returned empty.

overloads.semanticRole: The SQL Get current data source command returns the name of the current data source of the application.

sentinelValues.meaning: SQL All Records constant: retrieve all records of the table.

constraints: If numRecords is omitted, the command retrieves only the current record from the data source (for use in a loop that receives one record at a time).

overloads.semanticRole: Opens (or re-opens, implicitly closing any existing one) a per-process SQL connection to an external 4D Server, ODBC source, or the internal 4D database, becoming the target of subsequent SQL EXECUTE calls and (if '*' is passed) of code inside Begin SQL/End SQL tags.

jointConstraints.rule: userName and password are grouped as an optional pair in the syntax: pass both together or omit both, not just one.

constraints: dataEntry also accepts structured prefixed syntaxes documented separately: 'IP:<address>{:<port>}' for a direct 4D Server connection, '4D:<Publication_Name>' for a 4D Server publication name, and 'ODBC:<DSN>' (prefix required in uppercase) for an ODBC data source.
For a direct (4D Server) connection, passing empty strings for userName/password only succeeds if 4D passwords are not activated on the target database; otherwise the connection is refused.
Calling SQL LOGIN again without an explicit SQL LOGOUT automatically closes the previous connection first.
On success the OK system variable is set to 1; on failure it is set to 0, an error is generated, and the internal 4D database automatically becomes the current data source again.

overloads.semanticRole: The SQL LOGOUT command closes the connection with an ODBC source that is open in the current process (if applicable).
The SQL SET OPTION command modifies the value of the option passed in option .

constraints: option identifies which SQL-theme setting to change (e.g. SQL asynchronous, SQL charset, SQL connection timeout); the expected type and valid range of value depend on which option constant is passed, per the SQL theme constants documentation.
SQL connection timeout must be set before opening the connection (i.e. before SQL LOGIN) in order to take effect.

overloads.semanticRole: The SQL SET PARAMETER command allows the use of a 4D variable, array or field value in SQL requests.

constraints: paramType must be one of the SQL-theme 'SQL param ...' constants (e.g. SQL param in, SQL param in out); 'in out' is usable only in the context of an SQL stored procedure.
As an alternative to this command, a 4D object's name can be inserted directly between << and >> characters in the SQL request text.

The START MONITORING ACTIVITY command records operations exceeding a specified duration in memory.

constraints: Only available on 4D remote, 4D Server, and 4D standalone applications when source is not network activity; must be paired with a later STOP MONITORING ACTIVITY call to stop tracking.

overloads.semanticRole: The START SQL SERVER command launches the integrated SQL server in the 4D application where it has been executed.

constraints: Does not affect the internal 4D SQL kernel, which remains available for internal queries regardless of whether the integrated SQL server is started.

overloads.semanticRole: START TRANSACTION starts a transaction in the current process.

constraints: Transactions can be nested (sub-transactions); each transaction/sub-transaction must eventually be individually cancelled or validated.
If the main (outermost) transaction is cancelled, all of its sub-transactions are cancelled too, regardless of whether those sub-transactions were themselves already validated.

overloads.semanticRole: The STOP MONITORING ACTIVITY command stops tracking activity started with the START MONITORING ACTIVITY command.

constraints: Empties any activity record currently held in memory after stopping tracking; call Monitored activity before this command if you still need that data.
Can be called and executed on 4D remote, 4D Server, and 4D standalone applications.

overloads.semanticRole: The STOP SQL SERVER command stops the integrated SQL server in the 4D application where it has been executed.

constraints: Does nothing if the SQL server was not launched; does not affect the internal 4D SQL kernel, which remains available for internal queries.

overloads.semanticRole: The Select RGB color command displays the system color selection window and returns the RGB value of the color selected by the user.

constraints: If defaultColor is omitted or 0, the color black is preselected when the dialog box opens.
Under Windows: if the user validates with OK, the command returns the selected color in RGB format and OK is set to 1; if the user cancels, the command returns -1 and OK is set to 0.

Under macOS: the dialog can only be closed via the close box or Esc; OK is always set to 1 regardless of user action, and the command returns the selected color, or the value passed in defaultColor if the user made no selection.

constraints: Returns 0 if the current selection of aTable is empty or there is no current record.

constraints: aField and template are alternative ways to restrict which fields are serialized; pass at most one of them. If neither is passed, all JSON-expressible fields of aTable are included (BLOB and Picture fields are always ignored).
After the call, the current selection is unchanged but the current record is no longer loaded and may have changed.

constraints: Returns a valid pointer only when called from within an object method, or from a project method called directly/indirectly by an object method; otherwise returns a Nil pointer (->[]).
In the context of a list box, returns a pointer to the list box or to a column of the list box depending on the calling context.

overloads.semanticRole: A semaphore is a flag shared among workstations or among processes on the same workstation.

constraints: A semaphore name is limited to 255 characters (including the '$' prefix); longer strings are silently truncated before testing.
Semaphore names are case-sensitive.
Returns FALSE and creates the semaphore if it did not already exist (the semaphore is now set for the calling process); returns TRUE and does nothing if it already existed.

overloads.semanticRole: Sequence number returns the next sequence number for aTable .

constraints: Numbering starts at 1 by default and only begins incrementing at the first call to Sequence number (or another feature accessing the sequence number) for the table, so the returned value should not be treated as a count of records created.

overloads.semanticRole: The Session info command returns an object describing the session whose ID you pass in the sessionID parameter..

constraints: Returns a null object if sessionId does not identify a valid session.
This command returns the .info property of the sessionId session; to get information about the current session, call Session.info directly instead.

overloads.semanticRole: The Session storage command returns the storage object of the session whose unique identifier you passed in the id parameter.

constraints: Returns Null if no session exists with the given id.
The returned object is the .storage property of the session (a shared object usable from any preemptive or standard process).

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the Session object corresponding to the current session (a web session, a remote user session, a stored procedures session, or a standalone session, depending on the calling process).

constraints: Returns Null if called in a web process and scalable sessions are disabled on the web server.

params.name: groupID
params.description: in: unique ID number of the group to modify, or -1/-2 to add a new group; out: unique ID number of the added group, if one was added.

sentinelValues.meaning: Add a new group, affiliated with the Designer (binary databases).
Add a new group, affiliated with the Administrator (binary databases only).

params.name: owner
params.description: Binary databases only; ignored in project databases.

overloads.semanticRole: Set group properties enables you to change and update the properties of an existing group whose unique group ID number you pass in groupID , or to add a new group.

constraints: The mechanical draft left groupID with direction 'in', but the doc's arrow column marks it '<->' (inout): it is both an input (group ID to modify, or -1/-2 to add) and an output (receives the new group's ID number when adding).
If groupID is not -1, -2, or a valid existing group ID, the command does nothing.
If members is omitted, the group's current member list is left unchanged (or the new group has no members, when adding); passing an empty members array removes all members.

params.name: userID
params.description: in: unique ID number of the user account to modify, or -1/-2 to add a new user; out: unique ID number of the added/modified user.

sentinelValues.meaning: Add a new user, affiliated with the Designer (binary databases).
Add a new user, affiliated with the Administrator (binary databases only).

params.name: password
params.description: New unencrypted password (4D encrypts it before saving), or the * symbol to leave the existing password unchanged.

sentinelValues.meaning: Leave the account's existing password unchanged.

params.name: nbLogin
params.description: Binary databases only; ignored in project databases.

params.name: lastLogin
params.description: Binary databases only; ignored in project databases.

params.name: groupOwner
params.description: Binary databases only; ID number of the default owner group for objects created by this user.

overloads.semanticRole: Set user properties lets you change and update the properties of an existing user account whose unique user ID number you pass in userID , or add a new user.

constraints: The mechanical draft left userID with direction 'in', but the doc's arrow column marks it '<->' (inout): it is both an input (user ID to modify, or -1/-2 to add) and an output (receives the new/modified user's ID number).
If userID is not -1, -2, or a valid existing user ID, the command does nothing.
If the user account does not exist or has been deleted, error -9979 is generated (catchable with ON ERR CALL); check first with Is user deleted.
If name is not unique, the command does nothing and error -9979 is generated.
If memberships is omitted, the user's current memberships are left unchanged (or the new user belongs to no group, when adding); passing an empty memberships array revokes all memberships.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns TRUE if the Shift key is currently pressed.
Sin returns the sine of number , where number is expressed in radians.4D provides the predefined constants Pi, Degree, and Radian.
The Size of array command returns the number of elements in array .
The Split string command returns a collection of strings, created by splitting stringToSplit into substrings at the boundaries specified by the separator parameter.
Square root returns the square root of number .
Std deviation returns the standard deviation of series .
Returns the catalog of shared objects and shared collections registered in the Storage object of the current machine or component.

constraints: There is one Storage catalog per machine and per component; the returned object is itself a shared object and can only contain shared objects and shared collections.
Adding a property to the returned object must be surrounded by Use...End use; reading an attribute outside of Use...End use is possible, but writing without it raises an error.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the string form of expression (Real, Integer, Date, Time, Text, or Boolean) using the default format, or the format/addTime you specify.

discriminatedBy.rule: Applies when at most a display format and (for dates) an addTime are passed, as opposed to the numeric-base overload.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the string form of a numeric expression converted to the given base (radix), between 2 and 36.

discriminatedBy.rule: Applies when a second Integer parameter is passed as a radix (2-36) instead of a display format; only valid for numeric expression.

constraints: The String function is not compatible with "Integer 64 bits" type fields in compiled mode.

overloads.semanticRole: The Structure file command returns the pathname of the structure file for the database with which you are currently working.file.

constraints: When called from a component: if * is passed, returns the pathname of the host database's structure file; if * is omitted, returns the pathname of the component's own structure file.
In remote mode, only the name of the structure/project file is returned, not the full pathname.

For a compiled database merged with 4D Volume Desktop, returns the pathname of the executable application file instead of the structure file (kept for compatibility; use Application file to get the full software package pathname).

overloads.semanticRole: The Substring command returns the portion of source defined by firstChar and numChars .
Subtotal returns the subtotal for data for the current or last break level.

constraints: pageBreak controls page breaks during printing: 0 (or omitted) causes no page break; 1 causes a page break at each level-1 break; 2 causes a page break at each level-1 and level-2 break; and so on for higher levels.
Must execute BREAK LEVEL and ACCUMULATE before every form report for which subtotals are calculated.

overloads.semanticRole: Sum squares returns the sum of the squares of series .

constraints: If series is an array (one- or two-dimensional) rather than an indexed field, the array must be of Integer, Longint, or Real type.

overloads.semanticRole: The Sum command returns the sum (total of all values) for series .
Calls the parent (superclass) class constructor from within a subclass's Class constructor, forwarding param(s) to it; must be called before This can be used inside that constructor.

discriminatedBy.rule: Function-call syntax Super(...param), valid only inside a subclass's Class constructor.

overloads.semanticRole: Used as a bare reference (no parentheses) within a subclass class function to access the parent (superclass) implementation, e.g. Super.methodName(...); evaluates to the object's parent.

discriminatedBy.rule: Bare property-style reference Super (no parentheses), valid inside a subclass class function, not inside the constructor.

sentinelValues.meaning: System (default if omitted): active System folder
Fonts

User preferences_user: preferences folder customized for the current user

Startup Win_user (Windows only; returns an empty string on macOS)

Start menu Win_user (Windows only; returns an empty string on macOS)

Favorites Win (Windows only; returns an empty string on macOS)
Desktop
Applications or program files

Home folder: current home folder of the user

constraints: Constants suffixed 'Win' are usable on Windows only; when used on macOS, the command returns an empty string.
Constants 2-9 come in _all/_user pairs, selecting between a folder shared by all users vs. one customized for the current user.

overloads.semanticRole: The System info command returns an object containg information about the operating system and the characteristics of the system hardware and software from the machine it's executed on.

params.name: arrText

If passed, interpret varText as multistyle text; width/fontName/fontSize/fontStyle are then ignored, since the original per-run styles are used and preserved in arrText's elements instead.

constraints: Each arrText element must contain at least one word; if width is too small for a word to fit, the array is filled as close as possible to the requested width and the OK system variable is set to 0.
For raw (non-multistyle) text, width, fontName, and fontSize are mandatory so the command can measure line lengths.

Out: updated to the offset just past the written text, for reuse in a subsequent write. If omitted (and * also omitted), the text is written at the start of the BLOB, overwriting prior contents.

overloads.semanticRole: Writes text into the BLOB at a given (or default zero) offset, overwriting existing content there, and returns the post-write offset via the offset variable for chained writes.

discriminatedBy.rule: Used when the caller needs to track/reuse the write position (offset variable form); mutually exclusive with the trailing '*' append-flag overload.

params.description: If passed, the text is appended to the end of the BLOB, extending its size accordingly, instead of overwriting at an offset.

discriminatedBy.rule: Used when the caller wants simple append-or-overwrite-at-start behavior via the '*' flag, without tracking an offset.

constraints: Since this command alters the BLOB passed as a parameter, it does not support blob objects (4D.Blob type); only legacy BLOB variables/fields.
New bytes allocated in the BLOB beyond what is written (e.g. when writing past the current end) are initialized to zero.

overloads.semanticRole: The TEXT TO DOCUMENT command lets you write the text directly to a disk file.

constraints: In fileName, you can pass just a file name (placed next to the structure file), a pathname relative to the structure file, or an absolute pathname.
By default, documents generated by this command have no extension; you must include one in fileName if desired.
If the target file already exists, its prior contents are erased, unless it is already open elsewhere, in which case an error is generated.
charSet accepts either a standard character-set name (e.g. 'ISO-8859-1', 'UTF-8') or its MIBEnum ID (as a Longint).

overloads.semanticRole: You use TRACE to trace methods during the development of a database.

params.name: picture
params.description: In: source picture to be transformed. Out: resulting picture after transformation (the source picture is modified directly).

params.name: operator
params.description: Type of transformation to perform

sentinelValues.meaning: Reset: undoes all matrix operations (scale, flip, translate, ...) carried out on the picture; no param1-4 used
Scale: param1/param2 are horizontal/vertical resize factors (e.g. 1.5 to enlarge width by 50%, 0.5 to reduce height by 50%)
Translate: param1/param2 are horizontal/vertical pixel offsets (positive = right/down, negative = left/up)
Flip horizontally: no param1-4 used; any prior translation is not taken into account
Flip vertically: no param1-4 used; any prior translation is not taken into account
Crop: param1/param2 are the X/Y origin (pixels) and param3/param4 are the width/height of the cropped picture; not reversible
Fade to grey scale: no param1-4 used; not reversible
Transparency: param1 is a hexadecimal RGB color (e.g. 0x00FFFFFF for white, the default if param1 is omitted) whose matching pixels become transparent; not reversible

params.name: param1
params.description: First transformation parameter; meaning depends on operator (see operator's sentinelValues)

params.name: param2
params.description: Second transformation parameter; meaning depends on operator (see operator's sentinelValues)

params.name: param3
params.description: Third transformation parameter; meaning depends on operator (see operator's sentinelValues), used only by Crop

params.name: param4
params.description: Fourth transformation parameter; meaning depends on operator (see operator's sentinelValues), used only by Crop

jointConstraints.rule: The number and meaning of param1-param4 actually used depends entirely on operator: Reset/Flip horizontally/Flip vertically/Fade to grey scale use none of them; Scale/Translate use param1-param2; Transparency uses only param1; Crop uses all of param1-param4.

constraints: Transformations do not change the picture's underlying type (e.g. a vectorial picture remains vectorial after transformation).
Scale, Translate, Flip horizontally, and Flip vertically are cancellable (reversible via the opposite operation or Reset); Crop, Fade to grey scale, and Transparency are not.

If triggerLevel does not correspond to an existing trigger execution level, the command fills dbEvent, tableNum, and recordNum with 0.

overloads.semanticRole: The TRUNCATE TABLE command quickly deletes all the records of aTable .

constraints: Similar in effect to an ALL RECORDS / DELETE SELECTION sequence, but no trigger is called and referential integrity is not checked.

Fails (does nothing, sets OK to 0) if a transaction is underway in the calling process, or if one or more records of aTable are locked by another process; in the locked-record case an error is also generated and no LockedSet system set is created.
Does nothing and sets OK to 1 if aTable is already empty.
Does nothing and sets OK to 0 if aTable is in read-only.
After a successful call, there is no longer any current selection or current record for aTable.
The operation is recorded in the log file, if one exists.
Conceptually similar to the SQL TRUNCATE TABLE command.

overloads.semanticRole: The Table fragmentation command returns the percentage of logical fragmentation for the records of the table designated by the aTable parameter.
Returns the name of the table designated by its table number, tableNum.

discriminatedBy.rule: Used when identifying the table by its numeric table number.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the name of the table designated by a pointer to it, tablePtr.

discriminatedBy.rule: Used when identifying the table by a pointer to it (e.g. obtained via Table).

overloads.semanticRole: Tan returns the tangent of number , where number is expressed in radians.4D provides the predefined constants Pi, Degree, and Radian.
The Temporary folder command returns the pathname to the current temporary folder set by your system.
The Test path name function checks if a document or folder whose name or pathname you pass in pathname is present on the disk.

constraints: Return value: 1 if pathname refers to an existing document; 0 if pathname refers to an existing folder/directory; a negative value (an OS file manager error code, e.g. -43 for File not found) if pathname does not exist.

overloads.semanticRole: The Test semaphore command tests for the existence of a semaphore.

constraints: Unlike Semaphore, Test semaphore does not create the semaphore if it doesn't already exist; it only reports whether it currently exists.

overloads.semanticRole: The This command returns a reference to the currently processed object.

constraints: The value of This is determined by how the enclosing function was called, not by lexical scope; it cannot be set by assignment and may differ on each call.
Outside any context where This is meaningful (e.g. an object/class method, formula, or entity attribute context), the command returns Null.

overloads.semanticRole: Tickcount returns the number of ticks (60th of a second) elapsed since the machine was started.Tickcount returns a value of type Long Integer.
The Time string command returns the string form of the time expression you pass in seconds .

constraints: Returned string is in HH:MM:SS 24-hour format; if seconds exceeds a day's worth (86,400), the hours component keeps incrementing beyond 23 (e.g. Time string(86401) returns '24:00:01') rather than wrapping.

overloads.semanticRole: The Time command returns a time expression equivalent to the time specified in the timeValue parameter.

constraints: timeValue may be a Text string in one of the 4D standard time formats for the current system language, or a Longint representing the number of seconds elapsed since 00:00:00.
If timeValue evaluates to undefined, Time returns an empty time (00:00:00) rather than an error.

overloads.semanticRole: Timestamp returns the current UTC time in ISO format with milliseconds, i.e.
The Tool bar height command returns the height of the current visible tool bar, expressed in pixels.

constraints: Returns 0 if the tool bar is currently hidden.

overloads.semanticRole: The Transaction level command returns the current transaction level for the process.

constraints: Returns 0 if no transaction has been started in the current process.

overloads.semanticRole: Called from within a trigger, the Trigger event command returns a numeric value that denotes the type of the database event, in other words, the reason why the trigger has been invoked.

constraints: Meaningful only when called from within a trigger; the return value denotes the database event that invoked the trigger: 0 outside any trigger execution cycle, 1 On Saving New Record Event, 2 On Saving Existing Record Event, 3 On Deleting Record Event.
Same event-code numbering as the dbEvent output parameter of TRIGGER PROPERTIES.

overloads.semanticRole: The Trigger level command returns the execution level of the trigger.

constraints: Returns 0 if called outside any trigger execution cycle; otherwise returns the cascading execution level of the current trigger call (see Cascading Triggers).
Used together with TRIGGER PROPERTIES to perform different actions depending on the cascading of trigger execution levels.

overloads.semanticRole: The Trim end command removes whitespace from the end of the aString parameter and returns a new string, without modifying the original one.
The Trim start command removes whitespace from the beginning of the aString parameter and returns a new string, without modifying the original one.
The Trim command removes whitespace from both ends of the aString parameter and returns a new string, without modifying the original one.
True returns the Boolean value True.
Returns number with its decimal part truncated to the number of decimal places specified by places, always truncating toward negative infinity (not toward zero).

constraints: If places is positive, number is truncated to that many decimal places; if places is negative, number is truncated to the left of the decimal point.

overloads.semanticRole: The Type command returns a numeric value that indicates the type of field or variable you have passed in the fieldVar parameter.

constraints: Cannot be applied to scalar expressions such as object properties (emp.name) or collection elements (myColl[5]); use Value type for those.
In compiled mode, calling Type on a method parameter declared as variant returns the actual data type (same as Value type), not the Is variant constant.

overloads.semanticRole: UNION creates a set that contains all records from set1 and set2 .

constraints: set1 and set2 must both belong to the same table; resultSet is created on that same table.
resultSet replaces any existing set with the same name, including reusing the name of set1 or set2.
The resulting set's current record is the current record of set1.
In Client/Server mode, all three sets must be visible (interprocess, process, or local, created on the appropriate machine) to the calling process.

overloads.semanticRole: UNLOAD RECORD unloads the current record of table .

constraints: Unloads the record from memory but it remains the current record; the next record made current automatically unloads (and unlocks) the previous current record.
If the record was locked for other users, unloading it unlocks it for them while keeping it as the local user's current record.

overloads.semanticRole: The UNREGISTER CLIENT command “unregisters” a 4D client station.

constraints: A 4D client is automatically unregistered when the user quits the application.
If the client workstation was not previously registered (via REGISTER CLIENT), or if executed on 4D in local mode, the command has no effect.

overloads.semanticRole: USE CHARACTER SET modifies the character set used by 4D during data transfer between the database and a document or a serial port for the current process.

constraints: map must be the IANA name of the character set (or a recognized alias), e.g. "iso-8859-1"/"latin1" or "utf-8"; passing the literal * resets the map to the default character set (UTF-8) instead.
mapInOut selects which transfer direction the map applies to: 0 (or omitted) = export/output map, 1 = import/input map.

Only affects text/DIF/SYLK import-export and text-type SEND PACKET/RECEIVE PACKET/RECEIVE BUFFER transfers; has no effect on SEND RECORD, SEND VARIABLE, RECEIVE RECORD, RECEIVE VARIABLE, or BLOB-type packet transfers.

overloads.semanticRole: The USE ENTITY SELECTION command updates the current selection of the table matching the dataclass of the entitySelection parameter, according to the content of the entity selection.

constraints: Cannot be used with a Remote datastore.
In 4D single-user and 4D Server, entitySelection is directly connected to the resulting current selection for performance; once used, entitySelection must not be reused or altered afterwards.
After the call, the first record of the updated current selection (if any) becomes the current record but is not loaded into memory; use LOAD RECORD afterwards if field values are needed.

overloads.semanticRole: USE NAMED SELECTION uses the named selection name as the current selection for the table to which it belongs.
USE SET makes the records in set the current selection for the table to which the set belongs.

params.name: users
params.description: Receives the encrypted list of all user accounts and database groups

overloads.semanticRole: Stores in the BLOB users the encrypted list of all user accounts and database groups created by the Administrator, readable only via BLOB TO USERS.

constraints: Only works in binary databases; in 4D projects it always returns an empty BLOB.
Only the database Administrator or Designer can execute this command; otherwise it does nothing and generates privilege error -9949.
The generated BLOB is encrypted and can only be read back with BLOB TO USERS.

overloads.semanticRole: Undefined returns True if the result of the evaluation of expression is not a defined value, and False otherwise.

constraints: A variable is defined if it was created via a compilation directive or has been assigned a value; it is undefined otherwise. If the database is compiled, Undefined always returns False for variables.
An object property is undefined if it does not exist in the object.
Always returns False for field references.
Undefined($exp) is equivalent to (Value type($exp)=Is undefined); expression is evaluated as part of the call.

overloads.semanticRole: Uppercase takes aString and returns the string with all alphabetic characters in uppercase.

constraints: By default (when * is omitted), accented characters lose their accents after conversion; passing * keeps them as accented uppercase characters.

overloads.semanticRole: User in group returns TRUE if user is in group .

constraints: user must be an actual user account name; user aliases are not supported. If user aliases are defined, pass the value returned by Current user (rather than the alias) to guarantee an account name.

overloads.semanticRole: VALIDATE TRANSACTION accepts the transaction that was started with START TRANSACTION of the corresponding level in the current process.

constraints: Transactions can be nested (sub-transactions); if the main (outer) transaction is later cancelled, all sub-transactions are cancelled even if individually validated with this command.
Validates the transaction started by START TRANSACTION at the corresponding nesting level in the current process.

params.description: Variable to store in the BLOB

params.name: blob
params.description: BLOB to receive the variable

params.description: In: byte offset within the BLOB at which to write (0 if omitted, i.e. overwrite from the start). Out: returned incremented by the number of bytes written, for reuse in a subsequent BLOB-writing call.

overloads.semanticRole: Writes variable into blob at the given offset (or at the start, overwriting existing contents, if offset is omitted), returning the updated offset (advanced past the written bytes) for chaining further writes.

params.name: variable
params.description: Variable to store in the BLOB

params.name: blob
params.description: BLOB to receive the variable
If passed, append the value to the end of the BLOB instead of overwriting it from the start

overloads.semanticRole: Appends variable to the end of blob, extending the BLOB's size accordingly, so multiple variables/lists can be stored sequentially in the same BLOB.

constraints: Accepts any variable type, including other BLOBs and streamable objects; a Long Integer holding a hierarchical list reference (ListRef) is stored as a Long Integer, not the list itself -- use LIST TO BLOB/BLOB to list for lists.
Objects and collections are stored as a copy, not a reference; any pointers inside them are stored as their dereferenced values.
Content must be read back with BLOB TO VARIABLE, since 4D uses an internal format that is also platform-independent (no byte-swapping needed between Windows and Macintosh).
Does not support blob objects (4D.Blob type) since it alters the blob passed as a parameter; only classic BLOB values are supported.

overloads.semanticRole: Copies the value of each srcVar process variable of the current process into the corresponding dstVar process variable of the destination process whose number is passed in process (srcVar and dstVar may have different names); repeated dstVar/srcVar pairs copy several variables in one call.
The VERIFY CURRENT DATA FILE command carries out a structural check of the objects found in the data file currently opened by 4D.

constraints: Identical behavior to VERIFY DATA FILE but applied to the currently open database's own data file, so it takes no structurePath/dataPath.
If called with no parameters at all, defaults are: objects = Verify All (16), options = 0 (log file created, not timestamped), method = "", tablesArray/fieldsArray omitted.
Flushes the data cache and blocks all operations accessing the data for the duration of the verification.
If a log file is generated, its complete pathname is returned in the Document system variable.
See VERIFY DATA FILE for the full meaning of objects, options, method, tablesArray and fieldsArray.

params.name: structurePath
params.description: Pathname of 4D structure file to be checked; pass an empty string to show an Open file dialog

params.name: dataPath
params.description: Pathname (or file name) of the 4D data file (.4DD) to check; pass an empty string to show an Open file dialog

params.name: objects
params.description: Which object types to check: sum of Verify Records and/or Verify Indexes bit values, or Verify All

sentinelValues.meaning: Verify all (Verify Records + Verify Indexes plus a full internal check)
Verify indexes: checks physical index consistency only, cannot detect duplicated keys
Verify records
Equivalent to Verify Records + Verify Indexes (12)

params.name: options
params.description: Verification/log options: sum of applicable bit values

sentinelValues.meaning: Create the (non-timestamped) log file (default behavior)
Do not create a log file
Timestamp the log file name so it does not replace a previous log file

params.name: method
params.description: Name of a project method called regularly during verification with progress/error/warning events; an empty string or invalid name disables the callback

params.name: tablesArray
params.description: Table numbers whose records to check; if omitted/empty and objects includes Verify Records, all tables are checked

params.name: fieldsArray
params.description: 2D array: for each row, element {0} is a table number and elements {1...x} are indexed field numbers whose indexes to check; if omitted/empty and objects includes Verify Indexes, all indexes are checked

constraints: The designated data file is opened read-only; no other application should access it in write mode during the check, or results may be distorted.

The method callback receives up to 5 params ($messageType, $objectType, $messageText, $table, $reserved) and must return an Integer: 0 continues normally, -128 stops without error, any other value stops and is returned as the error number (interceptable by an error-handling method); execution cannot be interrupted after the End of execution event ($messageType=4).

By default a log file in XML format is written to the database's Logs folder, named after the structure file (e.g. myDB_Verify_Log.xml, or with a timestamp suffix if the Timestamp log file name option is passed); its path is returned in the Document system variable regardless of which options were passed.
To verify the currently open data file instead, use VERIFY CURRENT DATA FILE.

options.scope selects the sheet index (0-based) the name is local to, or the vk workbook constant to make it global to the whole document; vk current sheet scopes it to whichever sheet is current.

overloads.semanticRole: The VP ADD RANGE NAME command creates or modifies a named range in the open document.
