The VP ADD SPAN command combines the cells in rangeObj as a single span of cells.

constraints: Multiple cell ranges can be passed to create several spans at once; if ranges overlap, only the first range is used.
Only the upper-left cell's data is displayed; data in the other combined cells is hidden (but still accessible via formulas referencing the upper-left cell) until the span is removed.

overloads.semanticRole: The VP ADD STYLESHEET command creates or modifies the styleName style sheet based upon the combination of the properties specified in styleObj in the open document.

constraints: Errors if vpAreaName does not designate an existing 4D View Pro area.
If a style sheet with the same name and index already exists, it is overwritten with the new values; the same name can be reused across different scopes.

overloads.semanticRole: The VP ALL command returns a new range object referencing all cells.

constraints: Errors if vpAreaName does not designate an existing 4D View Pro area.
If sheet is omitted, or vk current sheet is passed, the currently displayed spreadsheet is used.

overloads.semanticRole: The VP COLUMN AUTOFIT command automatically sizes the column(s) in rangeObj according to their contents.
The VP CREATE TABLE command creates a table in the specified range.

constraints: tableName must be unique within the sheet, at least 5 characters long, and must not contain spaces or start with a number.
If source is omitted, an empty table is created with the size defined by rangeObj; if source's data cannot be fully displayed in rangeObj, no table is created.
source must reference a data context property containing a collection of objects (one per row); the table stays bound and updates when the data context updates.

options is a cs.ViewPro.TableOptions object; its tableColumns collection length should match the range's column count -- excess range columns become empty, and if tableColumns has more columns than the range, only as many columns as the range allows are shown.

If source is passed without a tableColumns option, columns are generated automatically: for a collection of objects, property names become column titles; for a collection of subcollections (scalar values), the subcollections' indices become column titles and rangeObj must designate a single-cell anchor rather than a multi-cell range. A collection of scalar data cannot be combined with the tableColumns option.

overloads.semanticRole: The VP Cell command returns a new range object referencing a specific cell.

constraints: Errors if vpAreaName does not designate an existing 4D View Pro area.
Intended for single-cell ranges only; use VP Cells for a range spanning multiple cells.
If sheet is omitted, or vk current sheet is passed, the currently displayed spreadsheet is used.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns a new range object that combines two or more existing range objects (by reference) from the same 4D View Pro area into a single combined range.

constraints: All ranges passed (rangeObj, otherRangeObj, and any further otherRangeObjN) must belong to the same 4D View Pro area.
The command incorporates the passed range objects by reference, not by copy.

overloads.semanticRole: Converts a legacy 4D View document (BLOB) into a 4D View Pro object, migrating all information to 4D View Pro attributes.

constraints: Does not require the legacy 4D View plug-in to be installed.

overloads.semanticRole: Converts a 4D View Pro object (or a specific range within it) to an SVG picture, e.g. for embedding in another document or for printing without loading the area.

constraints: vpObject must have been previously produced by VP Export to object or VP EXPORT DOCUMENT.
SVG conversion requires expressions and formats in the area to have been evaluated at least once beforehand, otherwise they may render unexpectedly.
If rangeObj is omitted, the whole document contents are converted.
Gridline visibility in the exported picture depends on the document's print-info attribute set via VP SET PRINT INFO.

overloads.semanticRole: Copies the contents, style, and formulas from a range into a plain object, optionally restricted to specific data categories and optionally removing the copied data afterward (cut semantics).

constraints: If rangeObj is a combined range, only the first range is used.
options.copy defaults to True (keep the copied values/formatting/formulas after execution); False removes them (i.e. behaves like a cut).

options.copyOptions selects what is copied via vk clipboard options constants (all, formatting, formulas, formulas and formatting, values, or values and formatting); defaults to vk clipboard options all.
Workbook paste-options settings are taken into account when copying.

overloads.semanticRole: Removes the columns designated by a range object, deleting from right to left.

constraints: If rangeObj contains both columns and rows, only the columns are removed.
If rangeObj contains only rows, the command does nothing.
Columns are deleted from right to left.

overloads.semanticRole: Removes the rows designated by a range object, deleting from bottom to top.

constraints: If rangeObj contains both columns and rows, only the rows are removed.
If rangeObj contains only columns, the command does nothing.
Rows are deleted from bottom to top.

overloads.semanticRole: Exports the 4D View Pro object attached to an area to a document on disk, in a format selected by the file extension or explicit export options, optionally invoking a callback on completion.

constraints: Passing a vpAreaName that does not exist raises an error.
If filePath has no path, the document is saved next to the Project folder.
Supported export formats (selected by filePath extension or paramObj.format): .4vp (4D View Pro, default), .xlsx (Excel), .pdf, .txt/.csv (CSV), .sjs (SpreadJS).
If paramObj.format doesn't match filePath's extension, 4D adds/corrects the extension automatically (except CSV, which never gets an appended extension).
paramObj can also specify a callback method invoked when the export completes.

overloads.semanticRole: Asynchronously exports the 4D View Pro document attached to an area into a 4D.Blob according to export options, delivering the resulting blob to a mandatory callback method.

constraints: paramObj.formula (a 4D.Function callback) is mandatory; it is invoked when the export completes and receives the area name, the exported 4D.Blob, and a reference object.
Exporting/importing 4D View Pro areas as blobs is fast and memory-efficient compared to file-based export.

paramObj supports several Boolean include* options (includeAutoMergedCells, includeBindingSource, includeCalcModelCache, includeEmptyRegionCells, includeFormulas, includeStyles, includeUnusedNames) and saveAsView, each with documented defaults.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the 4D View Pro object attached to an area (e.g. for storage in a database object field), with optional control over formatting-info and data-context-value inclusion.

constraints: Passing a vpAreaName that does not exist raises an error.
options.includeFormatInfo defaults to True (useful e.g. for SVG export); setting it False reduces export time.

options.includeBindingSource defaults to True and controls whether current data-context values are exported as cell values (data contexts themselves are never exported); cell binding itself is always exported.

overloads.semanticRole: Immediately executes the buffered 4D View Pro command batch for an area and clears the buffer, optionally invoking a callback once execution (including any triggered custom functions) has fully completed.

constraints: Passing a vpAreaName that does not exist raises an error.
4D View Pro commands are normally accumulated in a command buffer for performance; this command executes the buffered batch immediately and empties the buffer.
If callback is provided, it only fires once all buffered commands AND any 4D custom functions they triggered have finished executing, so follow-up actions (save/print) can safely run after it fires.
callback receives the area name and a status object with .success, .errorCode, and .errorMessage properties.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the name of the table that a cell (the first cell of rangeObj) belongs to, or an empty string if it belongs to no table.

constraints: If the designated cells do not belong to a table, an empty string is returned.
If rangeObj is not a cell range or contains multiple ranges, the first cell of the first range is used.

overloads.semanticRole: Searches rangeObj for the first cell matching searchValue using default search options, and returns the matching range.

discriminatedBy.searchCondition: omitted -> default search options (first match, case-sensitive, no wildcards)

overloads.semanticRole: Searches rangeObj for cell(s) matching searchValue under explicit search options (match scope, start position, all-matches flag, comparison flags), and returns the matching range.
Searches rangeObj for cell(s) matching searchValue under explicit search options and replaces each match with replaceValue, returning the affected range.

discriminatedBy.replaceValue: provided -> performs find-and-replace instead of find-only

constraints: searchCondition.all defaults to False (only the first matching cell is returned); True returns all matching cells.
searchCondition.afterColumn/afterRow default to -1 (search starts at the beginning of rangeObj); if rangeObj is a combined range, these must refer to the first range.
searchCondition.flags combines vk find flag constants (vk find flag exact match, vk find flag ignore case, vk find flag use wild cards, or vk find flag none as default) to control matching.
Passing replaceValue additionally replaces matched cell(s) with that value.

Date/time cell values are returned as an object with a value property (date, time portion completed to midnight) and a time property (seconds, date portion completed to Dec 30, 1899).

overloads.semanticRole: Imports and displays the document at filePath into the 4D View Pro area vpAreaName, replacing any existing content.

constraints: vpAreaName must name an existing 4D View Pro area; an unknown name raises an error.
The imported document replaces any data already present in the area.
Supported filePath extensions: .4vp (4D View Pro), .xlsx (Excel), .txt/.csv (UTF-8 text), .sjs (SpreadJS); an unrecognized extension is treated as a text document.
filePath must be a full path unless the document sits alongside the Project folder, in which case just its name may be passed.
An error is returned if filePath is invalid or the file is missing or malformed.
paramObj.formula is an optional 4D.Function callback invoked when the import completes.

overloads.semanticRole: Imports the 4D View Pro document contained in vpBlob into the 4D View Pro area vpAreaName, replacing its contents.

constraints: vpBlob must contain a 4D View Pro document previously saved as a Blob via VP EXPORT TO BLOB or the 4D View Pro interface.
The import replaces any data already present in vpAreaName.

paramObj is an options object; documented defaults include calcOnDemand=false, dynamicReferences=true, fullRecalc=false, includeFormulas=true, includeStyles=true, includeUnusedStyles=true, and an optional formula callback invoked when the import completes.

overloads.semanticRole: Imports and displays the 4D View Pro object viewPro into the 4D View Pro area vpAreaName, replacing any existing content.

constraints: vpAreaName must name an existing 4D View Pro area; an unknown name raises an error.
viewPro must be a valid 4D View Pro object, typically produced by VP Export to object; an invalid object raises an error.
The imported object's contents replace any data already present in the area.

paramObj.formula is an optional callback invoked once the object is loaded and all 4D custom functions have responded; it receives (param1: area name, param2: reserved/empty, param3: the paramObj reference, param4: a status object with a success boolean).

overloads.semanticRole: Inserts one or more columns into the sheet at the position designated by rangeObj, shifting existing columns right.

constraints: rangeObj carries both the starting column position and the number of columns to insert; if the count is omitted, a single column is inserted.
New columns are inserted on the left, directly before the starting column of rangeObj.

overloads.semanticRole: Inserts one or more rows into the sheet at the position designated by rangeObj, shifting existing rows down.

constraints: rangeObj carries both the starting row position and the number of rows to insert; if the count is omitted, a single row is inserted.
New rows are inserted directly before the first row of rangeObj.

sentinelValues.meaning: vk table insert before: insert column(s) before column (default if omitted).
vk table insert after: insert column(s) after column.

overloads.semanticRole: Inserts one or count empty column(s) into tableName at the specified column index, before or after it per insertAfter.

constraints: count must be greater than 0; if omitted, a single column is inserted.
Inserts columns inside tableName only, not the sheet: the sheet's total column count is unaffected, and data to the right of the table is automatically shifted right.
If tableName does not exist, or there is not enough room in the sheet, the command does nothing.

sentinelValues.meaning: vk table insert before: insert row(s) before row (default if omitted).
vk table insert after: insert row(s) after row.

overloads.semanticRole: Inserts one or count empty row(s) into tableName at the specified row index, before or after it per insertAfter.

constraints: count must be greater than 0; if omitted, a single row is inserted.
Inserts rows inside tableName only, not the sheet: the sheet's total row count is unaffected, and data below the table is automatically shifted down.
If tableName is bound to a data context, the command inserts new empty element(s) into the bound collection.
If tableName does not exist, or there is not enough room in the sheet, the command does nothing.

overloads.semanticRole: Moves or copies the values, styles, and formulas of cells from originRange to targetRange, according to options.

constraints: originRange and targetRange may refer to different 4D View Pro areas.

options.copy defaults to False (source cells are cleared after the move); pass True to keep the source (copy instead of move).

Not modeled as a plain enum_ref because return values are an OR-combination of these flags, not a single selected constant.

Predefined constants (4D Environment theme, VersionTypeBitFlag enum): 64 bit version = 1, Demo version = 0 (not available in current 4D versions), Merged application = 2 (version is an application merged with 4D Volume Desktop).

Autoparse dropped the return type entirely for this no-parentheses signature ('Version type : Integer'), a known autoparse bug for bare (no-parens) signature lines; restored via overloadPatches below. TypeRef's 'concrete' kind disallows additionalProperties (no sentinelValues on a bare return type), which is why the bit-field constant values are documented in prose above instead of structurally on the return type.

The doc page's own prose elsewhere suggests this might instead hold the original file's name -- see this command's top-level constraints for the full doc-inconsistency note.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB GET BODY PART command, when called in the context of a Web process, parses the "body" part of a multi-part request.

jointConstraints.rule: Optional together: when the part is a submitted file both are received; otherwise both are absent.

constraints: Use WEB Get body part count first to learn how many parts are available to parse.
For file parts, contents must be captured into a Blob; for plain Text form fields submitted in a multi-part request, contents can be captured into Text.
mimeType and name are optional but must be passed together: both are received only when the part was submitted as <input type="file">; otherwise both are absent.

The doc page's own text is internally inconsistent about what `name` holds: its lead prose sentence and the parameter table's own gloss both say 'name' is the variable name of the HTTP input field (e.g. "file1"/"file2" from <input name="file1" type="file">, per this command's own Example), while a later sentence says 'mimeType and name parameters receive the Mime type and the name of the original file' (which would duplicate fileName's own stated purpose instead). Modeled here per the majority/table-sourced reading (input field variable name), since two of the three signals agree and the third reads as a likely copy/paste slip that should have said fileName; this is a documented doc inconsistency 4D has not fixed, not an extraction error in this pipeline.

constraints: Valid regardless of whether the submitted form/URL used the POST or GET method.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the UUID of the session currently open for the Web request, or an empty string if there is no active Web session.

constraints: Returns an empty string "" if called outside the context of a Web session.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB Get server info command returns an object containing detailed runtine information on the 4D Web server current session.

constraints: The returned object reflects actual runtime parameters (e.g. started, uptime, httpRequestCount, startMode, SOAPServerStarted, security/cipherSuite/HTTPEnabled/HTTPSEnabled), which can differ from the configured values returned by WEB GET OPTION since runtime values depend on system settings and available resources.
The 'cache' property is included in the returned object only when withCache is True; it is omitted by default because it can be very large.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns True if the current 4D Web server connection was made in secured mode (TLS/SSL, i.e. an https: request), False otherwise.
Returns True if the 4D built-in Web server that handles requests in the calling execution context (standalone app, 4D Server, or remote mode) is currently running, False otherwise.
The WEB LEGACY CLOSE SESSION command invalidates an existing session designated by the sessionID parameter.

constraints: Only applies to legacy Web sessions (databases converted from versions prior to 4D v18 R6); it is ignored when scalable web sessions mode is enabled.
If the session designated by sessionID does not exist, the command does nothing.
In a 4D Mobile session context, closes the whole 4D Mobile session (all Web processes tied to that session ID), since a single mobile session can span several processes.

params.description: Session UUID

params.description: Filled with the date of cookie expiration

params.name: expTime
params.description: Filled with the time of cookie expiration

overloads.semanticRole: Returns, in expDate and expTime, the expiration date and time of the session cookie for the legacy Web session identified by sessionID.

constraints: Only applies to legacy Web sessions (databases converted from versions prior to 4D v18 R6); returns null date/time values when scalable web sessions mode is enabled.
Each new Web request resets the cookie's expiration to request-time + the 'Web inactive session timeout' setting, so the returned expDate/expTime reflect the most recent request, not a fixed value.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB SEND BLOB command allows you to send blob to the browser.

constraints: type selects how the browser interprets blob: an empty string "" lets the browser guess from content; a file extension (e.g. ".HTM", ".GIF") sets the MIME type by extension, which must be a standard/registered one; a full MIME string (e.g. "text/html", or a custom "application/x-TypeName") sets the MIME type directly and lets the client browser be configured to launch an associated application for custom types.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB SEND FILE command sends, to the Web browser, the HTML page or the Web file stored in the document whose pathname you pass in htmlFile .

constraints: Only has an effect when called from a Web process; called from any other process type, it does nothing and returns no error.
Sets the OK system variable to 1 if the file exists and the send did not time out, otherwise 0.
4D looks for htmlFile relative to the Web root folder defined in the Database Settings, unless an absolute pathname is given; both POSIX and system pathname syntax are accepted.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB SEND HTTP REDIRECT command allows you to transform a URL into another one.

constraints: By default 4D URL-encodes special characters in url; passing the optional '*' parameter tells 4D not to translate them.
This command takes precedence over any data-sending command (WEB SEND FILE, WEB SEND BLOB, etc.) called in the same method -- the redirect wins.
Sends HTTP status 302 (Moved Temporarily); to send a 301 (Moved Permanently), set a 'HTTP X-STATUS: 301' field in the header of the reply instead.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB SEND RAW DATA command lets the 4D Web server send “raw” HTTP data, which can be chunked.

constraints: Passing the optional '*' parameter marks the response as chunked (adds 'transfer-encoding: chunked' to the header if necessary); all subsequent WEB SEND RAW DATA calls in the same method become additional chunks of that same response until the method finishes executing.
data must contain both the HTTP header and body parts of the response; 4D performs a basic validity check and will complete/fix an incomplete header or request before sending.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): Chunked raw response: WEB SEND RAW DATA (data; *) starts a chunked response with a header -> subsequent WEB SEND RAW DATA calls in the same method (with or without '*') are treated as additional body chunks of that response -> the server ends the chunked send when the method terminates.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB SEND TEXT command directly sends HTML formatted text data.

constraints: If type is omitted, 4D sends htmlText as MIME type "text/html" (equivalent to WEB SEND BLOB with a TEXT TO BLOB conversion and "text/html" type).
4D does not validate htmlText's HTML encoding; references to 4D variables and 4DSCRIPT tags in the text are always parsed.

overloads.semanticRole: Registers the name/password credentials (and optional authentication method / proxy flag) to be encoded into the HTTP request sent by the next WEB SERVICE CALL.

constraints: Must be called before WEB SERVICE CALL for the authentication information to be applied to the next request; it configures state consumed by the following WEB SERVICE CALL, it does not perform the call itself.

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): Web Services (Client) SOAP call sequence: WEB SERVICE AUTHENTICATE (optional) and/or WEB SERVICE SET OPTION (optional) configure per-call client state -> WEB SERVICE SET PARAMETER is called once per request parameter to build the SOAP message -> WEB SERVICE CALL sends the request (consuming the authenticate/option/parameter state and erasing any previous result) -> WEB SERVICE GET RESULT retrieves each returned value (pass '*' on the final call to free memory) -> on error, WEB SERVICE Get info can be called from an ON ERR CALL method to inspect the SOAP fault.

Web Service manual in: RPC mode, complex input (manual XML BLOB via WEB SERVICE SET PARAMETER), simple output

params.description: If passed, keeps the underlying connection open for reuse by the next WEB SERVICE CALL instead of closing it at the end of execution

overloads.semanticRole: Sends a SOAP HTTP request built from the parameters previously registered via WEB SERVICE SET PARAMETER to the Web Service designated by accessURL/soapAction/methodName/nameSpace, replacing any previous result.

jointConstraints.rule: The trailing '*' occupies the parameter slot after complexType in the signature, so complexType must be passed (even if its default value) for '*' to be reachable.

constraints: Passing https:// in accessURL enables secure (SSL/TLS) mode automatically; an invalid server certificate sets OK to 0 and raises error 901, interceptable via ON ERR CALL.

Calling WEB SERVICE CALL erases any result from a previously called Web Service and replaces it with the new result(s); each new WEB SERVICE SET PARAMETER call after this one starts building a fresh request.

params.name: infoType
params.description: Type of information to retrieve about the last SOAP error

sentinelValues.meaning: Web Service error code: main 4D error code (also returned in the Error system variable); one of 9910 (Soap fault), 9911 (Parser fault), 9912 (HTTP fault), 9913 (Network fault), 9914 (Internal fault)
Web Service detailed message: a message describing the error, whose content depends on the main error code
Web Service HTTP status code: HTTP error code, used when the main error is 9912 (HTTP fault)

Web Service fault actor: SOAP-protocol-reported cause of the error, used when the main error is 9910 (Soap fault) -- e.g. Version Mismatch, Must Understand, Sender Fault, Receiver Fault, Encoding Unknown

overloads.semanticRole: Returns, as Text, the piece of information selected by infoType about the error generated during the last SOAP request sent via WEB SERVICE CALL.

constraints: Generally called within a method installed via ON ERR CALL, to inspect the error raised by the last SOAP request.
Returns an empty string when no information is available, particularly when the last SOAP request did not generate any errors.

params.name: option
params.description: Code of the option to set

sentinelValues.meaning: Web Service display auth dialog: value is 0 (never display, default) or 1 (display the authentication dialog box, only shown if the service requires authentication)
Web Service HTTP compression: value is the Web Service Compression constant; enables gzip/deflate compression of the next SOAP request (client and server 4D v11.3+ only)
Web Service HTTP timeout: value is the client-side wait timeout in seconds (180 by default)
Web Service reset auth settings: value is 0 (keep authentication info for the session) or 1 (erase it after each WEB SERVICE CALL, the default)
Web Service SOAP header: value is an XML root element reference to insert as a header in the SOAP request
Web Service SOAP version: value is the Web Service SOAP_1_1 or Web Service SOAP_1_2 constant

Gregorian month, e.g. --10--
Value expressed in hexadecimal
BLOB
Uniform Resource Identifier (URI), e.g. http://www.company.com/page
Qualified XML name (namespace and local part)
Notation attribute

overloads.semanticRole: Registers a named parameter (name/value, optionally forced to soapType) to include in the SOAP request built for the next WEB SERVICE CALL.

constraints: Call once per parameter to be included in the SOAP request; value is generally $param1/$param2/... (the proxy method's own parameters) but any declared 4D variable/array can be used.
Does not support 4D.Blob class objects as value (only classic Blob and other primitive/variable types).

Reference lifecycle (implied convention, not syntactically enforced): Web Services (Client) SOAP call sequence: WEB SERVICE AUTHENTICATE (optional) and/or WEB SERVICE SET OPTION (optional) configure per-call client state -> WEB SERVICE SET PARAMETER is called once per request parameter to build the SOAP message -> WEB SERVICE CALL sends the request (consuming the authenticate/option/parameter state and erasing any previous result) -> WEB SERVICE GET RESULT retrieves each returned value (pass '*' on the final call to free memory) -> on error, WEB SERVICE Get info can be called from an ON ERR CALL method to inspect the SOAP fault.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB SET HOME PAGE command allows you to modify the custom home page for the current Web process.

constraints: Passing an empty string "" in homePage stops sending a custom home page for the current Web process (reverts to the default home page from Database Settings).
If the named page does not yet exist when the Web process first accesses it, the Web server creates it with the default home page's contents.
The custom home page applies only to the current Web process, so it can vary per connected user.

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the entire HTTP reply header from a single pre-formatted Text field/variable (header), allowing arbitrary header lines such as status lines and Set-Cookie.
Sets the HTTP reply header field-by-field from two parallel arrays: fieldArray holds the header field names and valueArray holds their corresponding values, at matching positions.

jointConstraints.rule: fieldArray and valueArray must have the same size; each fieldArray[i] is paired with valueArray[i] as one header field/value.

constraints: Only has an effect within a Web process.
header must be a 4D variable or field (a literal Text constant is rejected); header fields must be separated by CR or CR+LF.

params.name: selector
params.description: Which Web server setting to modify.

params.name: value
params.description: New value for the selected option; accepted shape depends entirely on selector -- see discriminatedBy. Confirmed missing from the original draft by the LSP cross-check (tool4d rejected a selector-only call site with a parameter-count/type mismatch) and against the real doc syntax example "WEB SET OPTION(Web debug log;wdl enable without body)", which always passes two arguments.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB SET OPTION command modifies the current value of various options concerning the functioning of the 4D Web server.

discriminatedBy.rule: value's accepted type/range is selected by which WebServerOptionSelector constant is passed in selector; see each enum entry's description for its expected value shape. When selector is 'Web debug log', value is one of the WebDebugLogLevel enum constants.

constraints: selector selects which Web server setting is modified (see the WebServerOptionSelector enum), and the accepted shape/range of value depends entirely on which selector is passed: most are Integer or Boolean-as-Integer, Web IP address to listen/Web Client IP address to listen/Web session cookie name/domain/path are Text, Web CORS settings is a Collection of CORS objects, and Web debug log's value is drawn from the WebDebugLogLevel sub-enum.
Changes made via this command persist across Web server stop/restart but are lost when the 4D application itself is restarted.
Several selectors (e.g. Web scalable session, Web HSTS enabled) require a Web server restart to take effect; others apply immediately.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB SET ROOT FOLDER command is used to modify the default root folder where 4D looks for the HTML files requested of the Web server.

constraints: The Web server must be restarted for a new root folder to take effect.
rootFolder can be given in HTML/URL syntax (slash-separated, platform-independent) or system syntax (absolute platform-specific pathname).
An invalid pathname raises an OS file-manager error, interceptable via ON ERR CALL; if the handler displays an alert/message, it appears on the browser side.
This setting overrides (is independent of) any default root folder configured in the Database Settings.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB START SERVER command starts the Web server of the 4D application on which it has been executed (4D or 4D Server).

constraints: Sets the OK system variable to 1 on success, 0 on failure (e.g. TCP/IP not properly configured).

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB STOP SERVER command stops the Web server of the 4D application on which it has been executed (4D ou 4D Server).

constraints: If the Web server was not running, the command does nothing.
Stops all current Web connections and terminates all Web processes.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns a collection of all available 4D.WebServer objects (the database's own Web server plus any host/component Web servers).
Returns the default Web server object, i.e. the Web server of the project/database from which the command is called.

params.name: option
params.description: Which Web server object to return

sentinelValues.meaning: Web server database: Web server of the project from which the command is called (default if option is omitted)
Web server host database: Web server of the host database of a component
Web server receiving request: Web server that actually received the request (target Web server)

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the Web server object designated by option (the database's own Web server, a host component's Web server, or the Web server that received the current request).

constraints: The returned 4D.WebServer object exposes the current property values of the designated Web server (e.g. .isRunning); see the WebServer class.

overloads.semanticRole: The WEB Validate digest command checks the validity of the identifying information (name and password) provided by a user connecting to the Web server.

constraints: Must be called from the On Web Authentication database method, in the context of Web authentication in Digest mode.
Digest validation cannot be used jointly with 4D passwords.
If the browser does not support Digest authentication, an authentication error is raised instead of this command returning False.

params.name: windows
params.description: Filled with the window reference numbers of the currently open, visible windows
If passed, floating windows are included in windows; if omitted, floating windows are ignored

overloads.semanticRole: Fills windows with the reference numbers of all currently open, visible windows across all running processes, optionally including floating windows.

constraints: Only visible (non-hidden) windows across all running processes (kernel or user) are returned.

params.name: wpDoc
params.description: 4D Write Pro document

params.name: pictureSource
params.description: The picture to add: a 4D picture (Picture), a pathname to a picture file on disk in system syntax (Text), or a 4D.File object representing a picture file (4D.File). Omit entirely to add an empty image placeholder.

overloads.semanticRole: Anchors the given picture (or an empty placeholder image if omitted) at a fixed location in wpDoc and returns its reference object.

discriminatedBy.rule: The runtime type of the second argument selects its meaning: a Picture value is used directly as the image; a Text value is treated as a pathname (full, structure-file-relative, or a bare filename located next to the structure file, with extension required); a 4D.File value is treated as a picture-file reference. Passing nothing at all adds an empty image awaiting a wk image expression via WP SET ATTRIBUTES.

constraints: If the picture-source parameter is omitted entirely, a valid picture reference is still returned and an empty image is added; this lets you subsequently call WP SET ATTRIBUTES with the wk image expression selector to fill it with a computed 4D expression.
The returned reference object can be passed to WP SET ATTRIBUTES to reposition/resize/restyle the picture anywhere in wpDoc (page, section, header, footer, layer, etc.).

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Bookmark range command returns a text range object (rangeObj) containing the range for the bookmark with the specified bkName in wpDoc .

constraints: If bkName does not exist in wpDoc, an empty rangeObj object is returned rather than an error.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP COMPUTE FORMULAS command evaluates the formulas in targetObj .

constraints: targetObj can be a range, an element (table/row/cell(s)/paragraph/body/header/footer/section/subsection/inline or anchored picture/text box), or a whole 4D Write Pro document.

When targetObj is a section, only image formulas or formulas in text boxes anchored to that section (or to all sections) are computed; formulas anchored to a page or to the embedded view are not computed unless targetObj is the whole document.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP DELETE BOOKMARK command removes the bookmark named bkName from wpDoc .

constraints: If bkName does not exist in wpDoc, the command does nothing (no error).

overloads.semanticRole: The WP DELETE FOOTER command deletes the footer element associated to the section or subsection defined by the wpSection parameter.
The WP DELETE HEADER command deletes the header element associated to the section or subsection defined by the wpSection parameter.
The WP DELETE PICTURE command deletes the image defined by the imgObj parameter.
Deletes a single already-referenced section object directly (e.g. one previously returned by WP Get section).
Deletes one or more sections of wpDoc starting at indexNumber, removing count sections (default 1) when count is passed.

constraints: Raises an error if the requested deletion would remove all sections or if the document contains only one section.

Deleting a section also removes everything anchored to it (header, footer, part of the body, anchored pictures, text boxes, and the ending section break), and re-indexes the anchorSection attribute of remaining text boxes/pictures.

overloads.semanticRole: Deletes an already-referenced style sheet object directly (e.g. one created with WP New style sheet or returned by WP Get style sheet).
Deletes the named style sheet (optionally at a given list level) from wpDoc by name rather than by object reference.
Removes the subsection elements of the given subSectionType (wk first page / wk left page / wk right page) from wpSection.
Removes an already-referenced subsection object directly (e.g. one obtained via a prior lookup).

constraints: The body of the document is left untouched; only header/footer/column/anchored-picture subsection elements are removed.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP DELETE TEXT BOX command deletes the text box defined by the textBox parameter.
Exports wpDoc to a document on disk designated by a text file path.
Exports wpDoc to a document on disk designated by a 4D.File object.

constraints: Pass exactly one of filePath or fileObj to designate the destination, not both.
If filePath contains only a document name (no path), the file is saved at the same level as the 4D structure file.
If format is omitted, it is inferred from the file extension given in filePath/fileObj.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP EXPORT VARIABLE command exports the wpDoc 4D Write Pro object to the 4D destination variable in the specified format .

constraints: destination's resolved type depends on format: Blob for the native .4wp/.docx formats, Text for HTML/SVG formats.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP FREEZE FORMULAS command "freezes" the contents of the formulas in targetObj .
The WP Find all command searches the targetObj for the searchValue based on the searchCondition .

constraints: Does not search or replace text inside formulas; use WP Get formulas for that case.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Find next command searches the targetObj , after the searchAfter range, for the searchValue based on the searchCondition .

constraints: Does not search or replace text inside formulas; use WP Get formulas for that case.
Pass NULL in searchAfter to begin the search from the first value of targetObj.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Find previous command searches the targetObj , prior to the searchBefore range, for the searchValue based on the searchCondition .

constraints: Does not search or replace text inside formulas; use WP Get formulas for that case.

overloads.semanticRole: Gets one attribute's value by name; optionally also fills the caller-supplied attribValue variable with that value in the same call.
Gets the values of multiple named attributes at once by passing a collection of attribute names in attribColl, returned as an object keyed by attribute name.
The WP Get body command returns the body element of the wpDoc 4D Write Pro document.
The WP Get breaks command returns the collection of all breaks inserted in targetObj .
The WP Get data context command returns the data context of the wpDoc document.
The WP Get element by ID command returns an object containing the element of wpDoc passed in the ID parameter.
The WP Get elements command returns a collection of objects containing paragraphs, images, tables and/or rows.
Returns the footer of the first page in the range or the section/sub-section passed as targetObj (returns the visible footer if a sub-section is active).
Returns the footer of the section identified by sectionIndex (>=1) in wpDoc, or of a specific sub-section type of that section when sectionSubType is passed.

constraints: Returns Null if no footer is found for the given parameter(s).

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Get formulas command returns a collection of all formulas defined in targetObj .
Gets the cursor frame when wpArea is passed as a form object name (string), signalled by the leading * flag.

discriminatedBy.rule: Presence of the leading * literal indicates wpArea is a form object name; its absence (see sibling overload) indicates wpArea is a field/variable.

overloads.semanticRole: Gets the cursor frame when wpArea is passed directly as a 4D Write Pro object field or variable (no leading * flag).

discriminatedBy.rule: No leading * literal; wpArea is a Variable or Field reference rather than a form object name string.

constraints: Can only be used if wpArea is associated with a form object (i.e. displayed in the current form/page).

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the header of the first page in the range or the section/sub-section passed as targetObj (returns the visible header if a sub-section is active).
Returns the header of the section identified by sectionIndex (>=1) in wpDoc, or of a specific sub-section type of that section when subSectionType is passed.

constraints: Returns Null if no header is found for the given parameter(s).

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Get links command returns the collection of all links defined in targetObj .
The WP Get page count command returns the total number of pages defined in the targetObj you passed in parameter.
The WP Get position command returns an object describing the current position of targetObj .
Returns the first section intersected by the given range or element (targetObj).
Returns the section corresponding to sectionIndex within wpDoc.

constraints: In the targetObj syntax, passing a subsection or an anchored picture raises an error; only a range or element (table/row/paragraph/body/text box/header/footer) is accepted.

If targetObj is or belongs to a header/footer, the section to which that header/footer is attached is returned; if it is or belongs to a text box, the first section is returned unless the text box is anchored to a section.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Get sections command returns a collection of all sections defined in the targetObj parameter.
The WP Get style sheet command returns the style sheet object designated by the styleSheetName or by the style sheet name and the listLevelIndex in the case of a hierarchical list style sheet .
The WP Get style sheets command returns a collection of all the style sheet objects of the defined type in wpDoc .
Returns the first subsection intersected by a range or element passed in targetObj; returns a null object if no subsection intersects it.
Returns the subsection of the specified subSectionType (wk first page, wk left page, or wk right page) within wpSection.

constraints: If targetObj is or belongs to a header, footer, or text box, the command returns the subsection to which it is attached (or a null object if it is not attached to any subsection).

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Get text command retrieves text contents from a 4D Write Pro document within the specified targetObj .

constraints: If expressions is omitted, 4D expression references within targetObj are evaluated and returned in their evaluated form (equivalent to wk expressions as value, the default).
Only the wk expressions as space option keeps returned plain-text indexes consistent with the text range indexes used by WP/ST commands.

params.description: If present, wpArea is a form object name (Text); if omitted, wpArea is a 4D Write Pro object variable or field.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns the current view properties for the 4D Write Pro area designated by wpArea.

constraints: The command requires wpArea to be associated with a form object currently displayed in the form; if the document is displayed in several form objects, the '*' syntax is required to disambiguate which view to address.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP IMPORT STYLE SHEETS command imports all of the style sheets from the sourceDoc into the targetDoc .

constraints: If a style sheet from sourceDoc has the same name as a style sheet already in targetDoc, the imported style sheet overwrites (replaces) the one in targetDoc.

overloads.semanticRole: Imports a document stored on disk, given its path (filePath), and returns a new 4D Write Pro object.
Imports a document referenced by a 4D.File object (fileObj), and returns a new 4D Write Pro object.

constraints: Supported source formats are former 4D Write documents (.4w7/.4wt), 4D Write Pro (.4wp) documents, and MS Word (.docx) documents.
An error is returned if filePath/fileObj is invalid, the file is missing, or the file format is unsupported.

When option is an Integer, it selects the wk import html expressions as text behavior for legacy 4D Write documents (default: HTML expressions not imported); when option is an Object, its properties (anchoredTextAreas, anchoredImages, sections, fields, borderRules, preferredFontScriptType, htmlExpressions, importDisplayMode) configure .docx/.4w7-specific import behavior.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Insert break command inserts a new break of the breakType type in the targetObj according to the specified insertion mode and rangeUpdate parameters, and returns the text range of the break character In targetObj

constraints: rangeUpdate is only honored when targetObj is a range; it is ignored if targetObj is an element or document.
If rangeUpdate is omitted, the inserted break is included in the resulting range by default (equivalent to wk include in range).

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Insert document body command inserts the body of the wpDoc document into the specified targetObj according to the passed insertion mode and rangeUpdate parameters, and it returns the range of the inserted document

constraints: Only the body's children elements of wpDoc are inserted; headers, footers, text boxes, and anchored pictures are not inserted.
The mode parameter can combine one insertion-position constant (wk append/wk prepend/wk replace) with option flags (wk freeze expressions, wk keep paragraph styles) via bitwise combination.
rangeUpdate is only honored when targetObj is a range; it is ignored if targetObj is an element or document.
wpDoc is copied on insertion, so the same wpDoc object can be reused across multiple insertions.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Insert formula command inserts a formula in targetObj according to the specified insertion mode and returns the resulting text range.

constraints: formula may be either a formula object created by Formula/Formula from string, or a plain object with a required 'formula' property (the formula object) and an optional 'name' property (Text) used as the displayed label instead of the formula reference.
rangeUpdate is only honored when targetObj is a range; it is ignored if targetObj is an element or document.
The formula object is evaluated within the execution context (database/component) that created it, not necessarily the context in which it is later displayed.

overloads.semanticRole: Inserts a picture passed directly as a Picture field/variable value (or a path string) into targetObj, and returns a reference to the inserted picture element.
Inserts a picture referenced by a 4D.File object or a path string (pictureFile) into targetObj, and returns a reference to the inserted picture element.

constraints: rangeUpdate is only honored when targetObj is a range; it is ignored if targetObj is an element or document.
If the picture value encapsulates several formats/codecs, 4D Write Pro keeps only one format for display and one for printing (best formats auto-selected).

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Insert table command inserts a new table in the targetObj according to the specified insertion mode and returns the corresponding new table object.

constraints: rangeUpdate is only honored when targetObj is a range; it is ignored if targetObj is an element or document.
If nbCols and nbRows are omitted, a new table with 0 columns and 0 rows is created; rows/columns can then be added with WP Table append row.
If targetObj is itself a table, the newly inserted table replaces it or is inserted before/after it depending on mode; inserting a table inside another table is not possible.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Is font style supported command returns True if the wpFontStyle style is supported by any part of the text in rangeObj .
The WP NEW BOOKMARK command creates a new bookmark named bkName based upon the 4D Write Pro targetObj in the parent document.

constraints: targetObj must be a range that belongs to the document body, or a body element (body/table/row/inline picture/paragraph); bookmarks cannot be created from ranges in the header, footer, or a text box.

bkName must comply with HTML/CSS name rules (alphanumeric characters only; invalid characters such as spaces are automatically removed) and must be unique within the document; creating a bookmark with an existing name overwrites it.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP New footer command creates and returns the footer associated to the section or subsection defined by the wpSection parameter.

constraints: If a footer element is already defined for the section or subsection, an undefined object is returned and an error is generated.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP New header command creates and returns the header associated to the section or subsection defined by the wpSection parameter.

constraints: If a header element is already defined for the section or subsection, an undefined object is returned and an error is generated.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP New style sheet command creates a new (empty) style sheet object for the designated wpDoc .

constraints: listLevelCount is only meaningful when styleSheetType is wk type paragraph; if specified (value >= 1) the command creates a hierarchical list style sheet with the specified number of levels (a root-level style sheet plus sub-level style sheets).
If listLevelCount is omitted or 0, a standard (non-list) paragraph style sheet is created.

styleSheetName must start with a letter, may then contain alphanumeric/space/'-'/unicode (>=128) characters, must be unique in the document across both style sheet types, and must not start with 'section' (reserved).

overloads.semanticRole: The WP New subsection command creates and returns a new subsection of the subSectionType type in the wpSection 4D Write Pro section.

constraints: Creating a left-page or right-page subsection automatically creates the opposite subsection as well.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP New text box command creates and returns a new text box object in the page pageNum of wpDoc .

constraints: If pageNum < 0, page number 1 is used and no error is generated.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP New command creates and returns a 4D Write Pro object.

constraints: If source is omitted, an empty 4D Write Pro object is returned.
If source is Text, it must be a 4D HTML source string (as exported by WP EXPORT VARIABLE with wk web page html 4D).

If source is Blob, it must contain either a 4D Write Pro (.4wp) document or a legacy 4D Write document (.4w7/.4wt); option only applies in this legacy-blob case, to control whether HTML expressions are imported as raw text (wk import html expressions as text) or ignored (default).

If source is Object, it must be a range, a body-descendant element (table/row/paragraph/body/header/footer/inline picture/text box/section/subsection/style sheet), or a 4D Write Pro document; passing a range that is not the full document range exports only the first section and does not export bookmarks; passing a document returns a copy of it.
option is only meaningful when source is a Blob containing a legacy 4D Write document; it is ignored otherwise.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP PRINT command launches a print job for the 4D Write Pro document specified in wpDoc , or adds the document to the current print job if it is called between OPEN PRINTING JOB and CLOSE PRINTING JOB .

constraints: If printOptions is omitted, the default 4D Write Pro layout is used and expressions are recomputed before printing (wk 4D Write Pro layout + wk recompute expressions).
Page margins always come from the 4D Write Pro document's own page settings, regardless of print settings from 4D PRINT SETTINGS/SET PRINT OPTION.
If called between OPEN PRINTING JOB and CLOSE PRINTING JOB, the document is added to the current print job instead of launching a new one.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP Paragraph range command returns a specific range object that addresses only the paragraphs that intersect with the targetObj you passed as parameter.
The WP Picture range command returns a specific range object that addresses only the pictures contained in the targetObj you passed as parameter.

params.name: targetObj
params.description: Range, element (header/footer/body/table/paragraph/anchored or inline picture/section/subsection/style sheet), 4D Write Pro document, or a section/subsection object.

overloads.semanticRole: Resets one or more named attributes on targetObj using variadic attribName arguments; if targetObj is a section or subsection, all attribName arguments may be omitted to reset every attribute at once.

params.name: targetObj
params.description: Range, element (header/footer/body/table/paragraph/anchored or inline picture/section/subsection/style sheet), 4D Write Pro document, or a section/subsection object.

params.name: attribColl
params.description: Collection of attribute names to reset.

overloads.semanticRole: Resets multiple named attributes on targetObj at once using a Collection of attribute names (attribColl); if targetObj is a section or subsection, attribColl may be omitted to reset every attribute at once.

constraints: When targetObj is not a section nor a subsection, at least one attribName (or a non-empty attribColl) must be provided; omitting all of them raises an error in that case.
When targetObj is a section or a subsection, all attribName/attribColl arguments may be omitted, which resets every attribute at once.
If the attribute being reset was not defined on the target element, the command does nothing.
Resetting a style sheet object's attributes removes them from the style sheet, unless it is the default ('Normal') style sheet, in which case the default value is applied instead.

params.description: If present, wpArea is a form object name (Text); if omitted, wpArea is a 4D Write Pro object variable or field.

params.name: targetObj
params.description: Range, element (table/row/paragraph/anchored or inline picture/text box/body/header/footer/section/subsection), or a 4D Write Pro document (only its body element is used).

overloads.semanticRole: Creates a new selection in the 4D Write Pro wpArea area, based upon targetObj or upon a startRange/endRange pair.

jointConstraints.rule: targetObj and the startRange/endRange pair are alternative ways to specify the selection; pass one or the other, not both. startRange/endRange are only valid when the addressed element (targetObj, or the implicit area) is body/header/footer/section/subsection.

constraints: If no 4D Write Pro area is resolved from wpArea, the command does nothing.
wk start text may be passed in startRange and wk end text in endRange to mean the beginning/end of the area.
The command can only be used if wpArea is associated with a form object currently displayed in the form/page.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP SET DATA CONTEXT command sets the contextData object as data context of the wpDoc 4D Write Pro document.

constraints: Passing a null object in contextData resets/removes the document's data context.
Setting a new context replaces any existing context for that document.
The data context is process-local: it is not saved with the document, and it is null/undefined (This.data is undefined) when accessed from computed formulas running in a different process.

params.description: If present, wpArea is a form object name (Text); if omitted, wpArea is a 4D Write Pro object variable or field.

overloads.semanticRole: Sets the cursor into the frame designated by frameSelector (and, for a text box frame, textBoxID) in the 4D Write Pro wpArea area.

jointConstraints.rule: textBoxID must be passed when frameSelector is wk text box; if it is omitted, or no text box with that id exists (or no page corresponds to its anchor conditions), the command does nothing. textBoxID is ignored when frameSelector is not wk text box.

constraints: The command can only be used if wpArea is associated with a form object currently displayed in the current form/page.
If frameSelector requests a header/footer frame that does not exist for the selected section (or its sub-section type distinction), the command does nothing (no error is generated).

overloads.semanticRole: The WP SET LINK applies a hyperlink reference to the targetObj .

jointConstraints.rule: linkObj must contain exactly one of the url, bookmark, or method properties (the action to trigger); parameter and range may only be used together with method, and are ignored/inapplicable otherwise.

constraints: If a targetObj that already fully contains existing link(s) is re-linked, those existing links are removed and the new link is applied; a link that only partially overlaps targetObj is trimmed so the non-overlapping part keeps its previous link.
Setting a link on a targetObj spanning several paragraphs creates several separate links.
Only valid (encoded) URLs are accepted; an error is generated for an invalid link.
Links to 4D methods are removed when the document is exported to HTML, MIME HTML, or .docx format.
For a method-type link, the method must exist and be allowed via SET ALLOWED METHODS; it receives the 4D Write Pro area name in $1 and an object with method/parameter/range properties in $2.

overloads.semanticRole: The WP SET TEXT command inserts the text passed in the newText parameter as plain text in the targetObj at the position designated by the textPosition parameter.

constraints: WP SET TEXT inserts plain text only, exactly as written, with no style tags applied.
rangeUpdate is only honored when targetObj is a range; it is ignored if targetObj is an element or document.
If rangeUpdate is omitted, the inserted text is included in the resulting range by default (equivalent to wk include in range).

params.description: If present, wpArea is a form object name (Text); if omitted, wpArea is a 4D Write Pro document (object variable or field).

params.name: wpViewProps
params.description: Object whose properties are the view properties to modify; properties not included keep their previous values.

overloads.semanticRole: Dynamically sets one or more view properties of the 4D Write Pro wpArea area, leaving unspecified properties unchanged.

constraints: The command can only be used if wpArea is associated with a form object currently displayed in the form; if the document is displayed in several form objects, the '*' syntax is required to identify which view to set.
Property modifications made by this command are not saved with the document or the form and persist only while the form area is in use and not overridden by a later call.

params.description: If present, wpArea is a form object name (Text); if omitted, wpArea is a 4D Write Pro object variable or field.

overloads.semanticRole: Returns a new range object (or a picture reference object, if an anchored image is selected) based upon the currently selected content in wpArea.

constraints: If no 4D Write Pro area is resolved from wpArea, an empty object is returned.
The command can only be used if wpArea is associated with a form object currently displayed in the current form/page.

overloads.semanticRole: Removes all columns of every table intersecting targetObj (a range, element, or 4D Write Pro document); does nothing if targetObj does not intersect a table.
Removes numColumns column(s) from tableRef starting at colNumber (default numColumns = 1 if omitted).

constraints: With the targetObj syntax, the numColumns parameter (if it were passed) is ignored; only the targetObj syntax's own tables/columns matter.
Removing all columns of a table removes the entire table.

overloads.semanticRole: Removes all rows of every table intersecting targetObj (a range, element, or 4D Write Pro document); does nothing if targetObj does not intersect a table.

overloads.semanticRole: The WRITE PICTURE FILE command saves the picture passed in the picture parameter in the defined codec to disk.

constraints: If fileName is an empty string (""), the standard Save file dialog box is displayed for the user to choose name/location/format; a default name from SET PICTURE FILE NAME, if any, is pre-filled.
If fileName is just a file name (no path), the file is created next to the database structure file; the file extension must be included.
codec may be a file-extension-style string (e.g. ".gif") or a MIME type (e.g. "image/jpeg"); available codecs can be listed via PICTURE CODEC LIST.
If codec is omitted, the codec is inferred from fileName's extension; if there is no usable extension or codec, the picture defaults to PICT format.
If the extension does not correspond to any available codec, the file is not saved and the OK system variable is set to 0.
If the target write format matches the picture's current format and no transformation has been applied, the picture is written as-is without re-encoding.
On success, the Document system variable holds the full pathname of the created file and OK is set to 1; otherwise OK is set to 0.

Creates a ZIP archive from a single 4D.File.

overloads.semanticRole: Creates a ZIP archive from a single 4D.Folder, optionally excluding the enclosing folder itself from the archive contents.

discriminatedBy.note: first arg is a 4D.Folder; only this overload accepts the options parameter

overloads.semanticRole: Creates a ZIP archive from a full zip-structure description object, allowing per-entry destination paths, compression/encryption settings, a password, and a progress callback.

discriminatedBy.note: first arg is a plain Object describing compression/encryption/files rather than a single File/Folder

constraints: zipStructure object properties: compression (Integer constant: ZIP Compression standard [default]/LZMA/XZ/none), level (Integer 1-10 compression level; default depends on compression: 6 for standard, 4 for LZMA/XZ), encryption (Integer constant: ZIP Encryption AES128/AES192/AES256 [default if password set]/none [default if no password]), password (Text, used when encryption requires one), and files (a Collection of 4D.File/4D.Folder objects, or of objects with source: 4D.File-or-Folder, destination: Text relative path (optional), option: Integer such as ZIP Ignore invisible files or 0 (optional), and callback: 4D.Function receiving compression progress 0-100 in $1).
destinationFile should preferably use a '.zip' extension so the archive is recognized automatically by other software.

The returned status object has statusText (Text error message, e.g. 'Cannot open ZIP archive', 'Cannot create ZIP archive', 'Password is required for encryption'), status (Integer status code), and success (Boolean).

In the folderToZip overload, passing the ZIP Without enclosing folder constant in options compresses only the folder's contents (without it, decompressing recreates the enclosing folder, which is the default).

overloads.semanticRole: The ZIP Read archive command retrieves the contents of zipFile and returns it as a 4D.ZipArchive object.

constraints: Does not decompress the archive; it only provides a navigable view of its contents. Use file.copyTo()/folder.copyTo() on the returned structure to actually extract data.
The archive file is held open only until this command finishes executing and all extracted contents/references are released, after which it is closed automatically.
If the archive is password-protected and password is omitted (or wrong), an error is generated.
The returned 4D.ZipArchive object exposes a single 'root' property, a 4D.ZipFolder describing the whole archive contents.

overloads.semanticRole: The ds command returns a reference to the datastore matching the current 4D database or the database designated by localID .

constraints: If localID is omitted (or an empty string is passed), returns a reference to the datastore matching the local 4D database (or, when opening a remote database on 4D Server, the 4D Server database).
localID must reference a remote datastore previously opened by the current database (host or component) via Open datastore; the local id's scope is the database where it was opened.
The datastore is opened automatically and is available directly through ds; no separate open step is required for the default (no-localID) case.
Returns Null if no datastore matching localID is found.
Objects exposed on the returned cs.DataStore are mapped from the target database following the general ORDA rules.

overloads.semanticRole: Throws an error immediately, identified by a numeric error code and an optional description text.

discriminatedBy.note: first arg is a numeric Integer error code

overloads.semanticRole: Given an errorObj, throws a fully-described (optionally deferred) error built from its properties; called with no argument at all, instead throws (in deferred mode) every error currently queued for the calling method/Try block.

discriminatedBy.note: single optional Object arg; omitting it entirely switches to the zero-arg 'flush the deferred error stack' behavior rather than throwing a new error

constraints: If description is omitted in the errorCode form, it defaults to 'Error code errorCode: (host)' in the host application, or 'Error code errorCode: (C00x)' in a component.

errorObj properties: componentSignature (Text, 4-letter source signature; defaults to 'host' for the host database or 'C001', 'C002', ... for components), errCode (Number; defaults to -1), message (Text; may contain {propertyName} placeholders substituted from custom properties on errorObj; if omitted/empty, 4D looks up a description in the database's xliff files under resname 'ERR_{componentSignature}_{errCode}'), deferred (Boolean, default false; when true, the error is deferred until the current method/Try block ends), plus any custom properties referenced by message placeholders.
Errors thrown via throw are handled like any normal 4D error: the standard error dialog appears unless an interception method is installed via ON ERR CALL.
throw can be called multiple times in the same method to queue several errors, typically combined with deferred:true, then flushed together via the zero-argument call.

The zero-argument call is typically made from within an ON ERR CALL callback; queued errors are exposed via the Last errors command, and in a component the error stack can be relayed to the host application's ON ERR CALL.

relationships.note: If GRAPH was called with its Object (graphSettings) overload, GRAPH SETTINGS must not be called afterward — it is an error, not merely redundant.
Deprecation-by-absorption: GRAPH's Object overload folds GRAPH SETTINGS' functionality into a single call, rather than a different replacement command.
Identical signature; only difference is scope — whole table vs. current selection.
Variadic-pairs form and object-map form set identical data via structurally different call shapes.

Both use a leading literal '*' to switch whether a following parameter is a name string or a direct reference/variable — the star_operator_dual_signature pattern (category C), shared across ~167 commands corpus-wide.
